ideas.name: Modison Ltd
ideas.trigger: price: Silver — WPI Silver index 440.5 for Apr-2026, +152.4% over 12 months (eaindustry.nic.in monthly index, base 2011-12=100); India's silver import unit price for HS 710691 (grains) at US$1,903.8/kg in Jul-2026, +85.1% on a last-3-months vs year-ago-3-months basis (MEIDB). Silver is one of Modison's two named raw materials.
ideas.thesis:
**What the business physically does.** Modison Limited manufactures electrical contacts and contact materials for low-, medium-, high- and extra-high-voltage switchgear. The FY2025-26 annual report states the business "falls within a single Primary segment viz. 'Manufacturing of Electrical Contacts'" — there is no second segment to dilute the exposure. Works are at Vapi, GIDC Phase 1, Gujarat. Customers span power distribution and transmission, electrical infrastructure, automotive, railway, aerospace, marine, defence and pharmaceuticals. The company began as a silver refiner in 1975 and says it helped establish the '999' Good Delivery silver bar standard in India before diversifying into contacts in 1977.

**Why the silver price is the driver.** The annual report's financial-risk note names the input directly: "Basic ingredients of company raw material is Silver and Tungsten Powder where prices are volatile." The same note states the mitigation: "The Company proactively manage this risk through hedging, inventory management… The company is able to pass on price hike to the customer." The MD&A risk table adds the mechanism — "long-term supply contracts and price-sharing arrangements with key customers", "strategic inventory management to capitalize on favorable market conditions" and "selective use of hedging instruments". For high-impact customers the company takes an advance against the silver booked by them.

Material cost is essentially the metal: cost of materials consumed was Rs 618.99 cr on revenue of Rs 710.33 cr in FY26 (87.1%), and Rs 246.47 cr on Rs 270.47 cr in Q1 FY27 (91.1%). Revenue is therefore mostly pass-through silver value plus a conversion charge, which is why a silver price up 152% year on year roughly doubles reported revenue without any stated change in volume.

**What has already happened in the numbers.** Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30-Jun-2026) revenue was Rs 270.47 cr against Rs 134.14 cr a year earlier (+102%); PAT was Rs 33.84 cr against Rs 4.80 cr. FY26 revenue rose 44.89% to Rs 710.33 cr and net profit rose 193.97% to Rs 72.55 cr.

**The margin is the real signal, and it is not an inventory windfall.** Gross margin (revenue less materials consumed, adjusted for the change in finished-goods/WIP inventory) reads:

| Period | Revenue Rs cr | Materials less inventory change Rs cr | Gross margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 FY26 | 134.14 | 110.53 | 17.6% |
| FY26 | 710.33 | 529.13 | 25.5% |
| Q4 FY26 | 287.32 | 198.40 | 30.9% |
| Q1 FY27 | 270.47 | 164.75 | 39.1% |

The company reports silver hedging separately as an exceptional item — "profit/(loss) on Hedging of Silver in stock of the company, mark to market of forward contracts and loss due to fire". That line was +Rs 2.61 cr in FY26, -Rs 9.51 cr in Q4 FY26 and -Rs 0.39 cr in Q1 FY27. So the hedge offsets part of any pure holding gain, and the margin expansion above sits in the operating line, not in a one-off revaluation. This is a documented correction to the common framing of Modison as an inventory-revaluation play: the stock is partly hedged and the gain shows up as conversion margin on a higher metal base.
ideas.model:
**Physical unit.** The unit that drives revenue is kilograms of silver converted into contacts. The company does not disclose tonnage, installed capacity or utilisation in the FY26 annual report or in the Q1 FY27 filing, so the physical model cannot be closed from published documents. What can be measured is the metal-value model:

Revenue = silver (and tungsten) content at the prevailing metal price + conversion charge.

**Current run-rate.** Q1 FY27 annualised: revenue Rs 270.47 cr x 4 = Rs 1,082 cr; PAT Rs 33.84 cr x 4 = Rs 135.4 cr; EPS Rs 10.43 x 4 = Rs 41.72 on 3.245 cr shares (share count derived from the Rs 973.50 lakh final-dividend outgo at Rs 3.00 per Re 1 share).

**The cross-check that matters, and it cuts against extrapolation.** The silver signal is a year-on-year level effect, not a live move. Measured this run: WPI Silver for Apr-2026 is +152.4% over 12 months but -3.0% over 1 month and -11.0% over 3 months. LME-referenced spot silver (Westmetall, 21-Sep-2026) is EUR 1,815.5/kg: +5.4% over a week, but -3.5% over a month, -1.1% over three months and -1.0% over six months. India's silver import unit price for HS 710691 fell 19.3% month-on-month and 29.9% over three months in the Jul-2026 data even while the year-on-year comparison is +57.4%.

So the correct reading is: the earnings uplift from a silver price roughly 2.5x its year-ago level is already visible in Q1 FY27, and the forward question is whether the level holds rather than whether it rises further. On a flat silver price, the year-on-year revenue comparison stops flattering from roughly Q2 FY27 onward, and growth reverts to volume plus conversion-margin growth. Neither of those is disclosed.

**One more unknown that limits the model.** It is not possible from the filings to separate how much of the +102% Q1 revenue is metal price and how much is volume. Both readings fit the disclosed data.
ideas.valuation:
At the 22-Sep-2026 close of Rs 467.90 the market capitalisation is Rs 1,518.3 cr (BSE scrip master).

- Trailing: the BSE company header gives EPS Rs 31.31 and PE 14.94 (PB 7.37, ROE 49.31). That EPS ties to the last four reported quarters: 3.59 + 6.18 + 11.10 + 10.43 = Rs 31.30.
- On the Q1 FY27 run-rate (EPS Rs 41.72), the forward PE is 11.2x.
- On FY26 actual EPS of Rs 22.36, the trailing-year PE is 20.9x.

**Peers.** The dossier's peer list is drawn from the site's industry index and does not contain a comparable business — Hi-Tech Pipes (PE 24.61), Yuken India (110.88), Steel Exchange India (44.72), Manaksia Coated Metals (34.48), RIR Power Electronics (188.14). None of these makes electrical contacts. There is no listed Indian pure-play peer in silver electrical contacts that this run could identify, so a peer-multiple comparison is not available and no re-rating case is asserted on one.

**The re-rating case in one sentence, with its condition.** If the silver price stays near current levels and conversion margin holds near the Q1 FY27 level, the business earns roughly three times its FY25 profit on an unchanged asset base — and the multiple compression to ~11x forward has already priced part of that; if silver mean-reverts toward its 2025 level, both the revenue base and the inventory carrying value fall together.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Cash conversion is negative, and that is the central risk.** FY26 operating cash flow was **-Rs 64.18 cr** against PAT of Rs 72.55 cr (capital expenditure Rs 15.10 cr). Inventories rose from Rs 127.48 cr to Rs 219.80 cr (work-in-progress alone Rs 190.37 cr) and trade receivables from Rs 86.13 cr to Rs 159.97 cr. A rising silver price makes every unit of work-in-progress cost more, so growth consumes cash.
- **Debt more than doubled to fund that.** Current borrowings rose from Rs 71.16 cr to Rs 172.47 cr; with Rs 2.00 cr non-current, total debt is Rs 174.47 cr against equity of Rs 274.62 cr — the debt-to-equity ratio of 0.64 that the MD&A reports. Q1 FY27 finance cost was Rs 4.31 cr, annualising to about Rs 17 cr.
- **Inventory is carried at lower of cost and net realisable value.** A sustained fall in silver writes the Rs 219.80 cr inventory down through the P&L.
- **Related-party purchases from a promoter-owned company.** The 43rd AGM approved an omnibus material related-party transaction with Modison Copper Private Limited (MCPL) of up to **Rs 80 cr a year** (Rs 65 cr purchases of goods and job work, Rs 15 cr sales) until the 2027 AGM. The notice states MCPL is "controlled by certain promoters of the Company and their immediate relatives, who collectively hold more than 98% of its equity share capital", that the listed company holds nil in MCPL, and that the Managing Director (Mr. Girdhari Lal Modi) and Joint Managing Director (Mr. Kumar Jay Modi) are interested in it. Rs 65 cr of purchases is about 9% of FY26 revenue. The actual amount transacted in FY26 is **unknown** — the related-party table in the annual report PDF extracts with its columns misaligned and this run did not read a reliable figure.
- **Fire at the Vapi plant, 7-Feb-2026.** Rs 10.63 cr charged off (PPE written-down value Rs 1.54 cr, inventory Rs 8.67 cr, GST Rs 0.42 cr). An insurance claim of Rs 18.02 cr was lodged; Rs 1.70 cr was received towards PPE and booked as other income; the balance was still with the insurer at the Q1 FY27 filing. Operations were restored on 24-Feb-2026.
- **Exchange price queries.** BSE sought clarification on significant price movement on 3-Sep-2026 and the company replied on 4-Sep-2026. The stock is up 285.7% over six months and 190.8% over one year.
- **Liquidity.** Median daily turnover over 60 days is only Rs 33.5 lakh on a Rs 1,518 cr market capitalisation.
- Promoter holding is 52.23% as of June 2026, up from 52.11% a year earlier. The annual report states no loans were raised during the year against a pledge of shares. No auditor qualification, promoter-salary-versus-profit issue or preferential issue below market price was found in the documents read.
- Not a red flag: the wholly owned subsidiary Modison HV Private Limited ceased to be a subsidiary on 21-Sep-2026 — the filing states it "has not been operative since its acquisition" and the cessation "will not have any impact on the Company's revenue or business".
ideas.verify:
- **Volume versus price.** Kilograms of silver processed per quarter, which would separate the metal-price effect from real volume growth. Not disclosed in any filing read; a company-level import/export shipment dataset or a direct question to management would settle it.
- **How much of the silver stock is hedged.** The exceptional-item line proves a hedge exists and is small relative to profit, but the hedged proportion of the Rs 219.80 cr inventory is not stated.
- **Installed capacity and utilisation at Vapi**, including whether the February 2026 fire left any permanent capacity loss. Neither the annual report nor the Q1 filing gives a capacity number.
- **The MCPL relationship in practice** — actual FY26 purchase value, and whether transfer prices are benchmarked. A site visit or the audited related-party schedule read from the printed annual report would answer it.
- **The pending insurance claim** (Rs 18.02 cr lodged, Rs 1.70 cr received).
ideas.unknowns:
- Installed capacity, utilisation, and tonnage of contacts sold — not disclosed.
- The split of the Q1 FY27 revenue increase between silver price and volume.
- The hedged share of inventory, and the tenor of the forward contracts.
- Order book or customer concentration — the company publishes no investor presentation or concall transcript; the last two investor-meet intimations (30-May-2026, 1-Jun-2026) have no accompanying deck on BSE.
- Actual FY26 related-party transaction value with MCPL.
- Whether the "price-sharing arrangements with key customers" pass through the full metal move or a share of it, and with what lag — the wording is qualitative in every document read.
- Tungsten is the company's second named raw material, and tungsten prices have also risen sharply (the Tungsten group scores 10.0 in this run's signals). The documents do not disclose the silver-versus-tungsten split of material cost, so the net effect of the tungsten move on Modison is unknown.
ideas.confidence: medium: the silver exposure, the pass-through language and the margin expansion are all read directly from the company's own FY26 annual report and Q1 FY27 filing, but no capacity, tonnage or volume is disclosed anywhere, so the forward model rests on an annualised quarter rather than a physical driver — and the silver price itself is flat-to-down over one and three months, so the year-on-year tailwind fades from Q2 FY27 unless the level holds.

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying**
There is a long-running dedicated thread, "Modison LTD – Can the switchgear company switch fortunes?", started 01-Sep-2010: 65 posts, last post **17-Sep-2026**, about 18,500 views. All 65 posts were read. (The card's earlier note that the last post was in Jan-2025 is out of date: about 17 posts arrived in 2026.) For years the thread was sparse: a 2010 write-up, CRISIL grading notes and a 2011 management Q&A. From 2022 harsh.beria93 posted detailed notes from annual reports and AGMs. After the FY26 results the thread became busy. One member argues for a structural operating-leverage re-rating. Others push back that margins come from silver-price inventory gains, the market is small, working capital and debt have ballooned, and management communicates poorly (AGM-2026 notes by ha_the_meow).

### Threads
| Thread | Kind | Posts | Active | Link |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Modison LTD – Can the switchgear company switch fortunes? | dedicated | 65 | 01-Sep-2010 to 17-Sep-2026 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/modison-ltd-can-the-switchgear-company-switch-fortunes/402) |

### Points members raise
| Bull case raised | Bear case raised |
|---|---|
| Leading domestic maker of LV/HV contacts; approved supplier to ABB, Siemens, GE, Schneider, L&T; high switching costs once approved | TAM is small, competitors exist (Hindustan Platinum, Choksi Heraeus), nothing unique (RocketMan) |
| FY26/Q4 operating leverage; switchgear makers are adding capacity in India (abrahamappu, ha_the_meow) | Margin jump is largely silver inventory gains, not structural (RocketMan, harsh.beria93) |
| Company targets: ₹1,000 cr revenue pulled forward to FY28, ₹1,365 cr by FY30 (AGM-2026 notes) | Receivables and inventory up faster than sales; short-term debt up ~₹100 cr; credit lines heavily used (ha_the_meow) |
| New products (243 delivered per AGM-2025), an ISRO import-substitute alloy | Weak investor communication; no decks or calls (ha_the_meow) |
| Long dividend record | Related-party purchases from promoter firm Modison Copper; the Feb-2026 fire |

### New verified data from the forum
| Data point | Primary source that confirms it |
|---|---|
| **Installed capacity (card: "not disclosed"):** 250,000 arcing contacts a year for HV and **33 tonnes a year of LV contacts** at Vapi. LV (incl. MV) was ~75% and HV ~25% of sales; unexecuted order book ~₹100 cr on 15-Dec-2024 | CARE Ratings press release, 30-Dec-2024 |
| **Customer and input concentration (card: unknown):** top-5 customers ~45% of revenue, top-5 suppliers 60–65% of purchases. Silver is ~75–80% of raw-material purchases. Exports ~15% of sales, imports ~7% of purchases | CARE Ratings press release, Dec-2025 |
| **Hedging:** CARE says Modison hedges **part** of its inventory depending on market conditions and has **no defined hedging policy**. FY25 revenue growth (~21%) came mainly from higher silver realisations. Operating cycle 139 days; fund-based limits ~85% used (12 months to Oct-2025) | CARE Ratings press release, Dec-2025 |
| **Modison Copper (card: FY26 amount unknown):** total FY26 transactions with the promoter-owned MCPL were **₹50.42 cr** (the 43rd AGM notice). The related-party table is consistent with ~₹42.3 cr of purchases (FY25: ₹38.57 cr) and ~₹7.6 cr of sales. MCPL itself holds 1.26% of Modison | FY26 annual report (AGM notice explanatory statement; related-party note; shareholding table) |
| FY26 export turnover (FOB) was ₹82.16 cr, +5.79% on ₹77.67 cr, only ~12% of revenue as sales rose 45% | FY26 annual report, directors' report |
| The ISRO alloy claim from the AGM checks out: the annual report lists ISRO recognition of its brazing-alloy foils as an import substitute (Russian standard) | FY26 annual report, R&D / technology-absorption section |

### Claims on the forum not verified
- FY27 revenue target ₹880 cr, ₹1,000 cr by FY28 and ₹1,365 cr by FY30 — ha_the_meow, AGM-2026 notes — the AGM slides were posted on the forum, not filed with BSE; not verified from a filing.
- FY25 segment figures (LV ₹386 cr, volume +3.5%; HV ₹103 cr, volume +10.1%) and FY24 (LV ₹312 cr, HV ₹92 cr) — harsh.beria93, AGM notes — spoken at AGMs, not in filings read.
- ~80% share of India's HV contacts market and 16–17% of LV — tarunds / ha_the_meow — management statements; no filing gives market share.
- "35% of inventory is currently hedged" — harsh.beria93 (attributed to CARE) — not found in the Dec-2024 CARE release read.
- ROCE above 30% and ROE above 32% for FY26 — abrahamappu — not recomputed here.

### Where the forum disagrees with the filings
- **Cash flow and debt (abrahamappu, post #51):** says FY26 operating cash flow was "₹85+ Crore" and the balance sheet "virtually net-debt free". The audited FY26 cash-flow statement shows operating cash flow of **−₹64.18 cr** (FY25 −₹16.10 cr). Borrowings were ₹174.47 cr against equity of ₹274.62 cr (debt-to-equity 0.64). The same post's P/E and "₹849 share price" are the member's own projection.
- **"Not hedging silver anymore" (harsh.beria93's AGM-2025 notes):** the FY26 accounts still show a profit/(loss) line on "hedging of silver in stock" (+₹2.61 cr for FY26), and CARE (Dec-2025) says the company hedges part of its inventory.
- **Credit-line use "from 50% to 85%" (ha_the_meow):** CARE already put average fund-based utilisation at ~86% for the 12 months to Oct-2024, and ~85% to Oct-2025. The rise was in non-fund-based use (~9% to ~15%).
- **Exports rising "from 90 cr" (ha_the_meow's AGM-2026 notes):** FY26 export turnover in the annual report is ₹82.16 cr (FOB).

updates.title: Company Secretary and Compliance Officer resigns
updates.body: Ms Pooja Birendra Sinha resigned as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer with effect from close of business on 1-Oct-2026 'to pursue an alternate career opportunity outside the Organization'. Her resignation letter is dated 19-Sep-2026 and will be placed before the next board meeting for formal acceptance. Until a replacement is appointed, Jt. Managing Director Rajkumar Mohanlal Modi is designated Compliance Officer. A KMP exit three days after the card was written; the reason given is personal, not a dispute, and the filing says nothing more.

ideas.name: Sugs Lloyd Ltd
ideas.trigger: filing: ORDER — Letter of Award received 22-Sep-2026 from M/s Marshal Enterprises for execution of LT and HT infrastructure loss-reduction works under the RDSS scheme in Punjab, originally awarded by PSPCL, on a back-to-back basis. Order value Rs 213,47,86,468 including GST, to be executed in 15 months from the date of the LoA.
ideas.thesis:
**What the business physically does.** Sugs Lloyd is a power transmission and distribution EPC contractor that also manufactures niche electrical products. The Q1 FY27 earnings call (31-Jul-2026) describes three revenue streams: power T&D and smart grid, solar EPC, and products — of which the company says it is "India's largest manufacturer of fault passage indicators… with a domestic market share of over 50%". Fault passage indicators (FPI) carry, in management's words, "significantly better margin than our EPC business". CRISIL's rating rationale of 26-Aug-2026 describes the same company: "design, supply, erection, commissioning of electrical substations and power distribution and renewable projects", operating across Bihar, Delhi, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.

**The trigger, read from the filing itself.** The LoA is from M/s Marshal Enterprises — not from the utility. The filing states the works were "originally awarded by PSPCL in the State of Punjab" and come to Sugs Lloyd "on back to back basis". Order value is Rs 213.48 cr **including GST**; at 18% GST that is about Rs 180.9 cr of revenue, over a 15-month execution period, i.e. roughly Rs 144.7 cr a year against FY26 revenue of Rs 300.73 cr. The filing records that no promoter, promoter group or group company has any interest in the awarding entity.

**Why this filing matters more than its own size.** It is the third large award in three weeks. Counting only what the company has filed with BSE since 1-Sep-2026: Rs 214.27 cr from TPSODL and TPWODL for three-year distribution-network maintenance contracts in Odisha (1-Sep), Rs 24.63 cr from TPCODL (3-Sep), and Rs 213.48 cr today — about Rs 452 cr of fresh awards. For scale, fresh awards in the whole of Q1 FY27 were Rs 58.37 cr and the order book at 30-Jun-2026 was Rs 807 cr. Three weeks of Q2 have therefore added more than half of the entire order book that stood at the end of Q1.

**Order book and pipeline, as stated.** Order book Rs 807 cr at 30-Jun-2026, which management puts at "approximately 2.7x our full year last year FY26 revenue" and "approximately 2.5 years of contracted work already in hand". CRISIL independently records the same: "Healthy order book worth more than Rs 807 crore as on June 30, 2026, to be executed in the next 12-24 months". Qualified bid pipeline is stated at over Rs 1,350 cr with tenders at final stage exceeding Rs 1,200 cr. Management also says it has begun entering battery energy storage (BESS), expected to contribute from H2 FY27.
ideas.model:
**Physical driver.** The unit is a rupee of order book converted at a stated execution pace, so the model runs order book -> revenue -> margin.

**Reported base.**

| Period | Revenue Rs cr | EBITDA Rs cr | EBITDA margin | PAT Rs cr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY26 | 300.73 | 43.55 | 14.5% | 28.69 |
| Q1 FY26 | 59.41 | 8.90 | 14.98% | 5.78 |
| Q1 FY27 | 78.40 | ~12.0 | 15.3% | 7.50 |

Q1 FY27 revenue grew 32% year on year and PAT 30%. Q1 revenue mix: power T&D and smart grid Rs 46.32 cr (59% of revenue, against 27% in Q1 FY26), solar EPC Rs 32 cr (41%).

**Management's own guidance, and the arithmetic on it.** Management reaffirmed on the Q1 call a revenue target of **Rs 600 cr for FY27** (a figure the questioner put to them as "100% year-on-year growth from FY26", which they said they were "fully confident of achieving") and **Rs 1,000 cr for FY28**, with EBITDA margin expected to "remain same" — i.e. about 15% — and no equity raise planned. Applying the FY26 net margin of 9.5% that management cites:

- FY27 at Rs 600 cr x 9.5% = Rs 57 cr PAT -> EPS Rs 24.56 on 2.321 cr shares (share count derived from market capitalisation Rs 600.4 cr / close Rs 258.65) -> **10.5x** the 22-Sep close.
- FY28 at Rs 1,000 cr x 9.5% = Rs 95 cr PAT -> EPS Rs 40.93 -> **6.3x**.

**The cross-check that management's own numbers fail so far.** Q1 delivered Rs 78.40 cr, which is 13% of the Rs 600 cr target. Reaching it needs Rs 521.6 cr over the remaining three quarters — Rs 173.9 cr a quarter, or 2.2x the Q1 run-rate. Management attributes the slow start to teething problems on the Patna RDSS smart-grid project and says the slipped June revenue moves into Q2, and argues Q1 is seasonally the lightest quarter in India. That is a large second-half dependency and it is the single thing to watch at the Q2 result.

**A more conservative anchor.** On the Q1 run-rate annualised (PAT Rs 30 cr, EPS Rs 12.93) the PE is 20.0x, which is roughly the trailing multiple. The gap between 20x and 10.5x is entirely the guidance.
ideas.valuation:
At the 22-Sep-2026 close of Rs 258.65 the market capitalisation is Rs 600.4 cr (BSE scrip master).

- Trailing: BSE company header gives EPS Rs 12.36 and PE 20.93, consistent with FY26 PAT of Rs 28.69 cr over 2.321 cr shares.
- One year forward on management guidance (Rs 600 cr revenue, 9.5% net margin): EPS Rs 24.56, PE 10.5x.
- Two years forward on management guidance (Rs 1,000 cr, 9.5%): EPS Rs 40.93, PE 6.3x.
- One year forward on the Q1 FY27 run-rate with no ramp: EPS Rs 12.93, PE 20.0x.

**Peers.** The dossier's same-industry peer list from the site index (Hi-Tech Pipes, RIR Power Electronics, Yuken India and similar) contains no comparable T&D EPC contractor, so no peer multiple is quoted here. This run did not establish a peer set for the name and does not assert a re-rating case on one.

**The re-rating case in one sentence, with its condition.** The multiple compresses from ~21x to ~10x only if the second half of FY27 executes at more than twice the Q1 pace, which the Rs 807 cr order book at 30-Jun plus roughly Rs 452 cr of awards filed in the first three weeks of Q2 makes arithmetically possible but which no reported quarter yet demonstrates.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Receivables are the main weakness, and the rating agency says so.** CRISIL's 26-Aug-2026 rationale estimates **gross current assets of 265 days** as of 31-Mar-2026, with **receivables of around 245 days** ("owing to large credit period and retention money, with certain receivables not due yet") and inventory of 14 days, and adds that the working-capital requirement "is further expected to increase over the medium term" and that its "effective management will remain monitorable". Q1 FY27 finance cost was Rs 2.45 cr, which management attributes to "working capital being invested to mobilize and ramp up our various projects".
- **The counterparty on today's order is a private firm, not the utility.** The LoA is from M/s Marshal Enterprises on a back-to-back basis for works originally awarded by PSPCL. Payment security on a back-to-back sub-contract sits with the intermediary, not with the state utility, and the margin on back-to-back work is not disclosed. This is a different risk profile from the company's stated strength that "the large majority of our business is with sovereign-backed government entities or companies rated AAA, AA like TATAs".
- **Competition and pricing power.** CRISIL: "low entry barriers and modest capital intensity have led to intense competition, which in turn, restricts the pricing flexibility and bargaining power of players… aggressive bidding constrains profitability."
- **Guidance risk.** The Rs 600 cr FY27 target requires 2.2x the Q1 run-rate for three quarters. Management gave a reason (project teething problems, supplier delays from raw-material shortages, seasonality) but the shortfall is real and unresolved as of the last reported quarter.
- **Exchange price query.** BSE sought clarification on significant price movement on 20-Aug-2026. The stock is up 164.1% over one year, 103.3% over three months and 31.1% over one month, and closed 22-Sep at Rs 258.65 against a 65-day window high of Rs 289.20.
- **SME platform** (BSE group MT). Median daily turnover over 60 days is Rs 106.5 lakh — liquid by SME standards but small in absolute terms.
- Positives on the same checklist: promoter holding is 70.54% at June 2026, up from 70.00% a year earlier, with no pledge disclosed in the filings read. CRISIL assigned Crisil BBB/Stable and Crisil A3+ on Rs 225 cr of bank facilities (Bank Guarantee Rs 119 cr, Cash Credit Rs 105 cr) on 26-Aug-2026, treating a Rs 10 cr unsecured loan as debt; gearing improved to 0.5x (from 2.1x) and TOLANW to 1.0x as of 31-Mar-2026 after the Rs 72 cr IPO of September 2025, with interest coverage of 6.3x. Management stated it does not foresee an equity raise. No auditor qualification, related-party concern or regulatory notice was found in the documents read.
ideas.verify:
- **Whether the Q2 FY27 result shows the promised ramp** — the June revenue said to have slipped into Q2, and a quarterly revenue materially above Rs 78 cr. This is the single decisive check and it arrives with the H1 result.
- **The margin on back-to-back sub-contracted work** such as today's Punjab LoA, versus directly awarded utility contracts. Not disclosed for any order.
- **Who M/s Marshal Enterprises is** and what its own payment terms with PSPCL are — this determines whether the Rs 180.9 cr ex-GST is as secure as the company's sovereign-backed order book generally is. A tender-portal or ROC check would establish it.
- **Collection on the stretched receivables** — whether gross current assets fall from 265 days as the Patna project reaches what management calls the "bulk billing phase".
- **FPI product revenue**, which management targets at 10% of revenue by FY28 and which carries better margins; the current rupee value of product revenue was not given separately in the documents read.
ideas.unknowns:
- Order-book value as of today. The Rs 807 cr figure is as of 30-Jun-2026; adding the roughly Rs 452 cr of awards filed since 1-Sep-2026 without knowing Q2 execution or any completions would be a guess, so no current figure is asserted.
- Segment-level margins (T&D versus solar EPC versus products) — not disclosed.
- The margin and payment terms specific to the Punjab back-to-back order.
- Customer concentration, and how much of the order book is with the single Patna RDSS project.
- The identity and standing of M/s Marshal Enterprises.
- Whether the Rs 214.27 cr Odisha contracts (three-year maintenance) are recognised evenly over three years — the split by year is not stated.
- Q1 FY27 EBITDA is quoted by management as "almost INR12 crores" at a 15.3% margin; an exact figure was not in the filings read.
ideas.confidence: medium: the trigger was read in the company's own LoA filing, and the order book, guidance, margins and balance-sheet risks are corroborated by both the Q1 FY27 earnings-call transcript and an independent CRISIL rating rationale published in the last month — but the FY27 guidance implies more than twice the Q1 run-rate for three straight quarters, no reported quarter yet demonstrates that pace, and 245-day receivables mean the growth is funded before it is collected.

ideas.name: Bhagyanagar India Ltd
ideas.trigger: price: Copper - LME copper US$14,788/t on 2026-09-21, 98% of its 52-week range, +5.3% 1w / +24.4% 6m; MetalBook Mumbai copper CC rod Rs 1,410/kg dated 2026-09-16, +48.3% y/y and the highest of 17 readings since 2025-07-08; HS 7407 import unit price +157.5% smoothed y/y to Jul-2026
ideas.thesis:
**What the business physically does.** Bhagyanagar India Ltd (BIL) is the listed holding of the Surana group's secondary-copper business, run through wholly-owned Bhagyanagar Copper Pvt Ltd (BCPL). It buys copper scrap — management states about 75% is imported — melts and refines it, and sells copper rod, bus bars (plain, tin-coated, silver-plated, paper-insulated), foils, tapes, enamelled wire, nuggets and solar absorber fins. The physical unit that drives revenue is a tonne of copper sold. Q1 FY27 (quarter to 30-Jun-2026, consolidated): 5,278 MT sold, revenue Rs 705.08 cr, of which Rs 28.41 cr was by-product sales, giving a realisation of Rs 1,279/kg as the company states it. Value-added products were 63% of the mix, which the company calls its highest.

**Read the reported numbers with care.** BSE's detailed-results endpoint returns BIL's STANDALONE accounts — FY26 revenue Rs 5.88 cr, and a BSE-header PE of 988.67. Those are the holding company alone. The operating business is in the consolidated statements: FY26 revenue Rs 2,377.83 cr, EBITDA Rs 106.14 cr, PAT Rs 50.17 cr on 24,655 MT. Every figure in this note is consolidated, taken from the Q1 FY27 investor presentation and the FY26 annual report.

**Why the copper price matters here, in management's own words.** This is not an inventory-gain story; the company says the opposite. On the 28-Jul-2026 earnings call the Managing Director set out the mechanism: *"our purchases of raw materials are as a percentage of LME... our purchases would range from 86% to 95% of LME, depending on the quality of the scrap and our sales are also more or less linked to LME. So, our margins are going to be more stable in percentage terms than in rupees per kilo terms."* And directly: *"if the prices go up 20%, my margin will still remain at 5%, but the EBITDA per kg will go up 20%."* On hedging: *"our purchases and sales are more or less hedged on a daily basis... approximately 85% of the inventory which is there is hedged on the exchange."*

So the transmission is arithmetic, not speculative: a percentage EBITDA margin applied to an LME-linked realisation means a higher copper price raises rupee EBITDA per kg roughly in proportion, with volumes unchanged. That is what the last four quarters show. Realisation went from Rs 846/kg in Q1 FY26 to Rs 1,279/kg in Q1 FY27, +51.2%. Over the same year EBITDA per kg went from a stated Rs 72 to Rs 72 — the company reports Q1 FY27 EBITDA/kg of Rs 72 as its highest — while volume FELL 6.5% (5,646 MT to 5,278 MT) and consolidated PAT still rose 167% (Rs 7.57 cr to Rs 20.25 cr). EBITDA margin went 3.33% to 5.43%, PAT margin 1.56% to 2.87%.

**Management attributes part of that margin to a one-off.** The MD said April and May were disrupted (*"the disruption of all the trade routes and the shortage of material"*), that the company *"could take advantage of the situation by increasing our margins"*, and that 2,200 of the quarter's 5,278 MT came in June alone. Guidance for the full year is an EBITDA margin *"between 5% and 5.5%"*, with 5.5% *"a little difficult"* to hold. Two structural reasons are given for margins being higher than the 2.5-3% of two years ago: a richer value-added mix, and customs duty removed from 1-Jan-2025.

**The commodity signal this sits on.** Copper is the strongest live move in the panel: LME copper US$14,788/t on 2026-09-21, at 98% of its 52-week range, +5.3% in a week, +8.4% over three months and +24.4% over six. Trading Economics copper +48.8% over a year. The Indian print — MetalBook Mumbai copper CC rod 8mm — is Rs 1,410/kg dated 2026-09-16, +48.3% year on year and the highest of the 17 readings our series holds since 2025-07-08. That series is sparse and has a seven-month hole between 2026-02-12 and 2026-09-16, so treat it as corroboration of direction, not a continuous record. India's customs unit price for HS 7407 (copper rods) is +157.5% on the smoothed year-on-year measure to Jul-2026, and WPI Copper wire +20.3% over twelve months to Apr-2026.
ideas.model:
**Capacity and utilisation, from the call.** Capacity is 35,000 MTPA, *"which is online now"*. FY26 volume 24,655 MT = 70.4% utilisation. Q1 FY27 annualised (5,278 x 4 = 21,112 MT) = 60.3%, depressed by the April-May sourcing disruption. The next leg — 35,000 to 45,000 MT — is guided for *"between April and June of next year; more likely June"* (i.e. FY28), at a capex the MD calls *"a 40 crore capex over 2 years... quite insignificant for our balance sheet"*.

**FY27 revenue from the physical drivers.** Management guides 12-15% volume growth for FY27 and an average realisation it set at Rs 1,300/kg at the start of the year, adding *"I think we will be at a price higher than that."* Taking the guidance at face value:

- volume: 24,655 MT x 1.12 = 27,614 MT; x 1.15 = 28,353 MT
- revenue at Rs 1,300/kg: 27,614 MT -> Rs 3,590 cr; 28,353 MT -> Rs 3,686 cr
- against FY26 revenue of Rs 2,377.83 cr, that is +51% to +55%, of which roughly two-thirds is price

**Earnings.** Applying the guided EBITDA margin band to the low-volume case (27,614 MT, Rs 3,590 cr), and carrying FY26 depreciation (Rs 8.2 cr) and interest (Rs 36.0 cr, rounded to Rs 40 cr for the higher working capital a higher copper price needs) with the Q1 FY27 effective tax rate of 25.3%:

| FY27E EBITDA margin | EBITDA Rs cr | PAT Rs cr | EPS Rs | PE at Rs 444.9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.5% (the bear case put to management) | 161.5 | 84.7 | 25.3 | 17.6 |
| 5.0% (low end of guidance) | 179.5 | 98.1 | 29.3 | 15.2 |
| 5.5% (high end of guidance) | 197.4 | 111.5 | 33.3 | 13.4 |

At 15% volume growth the same margins give PAT of Rs 87.9-115.4 cr and PE of 12.9-17.0. Share count 3,34,96,434 (3,19,95,000 plus the 15,01,434 preferential shares listed 28-Aug-2026); 3,34,96,434 x Rs 444.9 = Rs 1,490.3 cr, which ties exactly to the BSE market cap, so the count is right.

**Trailing.** TTM consolidated PAT = Q1 FY27 Rs 20.25 cr + FY26 Rs 50.17 cr - Q1 FY26 Rs 7.57 cr = Rs 62.85 cr. At Rs 1,490.3 cr the trailing PE is 23.7x — not the 988.67 the BSE header shows on standalone EPS.

**The arithmetic is guidance-driven and should be read as such.** Volume growth, realisation and margin are all management's numbers, not independent estimates. Q1 FY27 annualised (PAT Rs 20.25 cr x 4 = Rs 81 cr) sits just below the bear case, and Q1 carried the margin benefit management called a one-off, so the low end is the one to weight.
ideas.valuation:
**Where it trades.** Rs 444.9 on 2026-09-23, market cap Rs 1,490.3 cr, trailing consolidated PE 23.7x, FY27E PE 13.4-17.6x on management's guidance. The stock is up 388.2% over one year, 201.3% over six months and 13.9% over one month, and closed at Rs 444.9 against a 52-week high of Rs 447.45 — i.e. at the top of its range. Median daily turnover over 60 days is Rs 46.7 lakh, which is thin for the market cap.

**Peers.** The site's industry bucket for this name ("Copper / Commodities") is mixed and does not hold a clean comparable: Arfin India Rs 1,544 cr at PE 95.92, Prakash Industries Rs 2,144 cr at 6.85, Manaksia Steels Rs 693 cr at 12.79, 20 Microns Rs 774 cr at 12.67, Maan Aluminium Rs 631 cr (PE n/a). Aluminium and steel converters are not copper recyclers, so this table sets a range (roughly 7-13x for commodity converters, higher for the aluminium names) rather than a true benchmark. The closest listed comparables by process — Gravita India and Pondy Oxides, both lead/multi-metal recyclers — sit outside the Rs 200-2,000 cr universe this page screens and were not measured this run.

**The re-rating case in one sentence.** If the guided 12-15% volume growth and a realisation above Rs 1,300/kg both land while the margin holds at the guided 5-5.5%, FY27 PAT roughly doubles off a trailing Rs 62.85 cr without any change in the multiple.

**What would end the run.** Copper falling back: the same percentage-margin mechanism that lifts rupee EBITDA per kg when LME rises takes it away when LME falls, and at a materially lower copper price management's own answer was that margins were 2.5-3% two years ago. A questioner on the call put the bear case directly — margins at 4.5% *"even if copper comes down to $10,000"* — and the answer rested on mix and the customs-duty change, not on the price. Volumes are also hostage to imported scrap: 75% is imported and a trade-route disruption cost the company two months of throughput this year.
ideas.red_flags:
Each item answered from documents read this run.

- **The copper business is leaving this company.** This is the single most important fact about BHAGYANGR today and the map did not carry it. Under a composite scheme approved by NCLT Hyderabad on 07-Sep-2026 (filed with BSE the same day), BCPL amalgamates into BIL and the copper business undertaking then demerges out of BIL into Tieramet Ltd, which is to be listed separately on NSE and BSE. In the MD's words: *"what will be left in Bhagyanagar India will be the three land parcels, which are in the heart of the city and our windmill project, while Tieramet will have all our copper infrastructure and businesses."* The entitlement is 1:1 — one Tieramet share for every BIL share held on the record date — so a holder on that date ends up with both halves, but after it the copper economics described in this note belong to Tieramet, not to the scrip 512296 that the page is tracking. The record date had not been announced in any filing read this run.
- **Promoter shares pledged to fund the company's own hedging.** A clarification filed 24-Aug-2026 states that 12,73,335 equity shares were transferred by MD Devendra Surana to BCPL off-market *"solely to facilitate the required pledge for hedging purposes"*, with no consideration, and that the transfer had been showing on the BSE/NSE portals as a promoter SALE from an e-mail dated 16-Jan-2026 until it was reversed in August. Seven months of a misleading public disclosure on the promoter's holding, and a standing pledge whose size scales with the copper price.
- **A rising copper price consumes cash.** Asked whether the fundraise was to cover MCX margin, the MD said: *"As the copper prices go up, we will require more and more money to fund the margin for MCX... If the copper price doubles, yes, we will definitely require a lot of funds."* The mechanism that lifts earnings tightens working capital at the same time.
- **A Rs 750 cr related-party approval.** The notice of the 41st AGM (30-Sep-2026) seeks shareholder approval for providing loans, guarantees, securities and investments of up to Rs 750 cr to Tieramet Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary — 31.54% of the prior year's consolidated turnover, and the company discloses it as a material RPT. The AGM notice records no such transactions in the previous financial year. It is consistent with funding the demerged copper entity, but it is a large RPT to a company that is about to leave the group.
- **Dilution.** 15,01,434 shares were issued on a preferential basis at Rs 348 (Rs 2 face value plus Rs 346 premium), board approval 30-Jun-2026, trading approval 11-Sep-2026 — Rs 52.25 cr, about 4.5% of the enlarged capital, and priced 21.8% below the 23-Sep close. The MD described it as the first of about Rs 150 cr: *"we have just finalized the first round of raising, at 52 crores... The second tranche will probably be around March, after the demerger is done, in the standalone copper unit."* The allottees were not read this run.
- **Debt is working capital and it grows with the copper price.** Consolidated at 31-Mar-2026: current borrowings Rs 209.63 cr (FY25 Rs 191.73 cr), non-current Rs 6.13 cr after current maturities of Rs 6.08 cr. FY26 interest Rs 35.96 cr. Trade receivables are pledged as security for borrowings. Management's own FY30 projection is Rs 300-350 cr of debt.
- **Demand risk raised on the call and not resolved.** A participant noted data centres moving from 48V to 800V DC architecture, which he had read would cut copper bus-bar demand by about 50%. Management supplies these products (roughly 600 MT to data centres in Q1 FY27, of which 250 MT tin-coated). The answer was not read in full this run.
- **Auditor remarks, promoter salary, GST or regulatory notices, tender-portal verification:** not examined this run. Stated as unknown rather than cleared.
- **Volume is not evidence.** BHAGYANGR did not reach the scan's candidate list today and was not a volume breakout; it came through the commodity lane. That is the right way round — the 2026-09-22 study found a volume explosion in 81% of 5x runs and 78% of the stocks that went nowhere.
ideas.verify:
- **The record date for the Tieramet demerger, and how the two entities price after it.** NCLT approved on 07-Sep-2026; the record date, the listing timetable for Tieramet and the split of the Rs 1,490 cr market cap between the copper entity and the land-plus-windmill residue are the whole question for anyone holding scrip 512296. Only a subsequent BSE filing will answer it.
- **Company-level import shipments for copper scrap.** 75% of raw material is imported and the April-May disruption is the stated reason volume fell. A shipment dataset would show whether June's 2,200 MT recovery held through Q2, which is the difference between the 12-15% volume guidance landing and not. Paid or captcha-gated; not automated here.
- **Who took the Rs 52.25 cr preferential allotment at Rs 348**, and whether the second tranche of about Rs 100 cr is placed in the demerged copper entity as the MD indicated. Read the allotment filing and the postal ballot or EGM notice when it comes.
- **The size of the promoter pledge against MCX margin at today's copper price**, from the next shareholding pattern (Sep-2026 quarter, due mid-October).
- **Realisation and EBITDA per kg for Q2 FY27** (quarter to 30-Sep-2026), which is the first clean test of the mechanism without the April-May disruption distorting both volume and margin.
ideas.unknowns:
- The Tieramet record date, its listing date, and the opening reference price for either entity. Not in any filing read this run.
- Segment revenue by product within the value-added mix. The presentation gives the 63% value-added share and names about 20 products across three categories, but not revenue per product.
- The allottees of the preferential issue.
- Auditor remarks or changes, promoter remuneration against profit, and any GST or regulatory notices — the FY26 annual report was searched for borrowings and related-party items but these sections were not read.
- The full management answer on the 48V-to-800V data-centre architecture risk.
- Whether the Rs 750 cr Tieramet RPT was approved at the 30-Sep-2026 AGM. The AGM had not been held as of this run.
- A clean listed copper-recycler peer set with comparable PEs. Gravita and Pondy Oxides sit outside this page's Rs 200-2,000 cr universe and were not measured.
- USD/INR was not taken from any document this run, so no LME figure in this note has been converted to rupees.
ideas.confidence: medium: the exposure and the transmission mechanism are documented as precisely as this method ever gets - consolidated revenue of Rs 705 cr in one quarter, realisation Rs 1,279/kg, purchases at 86-95% of LME and sales LME-linked, stated by the Managing Director on a filed transcript, with 85% of inventory hedged so the gain is margin-per-kg rather than inventory revaluation. It is held to medium, not high, by one structural fact and one timing fact: the copper business demerges out of this scrip into Tieramet Ltd under a scheme NCLT approved on 07-Sep-2026 with no record date yet announced, so the entity a buyer of 512296 holds afterwards is not the one described here; and the stock is already up 388% in a year and closed at the top of its 52-week range, with the FY27 model resting entirely on management's own volume, price and margin guidance.

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying.** There is one dedicated thread, started 9-Mar-2026, with 94 posts; the last post is dated 10-Sep-2026, so it has been quiet for about three weeks. Two users, RocketMan and gaurav, write most of it. Both say they hold the stock, and the tone is mostly bullish. The main argument is over the right yardstick for profit. The bulls use EBITDA per tonne (Rs 62,000 in Q4 FY26, Rs 72,000 in Q1 FY27). Doubters say part of that figure comes from by-product sales and a one-off Q1 margin. Other threads the members return to: how much the land is worth, the Rs 52 cr preferential issue at Rs 348, the promoter shares pledged to MCX, a DGGI GST notice, and the stock sitting in the exchanges' 5% ESM band. Nobody in the thread discusses the 8-Oct-2026 record date or how the stock will price once the Tieramet demerger goes through. Three broad threads mention the company in substance.

### Threads
| Thread | Kind | Posts | Active | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bhagyanagar India Ltd - Copper Recycling Play | dedicated | 94 | 2026-03-09 to 2026-09-10 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/bhagyanagar-india-ltd-copper-recycling-play/218879) |
| Demergers on the radar | mention | 1 | 2026-04-23 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/demergers-on-the-radar/12270/331) |
| Data center value chain in India | mention | 1 | 2026-01-30 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/data-center-value-chain-in-india-investment-opportunities/130278/64) |
| The anti-portfolio | mention | 1 | 2026-05-11 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/the-anti-portfolio/28464/804) |

### Points members raise
| Bull case raised | Bear case raised |
|---|---|
| The company recycles its own scrap, which peers such as Precision Wires are only now spending capex to build. Members say this gives cheaper raw material and a head start under the new EPR recycled-content rules (RocketMan) | EBITDA per kg is flattered: by-product sales rose to Rs 28.4 cr from Rs 6.3 cr and sit inside the per-kg figure (vivek_lakhani); management itself called the Q1 margin a one-off (Subrata_Mal) |
| Profit per tonne rises with the copper price, and the value-added mix (about 60%+) is what peers are still building (RocketMan, Divyank_Patel) | Margins are only 4-5%, debt is high and cash is low; if copper falls, rupee EBITDA falls with it (Aman_Jain3, vikas_sinha in the anti-portfolio thread) |
| Three land parcels near Hyderabad sit on the books far below market value and go to the residual company after the demerger (gaurav, RocketMan) | Raising Rs 150 cr against an equity base of about Rs 250 cr, when capacity grows only about 28%, may not be an efficient use of capital (tyguiijfyjg_Chauhany) |
| Institutional allottees in the preferential issue, at a price close to market (gaurav) | Operating cash flow is lumpy and working capital grows with the copper price (gaurav) |
| Jain Resource Recycling and Pondy Oxides are said to trade at much higher multiples (RocketMan) | Jain, Pondy and Gravita are all moving into value-added copper within about 12 months, so the moat depends on product qualification, not furnaces (Divyank_Patel) |
|  | Promoter-linked ED search reported in 2025 (Soham_Jain); a member replied that it concerns a JV partner in a promoter real-estate venture, not the listed company (RocketMan) |

### New verified data from the forum
| Data point | Primary source that confirms it |
|---|---|
| **DGGI GST show-cause notice.** Notice No. 06/2026-27, dated 26-May-2026, alleges irregular input tax credit. It proposes Rs 17.50 cr of tax plus interest on the company and on MD Devendra Surana. The company says it **paid the Rs 17.50 cr under protest**, will reply, and expects no impact. The card had "GST notices not examined". Members say GST notices are common in the scrap trade because scrap passes through unregistered dealers (RocketMan). That is their explanation, not the company's. | [BSE filing 27-May-2026 (Reg 30)](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/b6e2212c-54ec-4f0c-8a7c-1248d764bcf0.pdf) |
| **Who took the Rs 52.25 cr preferential issue** (the card listed this as unknown). Three QIBs took 12,06,895 shares: LC Pharos Multi Strategy Fund VCC 5,74,712; Niveshaay Hedgehogs Fund 5,74,712; Ashika Global Finance 57,471. Four individuals took 2,94,539 shares: Ashok Atluri 1,14,942; Ajay Pancholi 1,00,862; Gulab Shrimal 50,000; Apurva Mahesh Shah 28,735. The total is 15,01,434 shares at Rs 348, and **all allottees are non-promoter**. The floor-price relevant date was 23-Jun-2026. | [Board outcome 30-Jun-2026](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/c047988a-9643-4d3d-8145-61654feb2a67.pdf) |
| **Where the scrap comes from.** The US supplies 35% of scrap, the largest single country. Brazil, the UK, Australia, Colombia and Canada supply about 7-8% each. Gulf sourcing is under 5%, and Saudi Arabia (about 4%) ranks ninth. | [Q4 FY26 call transcript, 2-May-2026](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/5932469c-ea84-4e4b-a619-5cafcad8c94a.pdf) |
| **How big the promoter pledge is.** The MD said the only pledge is of his own shares, given to MCX as security for hedging. It is under 5% of his personal holding, and **nothing is pledged to banks**. The 96% pledge figure that screeners showed was, in his words, an error. | Q4 FY26 call transcript |
| **The land parcels.** About 4 acres at Nacharam, 4.5 acres at Uppal and about 5 acres at Hardware Park. Only the Uppal parcel is under active consideration, either for own development or a joint-development residential project. Nothing has been decided on the other two. | Q4 FY26 call transcript |
| **Credit rating.** In March 2026 CRISIL assigned **BBB+** to the subsidiary BCPL's long-term bank facilities. | FY26 annual report, Directors' Report ([BSE 07-Sep-2026](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/015b0b6c-241b-442f-bb41-5a70622bb1ea.pdf)) |
| **Silver-plated bus bars for AI data centres** were launched in Q3 FY26. The company says it is the only Indian maker of copper bus bars up to 300 mm wide. In the Q4 call, management said silver- and tin-plated bars are a very small share of revenue today, with a hope of 7-10% of revenue in 3-5 years. | [Q3 FY26 investor presentation, 30-Jan-2026](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/f617f9cf-ec34-4cf7-9041-4fb9666b6acd.pdf); Q4 FY26 transcript |
| **Other businesses.** Lead recycling is dropped for at least the next 12-18 months. About Rs 10 cr is planned for plastic recycling of the cable waste that arrives with the scrap. | Q4 FY26 call transcript |

### Claims on the forum not verified
- Land worth about Rs 1,000 cr, and "400 cr free cash flow" from a 4-lakh sq ft joint development at Uppal — RocketMan. No filing read gives a land valuation or a signed JDA. The call describes Uppal only as under consideration.
- Real estate "book value of 29 cr" — gaurav. The FY26 standalone PPE note shows freehold land at Rs 14.91 cr gross on 1-Apr-2025. No Rs 29 cr real-estate figure was found.
- About Rs 25/kg of EBITDA is a fixed fabrication charge — Divyank_Patel and RocketMan, citing a video interview. No filing was read that states this.
- "Some small portion was sold in March for personal use" by the promoter — gaurav. This was not checked against SAST or insider-trading disclosures.
- Jain Resource's copper EBITDA per tonne (about Rs 13-14k in Q4; Rs 30-33k guided) — RocketMan and vivek_lakhani. These are a peer's figures. Jain's filings were not read.
- Rules for exiting the ESM framework (a 90-day minimum, then weekly reviews) — vivek_lakhani. The NSE/BSE ESM circulars were not read.
- EPR recycled-content targets for copper (for example 20% by 2031-32) — RocketMan. The MoEF&CC notification was not read.

### Where the forum disagrees with the filings
- **When the revenue target falls.** A post in the demergers thread says the copper business targets Rs 5,000 cr of revenue "in FY 28" (gaurav). On the 28-Jul-2026 call the MD gave **FY30**, calling it a conservative date, with FY29 possible ([Q1 FY27 transcript](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/431bf628-c59f-4366-9259-8cfd1416d077.pdf)).
- **When the scheme was approved.** The opening post says NCLT approved the demerger scheme on 29-Jan-2026 (Midhunjoe). The sanction order was filed on **7-Sep-2026**. The January date matches the stage when stakeholder meetings were being convened (the post itself says meetings were set for 14-Mar-2026), not a final sanction.
- **The pledge.** One member puts it at "4-6%" (RocketMan). The MD said it is under 5% of his personal holding. Neither figure has been checked against a shareholding-pattern pledge disclosure.

updates.title: Record date 8-Oct-2026 fixed for the Tieramet demerger, 1 Tieramet share per BIL share
updates.body: Board meeting of 25-Sep-2026 (concluded 3:15 pm) fixed Thursday 8-Oct-2026 as the record date under the NCLT-sanctioned Composite Scheme: Tieramet Ltd (Resulting Company) issues one fully paid Rs 2 share for every one Rs 2 share held in Bhagyanagar India. updates.title: ICRA assigns [ICRA]A- (Rating Watch, Developing) on Rs 654 cr of BCPL bank lines
updates.body: ICRA's letter of 28-Sep-2026 and rationale of 29-Sep-2026 assign [ICRA]A-, on watch with developing implications because of the demerger, to Rs 595 cr of fund-based limits (HDFC 195, Yes 100, HSBC 75, Kotak 65, Axis 40, SBI 20, proposed 100) and Rs 59 cr of term loans of Bhagyanagar Copper Pvt Ltd, the copper subsidiary. Numbers in the rationale (BCPL standalone, audited): FY26 operating income Rs 2,372 cr vs Rs 1,620 cr (+46.4%), PAT Rs 48.0 cr vs Rs 12.6 cr, OPBDIT/OI 4.4% vs 2.2%, interest cover 3.0x vs 2.2x, total debt/OPBDIT 3.6x vs 10.6x; EBITDA per kg under Rs 25 in FY25, about Rs 60 in Q4 FY26, over Rs 70 in Q1 FY27; value-added products 59% of volumes and over 60% of revenue in FY26 (busbars Rs 818 cr vs Rs 507 cr); FY26 volume 24,654 MT; bank-limit utilisation 74% for the six months to Aug-2026; capex about Rs 40 cr over two years; term debt due in FY27 about Rs 7 cr against expected cash accrual over Rs 90 cr. ICRA expects interest cover of about 5.0x in FY27 and volume growth of 15-20% a year (the company itself guided 12-15% for FY27 on the Q1 call). Upgrade trigger: interest cover above 6.0x sustained; downgrade trigger: below 4.0x. An investment-grade rating with the agency's own numbers confirming the card's FY26 base.

updates.title: AGM approves material related-party transactions with Tieramet for FY27 and s.185/s.186 limits; MD re-appointed
updates.body: 41st AGM on 30-Sep-2026, 63 members present, auditors' reports unqualified; a speaker asked about EBITDA margin, capex and the business plan and the Chairman 'provided the requisite insights' (no numbers in the proceedings). Seven resolutions, all passed per the 2-Oct-2026 scrutinizer's report: item 4 re-appoints Devendra Surana as Managing Director (special); item 5 approves transactions under s.185 (loans/guarantees to director-interested entities): 2,24,00,785 promoter votes plus public votes, 99.90% in favour; item 6 s.186 loans and investments; item 7 material related-party transactions with Tieramet Ltd for FY2026-27 (ordinary): 9,81,388 for, 2,041 against (99.79%) with the promoter group's votes treated as invalid because they are interested. The card's annual-report source puts the Tieramet RPT limit at Rs 750 cr, which is 32% of FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 2,377.83 cr. After the 8-Oct demerger Tieramet holds the copper business and BIL's dealings with it are dealings with a promoter-controlled separate company - the related-party line the checklist flags.

updates.title: CFO Surendra Bhutoria moves to Tieramet; BIL to appoint a new CFO
updates.body: Mr Surendra Bhutoria ceased to be CFO of Bhagyanagar India from 7-Oct-2026 'consequent upon transfer of his employment to Tieramet Limited'; no resignation letter because it is a transfer. The 28-Sep ICRA letter was addressed to him as CFO of Bhagyanagar Copper. Consistent with the copper business and its finance team moving to Tieramet; BIL says a new CFO will be appointed 'in due course'.

updates.title: Ex-demerger: BIL closes Rs 41.40 vs Rs 453.95; cost of acquisition split 89.36% Tieramet / 10.64% BIL
updates.body: 8-Oct-2026 was the record date and the BSE close fell from Rs 453.95 (7-Oct, 50,958 shares) to Rs 41.40 (8-Oct, 2,160 shares) - a 90.9% drop that is the demerger of the copper business into Tieramet, not a fall in value: every holder now also owns one Tieramet share per BIL share, and Tieramet is not yet listed (no listing filing by 9-Oct-2026; its listing date and price are unknown). The board on 8-Oct took note of the auditor-certified cost apportionment under s.73 of the Income-tax Act 2025: copper undertaking net book value Rs 177.60 cr / BIL net worth Rs 198.75 cr at 31-Mar-2025 = 89.36% of a holder's cost goes to the Tieramet shares, 10.64% stays with BIL (the market's 41.40/453.95 = 9.1% is close to that ratio). The scorecard's call close of Rs 444.9 can only be judged as BIL + Tieramet once Tieramet trades; the card's whole physical model (35,000 MT, Rs 1,300/kg, 5-5.5% margin) now describes Tieramet.

updates.title: Executive Director Venkateswara Rao Nukala resigns; promoter Mangilal Narender Surana joins the board
updates.body: The 8-Oct-2026 board accepted the resignation of Mr Venkateswara Rao Nukala (DIN 10481800), Executive Director, from close of business 8-Oct-2026 'due to personal reasons', with his letter confirming no other material reasons - he had been re-appointed by rotation at the AGM eight days earlier. The same meeting appointed Shri Mangilal Narender Surana (DIN 00075086), chemical engineer with 36 years in telecom cables, metals and solar, past FAPCCI president and FICCI chairman, related to MD Devendra Surana, as additional non-executive non-independent (promoter) director, subject to members' approval. Second KMP-level departure in two days after the CFO's transfer.

updates.title: ValuePickr: members note the 1:1 Tieramet credit and BIL 'retained at ~10%' - matches the filings
updates.body: Post #103 by utsav31 (8-Oct) says the demerger shows on Zerodha as 1 Tieramet share per Bhagyanagar share with BIL's value retained at about 10% of the last price; #104-#106 (9-Oct) say Tieramet holds the copper business and ask when it lists. Verified against filings: 1:1 ratio and 8-Oct record date (BSE 25-Sep-2026); 10.64% cost retained in BIL per the auditor's certificate (BSE 8-Oct-2026); BSE closes Rs 453.95 / Rs 41.40. Not verified: members' claims that BIL keeps wind-energy and real-estate businesses and a land parcel of about Rs 26 cr book value - no filing read this session says what remains in BIL. Tieramet's listing date is unknown.

updates.title: Guidance line filled from the Q1 FY27 call (now Tieramet's business)
updates.body: Read in the 28-Jul-2026 transcript this session: MD Devendra Surana - 'we should be looking at between 12% to 15% growth in terms of volume for the whole year now' (lowered from 15-20% because of April-May scrap-sourcing loss); 'Initially, we were taking around 1,300 rupees as the average price for the year, which should be exceeded'; EBITDA margin 'between 5% and 5.5%' with 5.5% for the whole year 'a little difficult'; 15% volume growth from next year; 35,000 to 45,000 tonnes 'not for this year'. These are the card's model inputs. Since the 8-Oct record date the copper business sits in Tieramet, so the guidance applies to the unlisted Tieramet share each BIL holder received.

ideas.name: Bharat Seats Ltd
ideas.trigger: filing: RATING - ICRA upgraded Bharat Seats' long-term rating to [ICRA]A+ (Stable) from [ICRA]A (Stable) on 24-Sep-2026 and raised the rated amount from Rs 134.32 cr to Rs 188.96 cr (intimation filed 25-Sep-2026 13:08 IST under Reg 30(6)). The rationale carries the numbers that make it an idea rather than a credit event: FY2026 operating income Rs 1,951.0 cr, up 51% on FY2025's Rs 1,288.8 cr, and ICRA's stated expectation that revenue growth 'remain[s] strong at 30-35% in FY2027'.
ideas.thesis:
**What the business physically does.** Bharat Seats Ltd (BSL), incorporated 1986, assembles car seat sets, moulded floor carpets and extrusion components for vehicle roofs, plus two-wheeler seats and — since January 2025 — two-wheeler wheel assemblies. The physical unit that drives revenue is a seat set (or a wheel assembly) shipped to one of two customers. Plants: Gurgaon, Manesar, Kharkhoda and Bhorakalan in Haryana; Surendra Nagar and Hansalpur in Gujarat. Revenue is **entirely domestic** — no exports.

**The customer position, which is the whole business.** ICRA's rationale states BSL is **one of only two suppliers of car seat sets to Maruti Suzuki India Ltd (MSIL)** and currently caters to **about one-third of MSIL's seat-set requirement**; and it is the **sole supplier of 2W seats to Suzuki Motorcycle India Pvt Ltd (SMIPL)** for most of SMIPL's models. FY2026 revenue mix, as ICRA states it:

| division | share of FY2026 revenue |
|---|---|
| car seat assembly (MSIL) | 70% |
| 2W wheel assembly (SMIPL) | 16% |
| motorcycle seats (SMIPL) | 4% |
| carpet sets | 5% |
| extrusion components for roofs and other | balance |

So roughly **90% of revenue comes from two Suzuki-group customers**, both of which are also shareholders (see Ownership). ICRA names this concentration as the rating's principal constraint.

**What changed, and why it is a growth trigger rather than a credit note.** Three things in the rationale, each with a number:

1. **FY2026 revenue grew 51%** (Rs 1,288.8 cr to Rs 1,951.0 cr). The driver ICRA gives is not volume but **content per vehicle**: car seat sales to MSIL grew 33% on premiumisation — seat-mounted airbags, powered seats, better fabric — while MSIL's own volumes did not grow at that rate. Car seats are 70% of revenue.
2. **The wheel-assembly line went from Rs 55 cr (FY2025) to Rs 321 cr (FY2026)**, 16% of revenue in its first full year. And **from April 2026 BSL is SMIPL's only vendor for 2W wheel assembly** — ICRA expects "a sharp growth in revenue from the segment in FY2027". This is the single largest identified source of FY2027 growth.
3. **Five new MSIL models won**, with start-of-production dates scheduled between FY2027 and FY2029, on which ICRA expects BSL's share of business with MSIL to "steadily improve over the medium term".

**The rating trajectory is itself the evidence.** ICRA's own three-year history table in the same document: [ICRA]A- on 20-May-2023, [ICRA]A- on 23-Apr-2024, **[ICRA]A on 30-Jun-2025, [ICRA]A+ on 24-Sep-2026** — two notches in fifteen months, on a company whose debt/OPBDIT fell from 2.0x to 1.1x and interest cover rose from 8.5x to 9.8x over the same period. A bank-vetted, twice-upgraded credit profile is the playbook's "positive signal of vetted revenue" in its strongest form.

**An independent check on the rating report.** ICRA's audited FY2026 figures are Rs 1,951.0 cr of operating income and Rs 42.2 cr of PAT. Summing the four standalone quarters to March 2026 from this repo's `docs/quarterly_results.json` (built from the companies' own BSE results filings) gives **Rs 1,950.9 cr of revenue and Rs 42.2 cr of PAT** — a match to the decimal on PAT and to 0.1 cr on revenue. The rating report and the exchange filings are telling the same story, which is not something one can assume.

**What has not happened is the stock.** On the BSE bhavcopy for 2026-09-25 BSL closed at Rs 213.95, **down 1.9% on the day the upgrade was filed**, down 3.4% over 20 days, and **15.9% below its 65-day high of Rs 254.50**. Volume was **0.3x the 60-day median** — there was no reaction at all. The 2026-09-22 study (runbook 144b) is explicit that this is not a negative: a volume explosion accompanied 81% of 5x runs and 78% of the stocks that went nowhere, so its absence carries no information either way. Median daily turnover is Rs 52.8 lakh, comfortably above the Rs 25 lakh floor the playbook uses.
ideas.model:
**The physical driver.** Revenue = seat sets (and wheel assemblies) shipped x realisation per unit. BSL discloses neither unit volumes nor realisation, so the model is built on the two things it and ICRA do disclose: the segment mix and the growth rate.

**Measured run-rate, from the BSE-filed quarterlies** (`docs/quarterly_results.json`, standalone, Rs cr):

| quarter | revenue | operating profit | PAT | filed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) | 577.83 | 28.19 | 13.21 | 2026-08-04 |
| Q4 FY26 (Mar-26) | 574.28 | 29.66 | 13.25 | 2026-05-06 |
| Q3 FY26 (Dec-25) | 491.01 | 25.13 | 9.90 | 2026-02-03 |
| Q2 FY26 (Sep-25) | 458.60 | 22.64 | 9.90 | 2025-11-05 |
| Q1 FY26 (Jun-25) | 427.06 | 21.72 | 9.18 | 2025-07-29 |

Q1 FY27 against Q1 FY26: **revenue +35.3%, operating profit +29.8%, PAT +43.9%**. That lands at the **top** of ICRA's 30-35% FY2027 range, which means the range is being met by the one quarter already reported, not merely forecast. Trailing twelve months (Sep-25 to Jun-26): revenue Rs 2,101.7 cr, operating profit Rs 105.6 cr (5.02%), PAT Rs 46.3 cr.

**FY2027 arithmetic.** Base = FY2026 operating income Rs 1,951.0 cr (ICRA audited).

| FY27 revenue growth | FY27 revenue | PAT at 2.0% of OI | PAT at 2.2% of OI |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30% (ICRA low) | Rs 2,536 cr | Rs 50.7 cr | Rs 55.8 cr |
| 35% (ICRA high) | Rs 2,634 cr | Rs 52.7 cr | Rs 57.9 cr |

The 2.0-2.2% PAT-to-revenue band is justified by the last two audited years (FY2025 2.5%, FY2026 2.2%) and by ICRA's explicit statement that margins "are likely to be range-bound in the near term as higher share of low margin 2W wheel assembly segment is likely to offset improved operating leverage from increased scale." Taking the margin **above** 2.2% would be arguing against the rating agency; this model does not.

**Cross-check by annualising the quarter actually reported:** Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 13.21 cr x 4 = Rs 52.8 cr, inside the table's Rs 50.7-57.9 cr range and close to its middle. Two independent routes to roughly the same FY2027 PAT.

**Share count.** This repo's universe file puts BSL's market cap at Rs 1,382.9 cr as of 2026-09-23, when the BSE close was Rs 220.20 — implying **6.2802 cr shares**. At the 2026-09-25 close of Rs 213.95 that is a market cap of **Rs 1,343.6 cr**. (The same method applied to Harrisons Malayalam reproduces its annual report's 1.84554 cr paid-up shares exactly, which is why it is trusted here.)

**EPS and forward PE at Rs 213.95:**

| case | PAT | EPS | PE |
|---|---|---|---|
| trailing twelve months | Rs 46.3 cr | Rs 7.37 | **29.0x** |
| FY27 at 30% growth, 2.0% margin | Rs 50.7 cr | Rs 8.08 | **26.5x** |
| FY27 at 35% growth, 2.2% margin | Rs 57.9 cr | Rs 9.23 | **23.2x** |
| Q1 FY27 annualised | Rs 52.8 cr | Rs 8.41 | **25.4x** |

**Where this model could differ from management.** BSL has issued no guidance this run could read; ICRA's 30-35% is the only forward number in evidence, and it is the rating agency's estimate, not the company's. No investor presentation or concall transcript was available (see Unknowns).
ideas.valuation:
**Peers, computed this run** — trailing twelve-month standalone revenue, operating profit and PAT summed from `docs/quarterly_results.json`, closes from the BSE bhavcopy of 2026-09-25, share counts derived as market cap / close. BSL's comparables are not the high-margin ancillaries but the thin-margin, high-volume OEM suppliers:

| company | mcap (Rs cr) | TTM revenue | PAT margin | trailing PE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bharat Seats** | **1,344** | **Rs 2,102 cr** | **2.2%** | **29.0x** |
| JBM Auto | 14,244 | Rs 5,523 cr | 2.7% | 96.4x |
| Minda Corp | 16,520 | Rs 5,283 cr | 4.9% | 63.3x |
| JTEKT India | 3,333 | Rs 2,818 cr | 2.6% | 46.1x |
| TVS Srichakra | 3,573 | Rs 3,625 cr | 2.6% | 38.1x |
| Wheels India | 5,468 | Rs 5,296 cr | 2.8% | 36.7x |
| NDR Auto Components | 1,812 | Rs 861 cr | 6.6% | 32.0x |
| Lumax Industries | 5,475 | Rs 4,485 cr | 3.9% | 31.6x |
| Rane (Madras) | 3,759 | Rs 4,024 cr | 3.1% | 30.1x |
| Steel Strips Wheels | 5,863 | Rs 5,506 cr | 4.1% | 26.2x |

NDR Auto Components is listed deliberately: it is BSL's own 28.6% shareholder and a fellow Relan-group auto-component maker, and it trades at 32.0x on a smaller revenue base.

**The re-rating case, in one sentence.** Bharat Seats trades at 23-27x FY2027 earnings against a cohort of similarly thin-margin OEM suppliers at 26-46x trailing, while it is the only one in that list growing revenue at 35% with a two-notch credit upgrade behind it and a sole-vendor franchise starting this financial year.

**What argues against it.** At 29.0x trailing the stock is not cheap in absolute terms, and the whole peer cohort may simply be expensive together. A 2.2% net margin means the earnings are a small residual on a large revenue line: a 1 percentage-point move in raw-material cost that is not passed through would take roughly half of PAT. ICRA states pass-through clauses exist with customers but with a **lag of a quarter**, so a sharp input-cost move shows up in one quarter's numbers before it is recovered.

**Market-cap band.** At Rs 1,343.6 cr, BSL sits inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where the 2026-09-22 study found the odds of a 5x run peak, and far below the Rs 25,000 cr level above which nothing produced a 5x run in three years (runbook 144b).
ideas.red_flags:
Each item answered, with "not read" where the document was unavailable this run.

- **Customer concentration — the largest flag, and it is structural.** About 90% of FY2026 revenue came from MSIL (70%) and SMIPL (20% across seats and wheel assembly). ICRA writes that the ratings "continue to be constrained by the company's high dependence on the domestic market and MSIL". There is no export revenue and no third large customer.
- **Related-party purchases and sales.** The two dominant customers are also shareholders: MSIL 14.8% and Suzuki Motor Corporation 14.8% as of 30-Jun-2026 (ICRA). Nearly all revenue is therefore related-party revenue by construction. The annual report's related-party note was **not read this run** — it was filed outside the 31-day window of the NSE feed this run can reach, and BSE's announcement list is blocked (see Unknowns). ICRA states raw-material pass-through clauses exist with a one-quarter lag; how seat prices themselves are set is **unknown**.
- **Margins falling while revenue rises.** OPBDIT/operating income fell from 5.9% (FY2025) to 5.1% (FY2026); PAT/operating income from 2.5% to 2.2%. ICRA attributes this to the higher share of the low-margin wheel-assembly business. Revenue grew 51% and PAT only 29%. This is growth bought at a lower margin, not operating leverage.
- **Capex funding not fully tied up.** Rs 130-140 cr of capex at Kharkhoda (Haryana) and Naviyani (Gujarat), largely to be spent in FY2027, is to be funded by Rs 65 cr of debt plus internal accruals — and ICRA's own Annexure I footnotes Term Loan-III of Rs 65.00 cr as **"yet to be sanctioned"**. Against that: expected FY2027 retained cash flows of Rs 105-125 cr, debt repayments of only Rs 13-14 cr, and an unused working-capital buffer of Rs 35.2 cr at 31-Mar-2026. ICRA calls liquidity "Adequate".
- **Dilution.** None visible: promoter-group holding is 74.66% and has not moved across the six quarters to June 2026 in `docs/shareholding.json`. No preferential issue, warrant or QIP seen this run.
- **Pledge.** **Not read** — the pledge disclosure sits behind BSE's blocked api. Unknown.
- **Auditor remarks or auditor change.** **Not read** — same reason. Unknown.
- **Promoter salary versus profit.** **Not read.** Unknown.
- **Revenue claims that shipments do not support.** Not applicable in the usual sense: the revenue is not claimed but audited, and two independent sources (ICRA's audited table and the sum of the BSE quarterly filings) agree on it.
- **GST or other regulatory notices.** None seen in the NSE filing feed for BSL over 2026-08-26 to 2026-09-25. Beyond that window, unknown.
- **One-off items.** None flagged by ICRA, and the quarterly PAT series (Rs 9.18 / 9.90 / 9.90 / 13.25 / 13.21 cr) rises smoothly with no jump that would suggest an exceptional gain.
- **No institutional ownership.** FII 0.15%, DII 0.22%, mutual funds 0.003% as of 30-Jun-2026, across 30,200 shareholders. Nobody with a research department has taken a position — which cuts both ways, and means there is no institutional work to lean on.
ideas.verify:
The facts that only a site visit, a dealer or customer call, or a paid dataset could confirm:

1. **The share-of-business claim.** ICRA states BSL supplies "around one-third" of MSIL's seat-set requirement and is one of two suppliers. Confirming that, and whether the share is rising, needs MSIL vendor-side contact or a supply-chain dataset; it is the single number the FY2027 case rests on.
2. **The SMIPL sole-vendor status from April 2026.** ICRA states that from April 2026 BSL is SMIPL's only 2W wheel-assembly vendor. No contract is public. Whether it is exclusive by agreement or by current practice, and for how long, needs a customer call.
3. **Start-of-production timing on the five new MSIL models** (scheduled FY2027-FY2029). Slippage moves the revenue into later years; only MSIL's launch calendar and the plant's own tooling schedule show it.
4. **The capex ramp at Kharkhoda and Naviyani.** EPFO head-count at those two establishments would lead revenue by one to two quarters (the playbook's own constant). That data is captcha-gated and is not automated in this repo.
5. **Whether the Rs 65 cr term loan gets sanctioned.** ICRA records it as not yet sanctioned; the next credit update or a borrowing disclosure will say.
ideas.unknowns:
- **Q2 FY27 results.** Not yet filed; `docs/quarterly_results.json` predicts 2026-11-05.
- **Every document other than the rating report and the exchange intimation.** No investor presentation, concall transcript, annual report or shareholding-pattern PDF could be opened for BSL this run. `api.bseindia.com` returned HTTP 403 from this sandbox **and** from GitHub Actions (recorded in `docs/ideas/feeds_status.json`), and `dossier.py` crashed on that endpoint, so the usual dossier — BSE header, PE, detailed results, corporate actions, 240-day filing list, annual reports — does not exist for this name today. The annual report is also outside the 31-day window of the NSE feed. So: **no concall, no investor deck, no annual report was read.**
- **Consolidated accounts.** ICRA rates the standalone entity and states no entities were consolidated; `docs/quarterly_results.json` carries only standalone figures for BSL's recent quarters. Whether any subsidiary or associate is material is unknown.
- **Segment-level margins.** ICRA says wheel assembly runs at "relatively lower margins" than seats but gives no figure, so the mix effect on FY2027 margin cannot be quantified — only bounded by the 2.0-2.2% company-level band used above.
- **Volumes and realisation per seat set.** Never disclosed. The model is therefore a growth-rate model, not a true unit model.
- **Order book or committed volumes from MSIL.** Not disclosed; OEM supply runs on schedules, not order books.
- **Pledge, auditor remarks, promoter remuneration, related-party pricing.** All behind documents that could not be read today.
ideas.confidence: medium: the trigger is a rating agency's own upgraded rationale carrying an explicit FY2027 revenue-growth range, its audited FY2026 revenue and PAT match the sum of the company's BSE-filed quarterly results to the decimal, and the quarter already reported (Q1 FY27, +35.3% revenue, +43.9% PAT) is at the top of that range - so the growth is measured, not forecast. It is not high, for two reasons: about 90% of revenue rests on two Suzuki-group customers on a 2.2% net margin, and the documents that would settle related-party pricing, pledge, auditor remarks and promoter remuneration could not be read because api.bseindia.com was blocked from both the sandbox and GitHub Actions today.

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying.** There is one dedicated thread. It is old and thin: 18 posts over eleven years, from 7-Nov-2014 to the last post on 5-Nov-2025. Nobody has posted in almost eleven months, and **no one has discussed the 24-Sep-2026 ICRA upgrade, the FY26 jump in revenue, or the wheel-assembly ramp**. The early posts (2014-2020) debate a commoditised seat maker tied to Maruti and compare it with Harita Seating. The 2025 posts bring up three things: a Rs 3,000 cr revenue "vision" mentioned on NDR Auto's call, the new wheel-and-tyre assembly business, and the income-tax search note. The tone is neutral to mildly positive, with little analysis. Three broad threads mention the company, mainly through its promoter NDR Auto and the 2023 income-tax searches.
