ideas.name: Utssav CZ Gold Jewels Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — NSE Emerge B2B maker of lightweight CZ gold jewellery; FY26 revenue +78.7% / PAT +136%, but volume grew only ~11–19%; stock at an all-time high ₹722.10 (+296% in a year) after an NSE price-movement query on 17-Sep-2026
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Mumbai workshop that makes lightweight 18K/20K/22K gold jewellery set with cubic zirconia (CZ) — about 10 grams a piece — and sells it only to other businesses: big jewellers like Kalyan, Lalithaa, TBZ and Joyalukkas (~30% of sales) and distributors and small retailers (~70%). It is now adding plain gold and diamond pieces.
- **Headline growth looks huge:** FY26 revenue ₹1,155 cr (+79%), profit ₹59 cr (+136%).
- **But most of it is the gold price, not more jewellery.** Kilograms sold grew only about 11% (company) or 19% (CARE Ratings); the price of each kilo rose 50–61%. Gold itself rose ~59% on MCX over the year.
- **Cash goes out, borrowed money comes in:** operating cash flow was −₹89 cr in FY25 and −₹61 cr in FY26. Borrowings went from ₹73 cr to ₹186 cr in two years; its bank lines are ~96% used.
- **Unhedged gold:** about 150 kg (₹158 cr) of stock is not hedged — a 10% fall in gold would cost about ₹16 cr, roughly a quarter of FY26 profit.
- **Same owners as Shanti Gold:** the promoters also control listed Shanti Gold International, which guaranteed Utssav's bank loans; the MD denied promoter loans on a call while the filings showed ₹2.8 cr owed to him.
- **Price:** ₹722 is an all-time high, +296% in a year and 4x in six months; NSE queried the move on 17-Sep. 30.6x earnings — about twice Shanti Gold's 16.0x (restated trailing).

### 1. What the company is
- Incorporated 2007; listed on NSE Emerge (SME) on 7-Aug-2024; NSE-only; symbol UTSSAV, ISIN INE06IJ01010.
- One site: Andheri (E), Mumbai, 8,275 sq ft (corporate office + 2 production units), adding ~5,600 sq ft. About 130 staff (employee cost only ₹4.35 cr, 0.38% of sales).
- Promoters (Jagawat family): Pankajkumar H. Jagawat (MD, 62.2% after warrant conversion), Shashank B. Jagawat (WTD), Rakesh S. Jagawat (CFO); promoter group includes Shanti Gold International, Uzuri Jewels, Ganesh Gold, Sanskriti Gold, Shanti Developers.
- Auditor Jain V. & Co. (unmodified opinions FY24–FY26; no change). CEO Harpreet Singh Guleria since Apr-2024.
- Reach: 23 states + 2 UTs, 430+ touch points, 112 new clients in FY26. Exports ~1% of FY26 sales (UAE hub).
- New: Indian subsidiary Utssav Gold and Diamond (Jul-2026); a UAE subsidiary approved Feb-2026 (incorporation not confirmed).

**Capacity — stated four different ways**

| Source | Installed capacity | Utilisation |
|---|---:|---:|
| IPO documents / CARE Sep-2025 | 1,500 kg/yr | — |
| May-2026 presentation (p.4–5) | 2,000 kg | ~65% (FY26) |
| May-2026 presentation (p.10) | 1,500 kg | — |
| MD on May-2026 call | 2,500 kg | ~65% (up to 90% in season) |

- Target 6–7 tonnes a year through new buildings; FY27 capex ≈ ₹50 cr.

### 2. Growth — gold price vs kilograms
| ₹ cr | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 340.20 | 646.32 | **1,154.90** |
| Revenue growth | — | +90.0% | +78.7% |
| Gross margin | 7.63% | 7.16% | 8.86% |
| EBITDA (ex other income) | 21.25 | 38.99 | 91.14 |
| EBITDA margin | 6.25% | 6.03% | 7.89% |
| Profit after tax | 12.85 | 25.06 | **59.06** |
| PAT margin | 3.78% | 3.88% | 5.11% |

| Period | Revenue growth | Volume growth | Implied price per kg |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY25 | +90% | +42% (CARE) | ≈ +34% |
| H1 FY26 | +67% | +25% (MD) | ≈ +34% |
| FY26 (company figure) | +78.7% | ≈ +11% | ≈ +61% |
| FY26 (CARE figure) | +78.7% | ≈ +19% | ≈ +50% |

- The company's and CARE's FY26 volume figures conflict. On the company's 11%, H2 FY26 kilograms were roughly flat to slightly down year on year (our derivation).

**Half-years (₹ cr)**

| | H1 FY25 | H2 FY25 | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 284.53 | 361.79 | 475.41 | 679.49 |
| Gross margin | 6.32% | 7.82% | **10.19%** | 7.93% |
| EBITDA margin | 5.40% | 6.53% | **9.25%** | 6.94% |
| Profit after tax | 9.87 | 15.19 | 29.42 | 29.64 |

- The H1 FY26 margin spike included inventory gains on rising gold (MD: 0.5–1 point; CARE also cites them); H2 fell back to 6.9%. CARE expects EBITDA margin to normalise to ~6%; management guides 7–8%.

### 3. Cash and balance sheet — the weak spot
| ₹ cr, 31-Mar | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net worth | 35.22 | 126.79 | 197.89 |
| Borrowings | 72.89 | 130.34 | **186.23** |
| Cash and bank | 24.57 | 56.26 | 51.57 |
| Inventory | 21.73 | 84.09 | **157.55** |
| Receivables | 56.81 | 109.23 | 171.05 |
| Operating cash flow | +6.82 | **−89.17** | **−60.72** |
| Capex | 2.98 | 4.41 | 1.68 |

- Free cash flow FY25 + FY26 ≈ −₹156 cr against ₹84 cr of profit. Funded by the IPO (₹66.5 cr net), warrant money (₹26 cr) and short-term bank debt (+₹117 cr over two years).
- Net debt ₹134.7 cr at Mar-26; gearing 0.95x; working-capital cycle 71 → 76 → 84 days (CARE). Inventory ≈ 150 kg at Mar-26 (MD).
- Bank lines: Saraswat Bank ₹197 cr + Yes Bank ₹50 cr cash credit; ₹15 cr ICICI gold metal loan approved. CARE rating upgraded to BBB+ (Stable) / A3+ in Aug-2026.

### 4. Future scope
- Management guides FY27 revenue +60% with a 4–4.5% PAT margin and 35–40% volume growth; new plain-gold and diamond lines (target >₹200 cr in two years; ~2–3.5% of revenue today).
- **Industry:** India's 2025 jewellery demand fell 24% in tonnes but hit a record ~$49 bn in value; Q2 2026 jewellery volume −15%, value +34% (WGC). Buyers are shifting to lighter, lower-carat and studded pieces — Utssav's niche. But import duty went back up from 6% to 15% in 2026 and WGC expects demand to fall a further ~10%, with small retailers — ~70% of Utssav's sales — "most vulnerable".
- Mandatory HUID hallmarking (380 districts from Mar-2026) favours organised makers; Utssav hallmarks in-house.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Lightweight CZ jewellery is where Indian demand is moving | Growth is mostly gold price; FY26 volume +11–19% only |
| Blue-chip jeweller customers; 112 new clients in FY26 | Operating cash flow −₹150 cr over two years; bank lines ~96% used |
| ROE ≈ 36%; CARE upgrade to BBB+ | ~150 kg of unhedged gold; 15% import duty hurting small retailers |
| Diamond and plain-gold lines, 6–7 t capacity plan | Common promoters with Shanti Gold; disclosure gaps; 30.6x P/E at an all-time high after an NSE query |

Board meeting of 28-Sep-2026 approved expanding the gold-jewellery manufacturing, plain-casting and office facility.

| Item (Annexure I of the filing) | Value |
|---|---|
| Existing capacity | 1,500 kg per annum |

What it means against the card: the company itself states the current 1,500 kg line runs at 50% — i.e. ≈750 kg/yr — which matches the card's finding that volume grew only ~11–19% while revenue grew 79%. Adding 2,000 kg (2.3x today's capacity) when half the existing capacity is idle is a statement of intent for the 35–40% FY27 volume guidance, not evidence of demand; it will be judged by the kilograms sold in H1 FY27 (results due by mid-Nov-2026). The spend (₹10 cr) is small against FY26 PAT of ₹59 cr but comes on top of bank lines the card measured at ~96% used.

ideas.name: Shanti Gold International Ltd
ideas.trigger: deep-dive on request — main-board B2B maker of 22KT CZ gold jewellery; FY26 revenue +82% (≈+15% kilograms × ≈+58% gold price); inventory accounting changed and quarters restated May-2026; stock at an all-time high ₹325.68 (+14.8% on 25-Sep) on an HFT-heavy, 9%-delivery volume spike
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Mumbai company (since 2003) that makes 22-carat gold jewellery set with cubic zirconia — bangles, rings, necklaces, bridal sets — and sells it only to jewellers and wholesalers (Joyalukkas, Lalithaa, Alukkas, Kalyan and 400+ others). Listed on the main board (NSE + BSE) in Aug-2025.
- **Headline growth:** FY26 revenue ₹2,019 cr (+82%), profit ₹140 cr (+159%). But kilograms sold grew only ~15% (1,518 → 1,748 kg); the rest is the gold price, which rose ~58% in rupees. Revenue per gram tracks the gold price almost one for one.
- **Profit was helped by holding unhedged gold while prices rose.** Management's own "core" margin is 3.5–4% PAT; FY26 was 6.9%. On that core margin, roughly 40–50% of FY26 profit came from gold-price gains (our arithmetic).
- **The accounts changed mid-stream:** in May-2026 it switched inventory costing from FIFO to weighted-average, restated back to Apr-2024. FY26 profit on the new method is ₹140 cr; on the old method it would have been ₹193 cr. Quarterly figures published earlier were restated (Q2 FY26 PAT ₹43.8 cr → ₹26.0 cr).
- **Cash goes out fast:** operating cash flow −₹261 cr in FY26. It raised ₹360 cr in the Aug-2025 IPO and another ₹100 cr in an Aug-2026 rights issue (promoters did not subscribe), and is seeking a ₹2,000 cr borrowing limit.
- **Governance points:** the same promoters control listed rival Utssav CZ Gold Jewels (a promoter sits on its board and it guaranteed Utssav's bank loans); surplus cash went into listed shares, including a customer (Lalithaa) and a steel company (Ratnaveer).
- **Price:** ₹325.68 is an all-time high after +30% in a week on HFT-dominated volume with only 9% delivery and no company news. 16x trailing (restated) earnings — cheaper than Utssav (30.6x) but the gold-gain share of profit matters.

### 1. What the company is
- Main board, listed 01-Aug-2025 on NSE (SHANTIGOLD) and BSE (544459); ISIN INE06ZD01017. Partnership from 2003; public limited company since 2013.
- Promoters: Pankajkumar H. Jagawat (Chairman & MD), Manojkumar N. Jain (WTD), Shashank B. Jagawat (non-executive; also a whole-time director of Utssav CZ Gold Jewels). Auditor J. Kala & Associates (no change). CARE A- (Stable) / A2+ (Jan-2026). 286 employees.
- Subsidiary: Shanti Gold Jewellery Trading LLC, Dubai (incorporated May-2026; awaiting RBI approval; no operations to Jun-2026).
- New lines: machine-made plain gold, Mangalsutra, Turkish jewellery, Cuban bracelets.

**FY26 revenue by purity (₹ cr)**

| Purity | FY26 | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| 22KT | 1,871.3 | 92.7% |
| 18KT | 85.4 | 4.2% |
| 24KT | 50.4 | 2.5% |
| Other | 11.2 | 0.6% |

**Customer concentration (share of revenue)**

| | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Top 1 | 8.92% | 7.32% | 7.98% |
| Top 5 | 24.14% | 23.29% | 30.46% |
| Top 10 | 36.43% | 34.49% | **44.82%** |

- South India fell from 72.8% of revenue (FY25) to 44.6% (FY26); the ~₹1,036 cr sold elsewhere has no state split disclosed. Exports ₹82.9 cr (4.1%).

**Capacity**

| Plant | Capacity (kg/yr) | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| Andheri, Mumbai | 2,700 | running (68% in Jan-2026) |
| Marol, Mumbai | 4,000 | production from 08-Jun-2026 (₹8.5 cr capex) |
| Jaipur (plain gold) | 1,200 | under construction; now expected Nov–Dec 2026 (delayed) |
| **Total planned** | **7,900** | |

- FY26 sold 1,747.8 kg (≈65% of 2,700 kg). FY27 guidance of +30–40% volume would use only ~34–37% of the 6,700 kg running base (our arithmetic).

### 2. Growth — kilograms vs gold price
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 (restated) | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 679.4 | 711.4 | 1,106.4 | **2,018.7** |
| EBITDA | 42.7 | 49.9 | 89.9 | 199.0 |
| EBITDA margin | 6.3% | 7.0% | 8.1% | 9.9% |
| Profit after tax | 19.8 | 26.9 | 54.1 | **140.15** |
| PAT margin | 2.9% | 3.8% | 4.9% | 6.9% |

| | FY25 | FY26 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kilograms sold | 1,517.5 | 1,747.8 | +15.2% |
| Revenue per gram | ₹7,291 | ₹11,550 | +58.4% |
| International gold, ₹ per 10 g (avg) | 71,836 | 113,813 | +58.4% |

- FY26 growth ≈ +15% volume × +58% price. Revenue per gram tracks the 24K international gold price at 0.975–1.008x each quarter (our derivation).

**Quarters (₹ cr; FY26 restated to weighted-average cost)**

| | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY27 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 292.78 | 430.08 | 636.92 | 658.93 | **716.38** |
| Kilograms | 323 | 427 | 535 | 463 | 522.1 |
| Profit after tax | 34.36 | 26.00 | 27.87 (derived) | 51.93 | **50.48** |
| PAT as first published (FIFO) | 24.64 | 43.82 | — | — | — |

- Q1 FY27: revenue +144.7%, volume +61.6%, PAT +46.9% y/y; EBITDA margin 9.97%, of which management attributes 2–2.5 points to inventory gains.

### 3. Cash and balance sheet — the weak spot
| ₹ cr, 31-Mar | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inventory | 133.9 | 347.5 |
| Receivables | 181.6 | 362.9 |
| Borrowings | 233.0 | 205.6 |
| Cash + other bank balances | — | 49.2 |
| Net worth | 137.7 | 598.4 |
| Operating cash flow | −15.3 | **−260.6** |
| Capex | — | 6.3 |

- Inventory days 65 → 49 → 70 and receivable days 40 → 60 → 66 (FY24→FY26, year-end). No expected-credit-loss provision on ₹363 cr of receivables. Finished goods ₹320 cr but work-in-progress nil — unusual for a manufacturer.
- FY26 cash flow appears to add interest and rent income inside operating cash flow and deduct them again in investing (FY25 was presented correctly); corrected CFO ≈ −₹272 cr (our arithmetic).
- Working-capital gap ₹742 cr in FY26, projected ₹1,159 cr for FY27 (rights letter of offer). Borrowing limit being raised to ₹2,000 cr (AGM 28-Sep-2026).

### 4. Future scope
- Guidance: FY27 revenue ≈ ₹3,500 cr, volume +30–40%, core EBITDA margin 7.5–8% and core PAT 3.5–4%. Marol (+4,000 kg) is running; Jaipur plain gold due Nov–Dec 2026; Dubai trading arm pending RBI approval.
- **Industry:** Indian jewellery tonnage is falling (Q1 2026 −19%, Q2 −15%) while value rises (Q1 +47%). Buyers shift to lighter, lower-carat and studded pieces (good for CZ). Import duty rose from 6% to 15% on 13-May-2026; WGC expects 2026 demand −50–60 t (~10%). Organised share projected to rise from 35% (CY23) to ~60% by CY29; HUID hallmarking now covers 392 districts.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Real volume growth (+15% FY26, +62% Q1 FY27) with new Marol capacity | Most of FY26's growth and much of its margin came from the gold price |
| 400+ organised-jeweller customers; organised share rising | Accounting method changed and quarters restated; a cash-flow sign error |
| 16x trailing earnings, below Utssav (30.6x) and Sky Gold (36.7x) | Operating cash flow −₹261 cr; two equity raises in 13 months; ₹2,000 cr borrowing limit |
| ROE 38%, CARE A- | Common promoters with rival Utssav; cash put into a customer's and a steel company's shares; HFT-driven all-time high |

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying**
There is one young dedicated thread, "Shanti Gold- Sky Gold in making?", started on 30-Aug-2026: 6 posts, last post 28-Sep-2026, about 1,100 views. The opening post by Chandan_Sharma is a long, balanced write-up (business, promoters, Q1 FY27 call, risks) with a disclosed small holding. The same author posted a shorter version in his own journal thread. Replies are brief. They note that a key customer (Lalithaa) got only a token investment, and they ask why Shanti Gold and Utssav CZ share promoters and why Shanti Gold bought Ratnaveer shares (unanswered). The main debate is fast growth and capacity additions against cash-hungry working capital and the overlap with the sister company Utssav. Nobody on the forum discusses the May-2026 FIFO-to-weighted-average restatement.

### Threads
| Thread | Kind | Posts | Active | Link |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Shanti Gold- Sky Gold in making? | dedicated | 6 | 30-Aug-2026 to 28-Sep-2026 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/shanti-gold-sky-gold-in-making/224020) |
| Building on my mistakes – journaling my investing journey (posts #39, #40) | mention | 44 | 27–30 Aug-2026 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/building-on-my-mistakes-jornaling-my-investing-journey/219542) |

### Points members raise
| Bull case raised | Bear case raised |
|---|---|
| New Marol plant (+4,000 kg) and Jaipur (+1,200 kg) give room to grow; 400+ new designs a month | Working-capital heavy; cash flow negative and funded by fresh equity (₹100 cr rights) |
| 400+ customers, the largest only 7–8% of sales | Top-10 customers already 44.8% of FY26 revenue |
| Management guides 50–60% value and 30–40% volume growth for FY27 | Guided margins (7.5–8% EBITDA, ~4% PAT) are below FY26's, which gold gains lifted |
| Organised retail and outsourcing of manufacturing are structural tailwinds | No brand and little pricing power; gold-price swings |
| — | Same promoters run listed Utssav CZ; Raj7800 asks why, IndyaInvestor asks why Shanti bought Ratnaveer shares |

### New verified data from the forum
| Data point | Primary source that confirms it |
|---|---|
| **Promoter pay raised 66%.** MD Pankajkumar Jagawat and WTD Manojkumar Jain each go from ₹1,08,30,000 to **₹1,80,30,000 a year** from 01-Feb-2026 (basic ₹90 lakh, HRA ₹45 lakh, LTA ₹18 lakh and other items). Shareholders approved it by postal ballot on 25-Apr-2026. FY26 pay actually drawn was ₹1,20,30,000 each (+11.08%), 49.4x the median employee. This answers a gap the card listed as unknown | Postal-ballot notice, 24-Mar-2026 (explanatory statement); postal-ballot outcome, 25-Apr-2026; FY26 annual report (directors' report and remuneration annexure) |
| Mumbai (Andheri) plant utilisation "currently 75%" at the Q1 FY27 call, above the card's 68% (Jan-2026). Jaipur capex put at ~₹47 cr, with start-up expected mid-Nov to Dec-2026 | Q1 FY27 earnings-call transcript (call 14-Aug-2026, filed 20-Aug-2026) |
| Management said the growth rate should hold "for the next three, four years" (its FY27 guide is 50–60% value and 30–40% volume growth) | Same transcript |
| 61 CAD designers producing over 400 designs a month (at 30-Sep-2025) | Q2 FY26 earnings-call transcript (Nov-2025) |
| **Management said Utssav has "a completely different management"; the filings show otherwise.** Asked on the Q1 FY27 call why two group companies are listed, management said Utssav is run separately. But the same person (DIN 01843846), Pankajkumar Jagawat, is Managing Director of Utssav and Chairman & MD of Shanti Gold. Shashank Jagawat is a whole-time director of Utssav and a director of Shanti Gold | Q1 FY27 transcript; Utssav FY25 annual report (MD's letter, DIN 01843846); Shanti Gold FY26 annual report (director profile of Shashank Jagawat) |

### Claims on the forum not verified
- The promoters have no criminal cases against them — Chandan_Sharma — says he searched; no primary document reviewed this run covers it.
- The company website is "not secured" — Chandan_Sharma — a website check, not a filing matter; not tested.
- The FY27 forward valuation table in post #1 — Chandan_Sharma — it is an image of his own estimate, not a filed figure.

### Where the forum disagrees with the filings
- **IPO structure (journal post #40, Chandan_Sharma):** says the ₹360 cr IPO was entirely an offer for sale. The filings show it was **entirely a fresh issue** of 1,80,96,000 shares. His dedicated-thread version of the post says "fresh issue", so he corrected it there.
- **"Domestic sales contribute to 4%" (post #1):** on the Q1 FY27 call, management said **exports** were 4% of Q1 revenue. Domestic sales are about 96%.
- **"High degree of concentration in southern states" (post #1):** this is out of date. The FY26 annual report puts the South at 44.6% of revenue, down from 72.8% in FY25.
- **Promoters "each hold 37.43%" (post #1):** that was before the rights issue. The promoters did not take up their rights, and promoter-group holding fell from 74.89% to 70.35% (24-Aug-2026 shareholding).

The previous ₹1,000 cr limit dated from the 19-Jan-2024 EGM (annual-report explanatory statement). What this means for the card: the thesis measured FY26 operating cash flow at −₹261 cr with the business funded by the IPO (₹360 cr), the Aug-2026 rights issue (₹99.8 cr) and bank lines; a ₹2,000 cr ceiling is headroom, not debt drawn, but it is ≈1x FY26 revenue and the company's own guidance is ₹3,500 cr of revenue on 84+ day working-capital cycles. MD's AGM remarks (figures as stated): FY26 revenue ₹2,018 cr (+82.5% on ₹1,106 cr), EBITDA ₹199 cr (+121.3% on ₹89.92 cr), PAT ₹140.15 cr (+159% on ₹54.11 cr); the new Marol facility began commercial production in June 2026; Jaipur (Mahindra World City) is 'upcoming' — the card noted ₹38.99 cr of the ₹46.30 cr IPO-funded Jaipur capex still unspent at Jun-2026.

ideas.name: Shree Refrigerations Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME maker of air-conditioning and refrigeration systems for Indian Navy and Coast Guard ships; FY26 revenue +55.5% / PAT +65.6%; CARE upgrade to BBB- on 15-Sep-2026; stock +127% in six months to ₹407.60
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Karad (Maharashtra) company that designs and builds air-conditioning plants, refrigeration plants, chillers, air handlers and control panels for warships and Coast Guard vessels. Its customers are the Navy's shipyards and depots — Mazagon Dock, Garden Reach, Goa Shipyard, Hindustan Shipyard, Cochin Shipyard, Naval Dockyard Mumbai. It claims about 64% of naval HVAC&R.
- **Growth:** FY26 revenue ₹153.6 cr (+56%), profit ₹21.5 cr (+66%). Revenue has compounded about 45% a year since FY23.
- **But the order book is shrinking:** ₹327.6 cr at Sep-2025 → ₹270.8 cr at Mar-2026 (₹279.7 cr at Jun-2026, per CARE). Orders announced since April 2026 add up to only about ₹21 cr, against management's promise of ~40% annual growth.
- **Cash is slow:** the Navy's shipyards pay only after installation, so money is tied up for about a year (cash conversion ~368 days). Free cash flow was negative for three years running (FY26 −₹10.5 cr).
- **Governance points to check:** IPO spending rules widened the day before listing (to include residential property); 15% of the fresh issue went on issue costs; four family members on the board; ESOP shares issued at ₹2 face value; the cash-flow filing was revised twice.
- **Price:** ₹407.60 is 68x FY26 profit and 44x EBITDA — priced like a large defence stock for a ₹154 cr, one-customer-type business. An early backer (Maharashtra Defence & Aerospace Venture Fund) keeps selling.

### 1. What the company is
- BSE SME only (listed 01-Aug-2025): scrip 544458, symbol SHREEREF, ISIN INE0FMZ01045, face value ₹2. Registered office Karad, Satara.
- Products: AC plants 5–300 TR (including oil-free magnetic-bearing chillers), refrigeration plants 0.5–35 TR, self-contained and split ACs, air-handling and fan-coil units, turnkey ship HVAC&R, motor starter and control panels, heat exchangers, spares and service. Navy approvals from DME, DNA and DEE.
- Programmes cited (company claims): P17A Nilgiri frigates, P75 Scorpene AC indigenisation, Fleet Support Ships at HSL, Coast Guard FPVs at GSL and MDL, NGMV at CSL, NGOPV.
- Promoters: Ravalnath G. Shende (CMD, 35.0%), Rajashree R. Shende (ED, 9.56%), Devashree Nampurkar (WTD); Rucha R. Shende joined the board Feb-2026 — four family directors. CEO Abhijit Saoji; CFO Manoj Kothale. 152 permanent employees.
- Auditor SSSS & Associates, Karad (unmodified opinion; ₹11 lakh fee). Its partner shares a surname with the company secretary who resigned in Jan-2026 — any relationship is unknown.
- Subsidiaries: Trezor Technologies (no revenue; holds the Smardt data-centre chiller distribution deal; lends ₹2 cr to the parent) and Aquilon Deep Chill (approved Aug-2026). Danfoss Turbocor service partner since Mar-2026.

**FY26 closing order book by product (₹ cr)**

| Product | Order book | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| HVAC | 159.69 | 59.0% |
| AC plant | 61.66 | 22.8% |
| Refrigeration plant | 17.99 | 6.6% |
| Spares & services | 14.32 | 5.3% |
| Turnkey | 12.34 | 4.6% |
| Chiller & others | 4.76 | 1.8% |
| **Total** | **270.77** | |

**Order book over time**

| Date | Order book (₹ cr) | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| 01-Apr-2025 | 215.41 | company |
| 30-Sep-2025 | **327.57** | CARE |
| 31-Dec-2025 | 290.98 | company update |
| Feb-2026 | "more than 320" | press note — conflicts with the Mar-26 figure |
| 31-Mar-2026 | 270.77 | company |
| 30-Jun-2026 | 279.67 | CARE (1.82x FY26 income) |

- FY26 ties out: opening ₹215.41 cr + inflow ₹208.91 cr − executed ₹153.55 cr = ₹270.77 cr.
- Top three customers: ~88% (FY24) → ~73% (FY25) → ~69% (FY26) of income.

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 50.58 | 80.31 | 98.73 | **153.55** |
| Growth | — | +58.8% | +22.9% | +55.5% |
| Gross margin | — | 50.1% | 49.3% | 43.6% |
| EBITDA (ex other income) | 11.90 | 24.15 | 26.95 | 32.81 |
| EBITDA margin | 23.5% | 30.1% | 27.3% | **21.4%** |
| Profit after tax | 3.38 | 11.03 | 13.00 | **21.53** |

- Margins are falling as the high-margin spares share dropped from ~30% of revenue (FY25) to ~7% (FY26); management targets 15–20% spares and a 20–24% EBITDA margin.
- FY26 tax was only 13.8% of profit before tax.
- Restated FY25 in the prospectus (revenue ₹99.10 cr, PAT ₹13.55 cr) differs from the audited FY25 (₹98.73 cr, ₹13.00 cr).

**Half-years (consolidated, ₹ cr)**

| | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 50.39 | **103.16** |
| EBITDA margin | 11.2% | 26.3% |
| Profit after tax | 1.57 | **19.96** |
| PAT margin | 3.1% | 19.3% |

- The business is heavily second-half: H2 carried 93% of FY26 profit.

### 3. Cash and balance sheet — the weak spot
| ₹ cr | Mar-25 | Sep-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net worth | 118.2 | 196.19 | 215.86 |
| Receivables | 95.16 | 64.28 | 105.43 |
| Inventory | 47.40 | 49.58 | 54.77 |
| Payables | 17.06 | 8.61 | 27.02 |
| Borrowings | 46.9 | 24.19 | 37.46 |
| Cash | 5.93 | 17.08 | 57.66 |
| Current investments (FDs + MFs) | 3.50 | 50.01 | 5.15 |
| Capital work in progress | 0.06 | 0.14 | 17.55 |

| ₹ cr (standalone) | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Operating cash flow | −5.33 | −24.92 | +13.85 |
| Capex | 1.43 | 13.51 | 24.38 |
| Free cash flow | −6.76 | −38.43 | **−10.53** |

- FY26 working capital (days): receivables 251, inventory 231, payables 114 → cash conversion ≈ 368 days (FY25 higher). Invoices are raised only after installation in the shipbuilding process (CARE).
- Bank guarantees jumped to ₹28.10 cr from ₹9.66 cr. Non-current investments include commercial property ₹2.10 cr and **residential property ₹2.50 cr**; one building is still titled in the CMD's name.

### 4. Future scope
- **Navy build-out:** ~45 major platforms under construction; 75 ships on order (May-2026); a 200-ship fleet targeted by 2035; 19 commissionings planned in 2026. The company cites ~₹2.35 lakh cr of approvals with HVAC&R at ~1% of project value and expects ~₹1,000 cr of naval HVAC tenders in FY27 (company figures, not verified).
- **Capacity:** new Unit 2 at Hanbarwadi, Satara (50,000 sq ft on 6.5 acres, expandable to 100,000) inaugurated 20-Jun-2026; Phase-1 capex ~₹25 cr, possibly 40–50% subsidised under Maharashtra's PSI scheme (company claim). Management says current facilities can support ~₹400 cr of revenue.
- **New adjacencies:** data-centre cooling via Smardt oil-free chillers (reference site targeted FY27, meaningful revenue FY28); Danfoss Turbocor service aftermarket.
- **Guidance:** ~40% revenue CAGR for 3–5 years; an earlier deck targeted ₹1,000 cr sales and ₹120–130 cr PAT by FY30–31.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Dominant niche (claims ~64% of naval HVAC&R) with Navy type approvals | Order book down 17% from its Sep-2025 peak; only ~₹21 cr of new orders announced since April |
| Navy's 200-ship plan and indigenisation lists | ~368-day cash cycle; free cash flow negative three years running |
| Revenue CAGR ~45% since FY23; CARE upgrade to BBB- | EBITDA margin falling (30% → 21%) as spares shrink |
| New plant, data-centre chiller option | 68x P/E, 44x EV/EBITDA; IPO-proceeds and filing-quality flags; family board; early investor selling |

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying** — There is one dedicated thread, "Shree Refrigerations - SME". It has 24 posts from 14-Sep-2025 to 30-Aug-2026 and about 7,450 views. Two broad threads also discuss the company (Jun-2026 and May-2026). The tone is mixed but leans positive. Holders base their case on the management bench (an ex-Navy whole-time director and retired defence officers on the board) and on the naval shipbuilding pipeline. Sceptics point to the working-capital stretch, lumpy half-years, compliance lapses listed in the prospectus, nil R&D spend, family pay and the price. The main debate is whether management quality and the Navy pipeline justify the valuation. The last two posts (Aug-2026) ask why the stock is rising when no new orders have come in; the one small order since then is described as "small".

### Threads
| Thread | Kind | Posts | Active | Link |

- Data-centre cooling at ~10–15% of revenue within about 3 years — sujain11, citing ET. Not in any filing read; management's own words are "double-digit" from FY28.

The attached press note says the company won "over ₹14 crore" of Navy orders in the past one-and-a-half months (this plant order plus spares, defect rectification and MBC plants); only this one and the 29-Aug ₹3.93 cr MBC order were filed individually, so the remaining ≈₹2.2 cr is unverified. ideas.name: Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Ltd
ideas.trigger: deep-dive on request — main-board stainless-steel sheets, washers and pipes maker adding a ₹338–472 cr copper-clad-laminate plant; seven equity raises (~₹815 cr) in three years; ₹330 cr rights issue allotted 10-Sep-2026; stock at an all-time high ₹333.95 (+145% in six months); Shanti Gold bought 2.65 lakh shares on 25-Sep
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Vadodara company (since 2002) that processes stainless steel into finishing sheets (about half of sales), washers and small stamped parts (including solar-roof hooks), welded and seamless pipes, and nuts and bolts. It is now building a plant to make copper-clad laminates — the base board for printed circuit boards — with government ECMS support.
- **Growth is steady, not spectacular:** revenue ₹1,069 cr in FY26 (+20%), profit ₹64 cr (+37%); about 30% a year since FY23. EBITDA margin ~10.5%. Q1 FY27: revenue +19%, profit +22%.
- **But it keeps raising money:** seven equity raises in three years — IPO, preferential shares, promoter warrants twice, convertible preference shares, a ₹185 cr QIP and a ₹330 cr rights issue — about ₹815 cr in all. Share count up 72% since the IPO. Yet at 30-Jun-2026, ₹150 cr of QIP money was still sitting in fixed deposits pledged against its own overdraft.
- **Cash goes out:** free cash flow was negative three years running (≈ −₹260 cr). In FY26 receivables more than doubled and advances to suppliers tripled (to ₹170 cr).
- **The export story doesn't match the accounts:** investor decks call it the "#1 exporter of SS washers" with 35–52% exports; the audited accounts show exports of only 5.2% of FY26 revenue.
- **Promoter:** stake down from 55.5% to 38.7%; he skipped the ₹264 rights issue but holds 38 lakh warrants at ₹159.25 — about 110% in the money.
- **Price:** ₹333.95 is an all-time high, +145% in six months, on very heavy trading (August turnover ≈ 1.9x the market cap, delivery ~24%). 41x trailing earnings — in line with Ratnamani and Venus Pipes, which have higher margins.

**The Shanti Gold link.** Shanti Gold International (whose deep-dive is in this tab) bought 2,65,000 Ratnaveer shares in the open market on 25-Sep-2026 at about ₹333.33 (₹8.83 cr) — a plain market purchase, not a preferential allotment. Shanti Gold called it about 0.37% of Ratnaveer; on the post-rights share count it is **0.32%**. Shanti Gold says it is not a related-party deal.

### 1. What the company is
- Main board since 11-Sep-2023: NSE RATNAVEER, BSE 543978, ISIN INE05CZ01011. Registered office GIDC Savli (Manjusar), Vadodara.
- Sole individual promoter Vijay R. Sanghavi — Chairman, MD **and CFO**. Seema Sanghavi (wife) became executive director in Apr-2026. Frequent company-secretary and independent-director changes since listing.
- Auditor Pankaj R. Shah & Associates (since Feb-2022, after the previous auditor resigned; re-appointed Sep-2026; unmodified opinion; ₹5.5 lakh fee). Rating Infomerics A- (Stable) / A2+ (Apr-2026).
- Plants: Units I–II at Savli (sheets, washers, hooks, pipes), Unit III Waghodia (scrap melting), Unit IV Vatva (rolling; leased). A plot is leased from a promoter-group firm at ₹6 lakh a month. Dormant UAE subsidiary.

**Product mix (latest company slide; year label ambiguous)**

| Product | Share of revenue |
|---|---:|
| Finishing sheets | 52.4% |
| Washers | 14.7% |
| Sheet-metal parts (incl. solar hooks) | 11.0% |
| Scrap | 9.0% |
| Pipes and tubes | 6.5% |
| Nuts and bolts | 5.5% |

**Volume and realisation**

| | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Volume processed (MT) | 36,129 | 46,668 (+29%) |
| Revenue per kg (our calc) | ₹246.9 | ₹229.0 |
| Company EBITDA per tonne (₹) | 25,028 | 26,011 |

- Stated capacity 41,000 MTPA — below the 46,668 MT "processed" in FY26 (definitions differ; utilisation not disclosed).
- Customers: top-1 18%, top-5 45%, top-10 56%; mostly via distributors on purchase orders. Suppliers: top-1 39%, top-10 71%. Raw material ~87–90% of revenue (FY21–23); the MD says cost increases are passed on, but no formula is disclosed.

**Exports: decks vs audited accounts**

| Year | Audited export sales (₹ cr) | Share of revenue |
|---|---:|---:|
| FY23 (RHP) | — | 19.2% |
| FY24 | 44.94 | 7.5% |
| FY25 | 49.91 | 5.6% |
| FY26 | 55.18 | **5.2%** |
| Q1 FY27 | 9.96 | 3.2% |

- FY26 exports by country: Germany ₹29.6 cr, Spain 8.4, Italy 7.1, USA 3.9, France 2.3, UK 1.2. FY26 foreign-exchange earnings reported: only ₹2.68 cr. US tariff exposure is small on audited numbers.

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 479.75 | 595.38 | 891.88 | **1,068.74** |
| Growth | — | +24.1% | +49.8% | +19.8% |
| Gross margin | 11.8% | 14.0% | 15.4% | 16.5% |
| EBITDA (ex other income) | 47.0 | 49.98 | 86.39 | 112.21 |
| EBITDA margin | 9.8% | 8.4% | 9.7% | 10.5% |
| Profit after tax | 25.04 | 31.05 | 46.82 | **64.31** |

**Quarters (₹ cr)**

| | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY27 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 264.6 | 285.9 | 269.3 | 249.0 | **314.6** |
| EBITDA margin | 10.2% | 9.9% | 10.6% | 11.4% | 10.2% |
| Other income | 0.3 | 2.0 | 0.0 | 7.3 | 3.8 |
| Profit after tax | 15.0 | 15.4 | 16.9 | 17.0 | **18.2** |

- FY26 tax rate 15.4% (current tax only ₹5.2 cr). ROE ≈ 12.4% on average equity.

### 3. Cash, balance sheet and capital raising — the weak spot
| ₹ cr, 31-Mar | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Inventory | 244.9 | 292.9 | 289.4 |
| Receivables | 44.8 | 65.6 | **174.6** |
| Advances to suppliers | 24.7 | 52.7 | **169.5** |
| Payables | 43.9 | 120.7 | 222.4 |
| Gross debt | 207.2 | 195.1 | 335.0 |
| Cash + FDs | — | 65.9 | 268.9 |
| Net worth | 252.1 | 370.9 | 669.2 |
| Operating cash flow | 12.35 | 94.93 | **−48.41** |
| Capex | 66.0 | 138.1 | 114.5 |
| Free cash flow | −53.7 | −43.2 | **−162.9** |

- FY25 operating cash flow was flattered by ₹31 cr of capital-goods creditors (reversed in FY26); ex that, FY25 ≈ ₹64 cr and FY26 ≈ −₹22 cr.
- An export-incentive receivable of ₹16.68 cr has not moved in two years.
- Large FDs are pledged while ₹286 cr of short-term borrowing is outstanding; borrowing limit raised from ₹900 cr to ₹1,500 cr at the 26-Sep-2026 AGM.

### 4. Future scope
- **Copper-clad laminates (CCL):** ECMS approval (31-Mar-2026) for FR-4 CCL at Alindra, Savli — 15.84 lakh sheets a year in Phase 1, up to 79.2 lakh over five lines. India is ~100% import-dependent. Cost stated three ways: ₹338 cr (ECMS), ₹472 cr (Gujarat policy), ₹351 cr + ₹250 cr working capital (call). ~60% complete in Jul-2026; start slipped from Sep- to Nov-2026; Chinese machinery; no customer orders confirmed. Wipro, Kaynes and Syrma are entering too.
- **Guidance:** FY27 revenue ₹1,350–1,500 cr; ~₹2,500 cr in ~3 years (₹750 cr CCL + ₹1,800 cr stainless). A European precision-parts acquisition is in due diligence.
- **Industry:** India stainless demand grows ~7–9%; imports surged (Apr-2026 +65% y/y); anti-dumping duty on cold-rolled flats still pending (deadline Mar-2027) — duty-free imports help a processor's input costs. EU CBAM now covers washers and fasteners; EU rooftop solar is shrinking (a headwind for solar hooks).

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| ~30% revenue CAGR; margins edging up; Q1 FY27 +19% | ~₹815 cr raised in three years; ₹150 cr of QIP money idle in pledged FDs while raising ₹330 cr more |
| CCL import-substitution plant with ECMS support | CCL cost stated three ways, delayed, no orders, strong competitors |
| Rating upgraded to A-; volume +29% in FY26 | Free cash flow −₹260 cr over three years; receivables and supplier advances ballooning |
| Heavy capital already raised for growth | Export claims contradict audited accounts; promoter at 38.7% with cheap warrants; 41x P/E after +145% in six months |

updates.title: AGM: borrowing limit raised ₹900 cr → ₹1,500 cr; promoter-family whole-time director appointed with 6% of institutional votes against
updates.body:
24th AGM held 26-Sep-2026; voting results filed 28-Sep. All eight items passed. Two matter for the card:

| Item | Type | For | Against | Note |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 6. Borrowing limit from ₹900 cr to ₹1,500 cr (or paid-up capital + free reserves if higher) | special | 3,59,45,686 | 1 | 42.8% of shares polled; promoters 'not interested' |
| 8. Mrs Seema Sanghavi (DIN 11046663) appointed Whole-time Director | special, promoter group interested | 3,58,61,069 (99.76%) | 84,618 | institutions: 13,18,250 for / 83,767 against = 5.97% of institutional votes against; public non-institutions 851 against |

Also passed: Vijay Sanghavi (MD & CFO) re-appointed by rotation; Pankaj R Shah & Associates re-appointed statutory auditors; cost-auditor fee ratified; charge-creation authority to match the new limit.

Against the card: the company has raised ≈₹815 cr of equity in three years and still had ₹150 cr of QIP money in fixed deposits (liened to its own overdraft) at Jun-2026; a ₹600 cr increase in borrowing headroom on top of the ₹330 cr rights issue says the CCL build (₹338–472 cr) and the working-capital cycle will also be debt-funded. The institutional dissent on the family WTD appointment is small but is the first measured pushback in these filings; the filing does not state her relationship to the MD beyond 'promoter group interested: yes'.

ideas.name: GP Eco Solutions India Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — NSE Emerge solar-inverter distributor / assembler (Sungrow, own Invergy brand), BESS and solar EPC; FY26 revenue +68% / PAT +310%; ₹124 cr preferential + warrant issue Jul-2026; promoter pledge rose to 55.5% of promoter shares
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Noida company that mainly sells solar inverters — as one of North India's larger distributors for China's Sungrow, and under its own "Invergy" brand (assembled in India, with imported parts) — plus battery storage systems (BESS) and ground-mounted solar projects (EPC) for factories and the PM-KUSUM farm-solar scheme.
- **Growth is fast:** FY26 revenue ₹414 cr (+68%), profit to owners ₹40.1 cr (from ₹10.4 cr). Margins jumped as the mix moved from plain distribution (~76% → 53% of sales) to its own inverters and EPC.
- **But cash did not follow:** receivables tripled to ₹195 cr (172 days). Reported operating cash flow (+₹29 cr) includes ₹35.6 cr of new short-term borrowing — take that out and it was negative. Free cash flow ≈ −₹60 cr. 74% of year-end "cash" was uncleared cheques.
- **Promoters have pledged their shares:** the pledged share of promoter holding went from ~5% (Sep-2025) to 29% (Mar-2026) to **55.5% (Jul-2026)** — a third of the whole company. The FY26 annual report shows why: promoter shares secure the company's own high-cost loans — ₹7.5 cr from Satin Finserv at 16.5% and ₹10 cr from Rajasthan Securities (a broker) at 16% — each with 2.5x share cover. No pledge-creation disclosure was found in NSE's feed.
- **The auditor raised flags:** it was not shown the monthly stock statements filed with the banks; loans to subsidiaries are interest-free and overdue beyond 90 days; it says the company "needs more strong ERP system for recovery from debtors and stock management"; the MD took and repaid ₹6.6 cr of loans from the company during the year. These internal-control remarks repeat in FY24, FY25 and FY26, and the FY25 secretarial audit notes that the promoters' encumbrance (pledge) disclosure under SAST 31(4) was not made. The previous statutory auditor resigned during FY24; NKMR was appointed in Nov-2023, seven months before the IPO.
- **Disclosure quality is weak:** a ₹121.9 cr order was quietly cut to ₹76.9 cr 13 months later, and part of it had already been announced as a "new" order; order values and customers are often left blank; guidance of "3x" revenue became "₹550–600 cr" and the actual was ₹414 cr.
- **Price:** ₹402 is only 12.5x FY26 earnings — in line with SME solar peers — but 35% below its Sep-2025 peak. The ₹124 cr Jul-2026 issue (100% for working capital) brought in two Mauritius funds with ~6% each.

### 1. What the company is
- NSE Emerge (SME) only, listed 24-Jun-2024; symbol GPECO, ISIN INE0S7E01015. Registered office Noida. Indian GAAP. Auditor NKMR & Co (unmodified FY26 opinion; two different firm registration numbers appear in filings).
- Promoters: Deepak Pandey (MD), Anju Pandey, Astik Mani Tripathi; Chairman Pradeep Kumar Pandey (ex-IREDA). CFO changed Aug-2026 (the previous CFO stays as "advisor").
- Group: Invergy India (100%; own-brand inverters and BESS), AN3 Techno Power (51%; BESS assembly, "FuelON", Dasna UP), GPES Green Projects (EPC), GPES Solar 1–10 (PM-KUSUM / IPP power-sale SPVs), and an Invergy Medicare trading arm.
- Chinese supply chain: Sungrow (distributed), TBEA central inverters (resold), imported lithium cells, Sinexcel BESS testers. Invergy's local content is said to reach ">50% by Dec-2026" — i.e., below 50% today.

**Revenue mix (management figures)**

| Segment | FY25 | FY26 | FY27 indicative |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Distribution (Sungrow etc.) | 76% | 53% | ~13% |
| Own manufacturing (Invergy) | 17% | 31% | ~53% |
| EPC | 7% | 16% | ~33% |

- No audited segment split. FY25 annual report: sales ₹241.05 cr = inverters ₹140.21 cr (58%), modules ₹78.26 cr (32%), other ₹22.58 cr; **Sungrow alone was ₹115.80 cr — 82.6% of inverter sales**. FY24: 100% domestic, 99.5% B2B, >80% from UP, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Delhi and Haryana.
- Standalone (mostly distribution) gross margin is only 14.4%; the margin gain sits in the subsidiaries. In-house inverters assembled: 4,338 (FY25) → 16,529 (FY26); PCBs and casings are bought in. Permanent staff 13 (FY24) → 28 → 45 (FY26).

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr (consolidated) | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 138.44 | 246.43 | **414.38** |
| Growth | — | +78% | +68% |
| Gross margin | — | 12.4% | 21.2% |
| EBITDA (ex other income) | — | 15.9 | 59.3 |
| EBITDA margin | — | 6.4% | 14.3% |
| Profit before tax | 9.96 | 14.06 | 53.96 |
| Profit after tax (owners) | 7.33 (total) | 10.36 | **40.12** |
| EPS (₹) | 8.68 | 8.85 | 33.91 |

| ₹ cr | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 121.47 | **292.91** |
| Gross margin | 22.0% | 20.9% |
| Profit after tax (owners) | 10.40 | 29.72 |

- FY25 profit appears three ways across filings (₹10.46 / 10.36 / 10.24 cr).
- Guidance: Nov-2025 "3x" (₹700–750 cr) for FY26 → Jun-2026 reframed as "₹550–600 cr" → actual ₹414 cr. FY27 guided at 2–3x revenue; management said H1 FY27 would be "one of the lowest".

### 3. Cash, balance sheet and pledges — the weak spot
| ₹ cr | Mar-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Trade receivables | 64.30 | **195.11** |
| Inventory | 18.74 | 56.64 |
| Payables | 49.94 | 140.41 |
| Other current liabilities | 10.89 | 69.41 |
| Borrowings | 33.09 | **108.97** |
| Cash & bank (of which uncleared cheques) | 12.12 | 19.70 (14.60) |
| Fixed assets (PPE + CWIP) | 20.96 | 80.86 |
| Net worth (owners) | 64.88 | 109.15 |

| ₹ cr | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Operating cash flow, reported | 22.33 | 29.33 |
| of which short-term borrowing booked inside it | 19.83 | 35.55 |
| Operating cash flow ex borrowing | ≈ 2.5 | **≈ −6.2** |
| Capex | 18.68 | 53.57 |
| Free cash flow (ex borrowing) | ≈ −16 | **≈ −60** |

- Working capital (FY26 days): receivables 172 (95 in FY25), inventory 63, payables ~157. Management proposes channel financing for its ~40 dealers — the receivables look like dealer credit more than DISCOM dues (inference).
- Net debt ≈ ₹89 cr at Mar-26 (≈ ₹104 cr counting uncleared cheques out of cash). Infomerics assigned IVR BBB (Stable) / A3+ on 25-Sep-2026.
- Receivables ageing (consolidated): ₹11.07 cr of ₹195.11 cr is over 6 months; no bad-debt provision; ₹4.48 cr is owed by SAR Renewables — the MD's wife's proprietorship, which *sold* goods to GP Eco (₹10.9 cr in FY24, ₹3.6 cr in FY25) yet sits on GP Eco's books as a receivable. The ageing doesn't roll forward: Mar-24 shows nothing older than 2 years, Mar-25 shows ₹1.19 cr older than 3 years. No expected-credit-loss provision in any year. Customer advances jumped to ₹59.4 cr (from ₹7.7 cr).

**Lenders (FY26 annual report)**

| Lender | Facility | Rate | Security |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Satin Finserv | business loan ₹7.50 cr | 16.50% | Anju Pandey's shares (2.5x) + ₹75 lakh FD lien |
| Rajasthan Securities | term loan ₹10.00 cr | 16.00% | Anju Pandey's shares (2.5x) |
| SBI | cash credit ₹12.50 cr | EBR + 1.25% | — |
| IndusInd | cash credit ₹6 cr | Repo + 3.40% | Noida properties owned by Pradeep Kumar Pandey |
| HDFC | overdraft ₹3 cr | — | Dasna land owned by Invergy Medicare |
| AU Small Finance Bank | ₹9.16 cr | 9.75% | Jhalawar PM-KUSUM project |

- All facilities carry the three promoters' personal guarantees.

**Promoter pledge (shareholding-pattern filings)**

| Date | Shares pledged | % of promoter holding |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sep-2025 | 3,64,619 | ~5% |
| Mar-2026 | 21,30,553 | 29% |
| Jul-2026 | **40,65,981** | **55.5%** (≈ 33% of the company) |

- Jul-2026 by person: Anju Pandey 22,96,953 of 36,00,000; Deepak Pandey 16,01,428 of 32,33,600; Astik Tripathi 1,67,000 of 3,70,000. No Reg 31 pledge-creation disclosure found; NSE's pledge data returned empty; the promoters' Apr-2026 annual declaration says no encumbrance "other than those already disclosed". The Jul-2026 pledge coincides with the promoters paying ₹6.37 cr upfront on ₹25.5 cr of warrants.

### 4. Future scope
- **Orders:** Jul–Aug 2026 disclosures total ≈ ₹219 cr (0.53x FY26 revenue): KPI Green tracker/MMS supply for SJVN Khavda (₹57.2 cr + ₹58.3 cr), an Invergy inverter/BESS package (₹72.1 cr; buyers "to be disclosed separately" — not found), E-KORS DISCOM inverters (₹18.2 cr), Neelkanth Rolling Mills 4 MW (₹13.0 cr). No confirmed order book is disclosed; management declined to give one on the Jun-2026 call.
- **BESS:** Dasna plant plans moved from "5 GWh by Q3 FY26" to "3 GWh by 30-Sep-2026"; capex guidance from ₹30–40 cr to ~₹200 cr. Module/cell plans (a ₹1,000 cr MP MoU) were "dropped… postponed".
- **IPP:** a 100 MW solar park SPV has 765 kV grid connectivity (project ~₹350 cr — funding not shown); 15 MW PM-KUSUM power sale to MP (PPAs Jun-2026).
- **Industry:** India added a record 44.6 GW of solar in FY26 (16.3 GW distributed, incl. 7.6 GW PM-KUSUM); PM Surya Ghar passed 50 lakh homes (target 75 lakh by Dec-2026) — the market for residential inverters. PM-KUSUM's current timeline ends Sep-2026 (PPA projects to Mar-2027) with a 2.0 version being prepared. DISCOM legacy dues are down to ₹3,330 cr. ALMM List-II (domestic cells) applies to government-backed projects from Jun-2026.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Revenue +68%, margins up as own-brand inverters and EPC grow | 55.5% of promoter shares pledged, no pledge disclosures found |
| Rooftop (PM Surya Ghar), KUSUM and BESS demand at record levels | Operating cash flow negative once borrowing is taken out; receivables 172 days |
| 12.5x P/E, ~10x EV/EBITDA — cheap vs growth, ROE ~46% | Order cut 37% and re-announced; guidance rewritten; frequent NSE queries |
| New ₹124 cr of equity for working capital; BBB rating | Chinese inverter/cell dependence; heavy dilution (28.5 lakh warrants outstanding) |

| # | Risk | Detail |

ideas.name: Trishakti Industries Ltd
ideas.trigger: filing: CAPEX - Trishakti Industries disclosed on 28-Sep-2026 (15:07 IST, Reg 30 press release) that it has PLACED a purchase order with XCMG worth Rs 105.39 cr for 60 machines - 11 crawler cranes (ten 150-tonne, one 250-tonne), 10 fifty-tonne truck cranes and 39 XGS-series articulated boom lifts - described as part of the balance Rs 130-140 cr of a cumulative Rs 400 cr capex plan. It is a fleet capex, not an order won: Trishakti is the buyer.
ideas.thesis:
**Read the filing before anything else: the direction of this order is the opposite of how it scans.** BSE's own classifier files it under *Award of Order / Receipt of Order*, and the day's scan scored it as an ORDER signal. The press release, opened and read in full (4 pages), says Trishakti **issued** a Rs 105.39 cr purchase order **to** XCMG, the Chinese construction-machinery maker. Nobody has awarded Trishakti anything. This is a fleet purchase - capital going out, capacity coming in - and every number below is framed that way.

**What the business physically does.** Trishakti Industries (BSE 531279, no NSE listing; also on the Calcutta Stock Exchange) rents heavy lifting equipment: crawler cranes, truck-mounted cranes, all-terrain cranes, piling rigs and manlifters, with lifting capability up to 750 MT. The FY26 annual report states a fleet of **143 machines** at 31-Mar-2026, deployed to 100+ customers across 25+ industries, with **Renewable Energy the largest single vertical at about 48% of the deployed fleet**. The customer takes the machine for a project's duration; Trishakti carries the capital cost, the depreciation and the maintenance, and earns rental linked to utilisation. The one physical unit that drives revenue is therefore **a machine-year**, and the one ratio that matters is rental revenue per machine at the utilisation achieved.

**The scale-up already on the record (audited, FY26 annual report).**

| | FY2025 | FY2026 | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue from operations (Rs cr) | 14.99 | 27.85 | +85.7% |
| Other income (Rs cr) | 2.03 | 4.60 | +126.9% |
| EBITDA (Rs cr) | 6.28 | 20.21 | +221.9% |
| Depreciation (Rs cr) | 1.18 | 6.82 | +478.7% |
| Finance costs (Rs cr) | 1.47 | 3.88 | +163.7% |
| PAT (Rs cr) | 3.55 | 7.66 | +115.9% |
| Fleet (machines) | ~29 (fleet "nearly quintupled" in FY26) | 143 | - |
| Capex deployed (Rs cr) | 48.80 | 210.00 | - |
| Total assets (Rs cr) | 67.96 | 289.10 | +325% |

Q1 FY27, filed with BSE: revenue **Rs 14.38 cr against Rs 4.08 cr** a year earlier (**+252%**), PAT **Rs 4.30 cr against Rs 0.91 cr** (+372%). One quarter of FY27 has already produced more revenue than the whole of FY25. The company states **near-100% fleet utilisation** through FY26 and Q1 FY27, and today's release puts the fleet at **approximately 155-158 machines** as of the Q1 FY27 earnings call of 23-Jul-2026, with an **executable order book of about Rs 70-72 cr for FY27**.

**Why the growth is credible and where the doubt sits.** The revenue is not a claim; it is filed quarterly and it accelerated for four consecutive quarters (Rs 4.08 cr, 6.65, 8.00, 9.11, then 14.38). Utilisation near 100% while the fleet quintupled is the non-trivial part - fleet growth without utilisation is the classic warning sign, and it did not happen here. What is unproven is whether the *returns* justify the capital: statutory **ROCE was 11.83% in FY26** against management's stated aspiration of 22-25% on incremental capex, and the funding structure (below) is where this idea is most likely to break.

**One arithmetic inconsistency in the company's own release, recorded not resolved.** It says the 60 new machines take the fleet to "230 units", and separately restates a target of "200+ units by FY27". 155-158 plus 60 is 215-218. The three numbers do not reconcile; the release does not give a delivery schedule, so how many of the 60 machines earn rental in FY27 at all is unknown.
ideas.model:
**Revenue per machine, measured rather than assumed.** Two anchors exist and they differ, so both are shown.

| basis | revenue | fleet | revenue per machine-year |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY26 full year | Rs 27.85 cr | average of ~29 opening and 143 closing = ~86 | **Rs 32.4 lakh** |
| Q1 FY27 annualised (x4) | Rs 14.38 cr x 4 = Rs 57.52 cr | ~156.5 (company's own 155-158) | **Rs 36.8 lakh** |

The Q1 FY27 figure is the better forward anchor: it is the most recent filed quarter and the fleet was not doubling inside it. It is still one quarter annualised, and crane rental is not perfectly even across quarters - that is a stated limitation, not a hidden one.

**What the 60 machines can add, at the company's own numbers.**

- Fleet after delivery: 155-158 + 60 = **215-218 machines** (using the release's arithmetic inputs, not its "230").
- At Rs 36.8 lakh per machine-year: 218 x 0.368 = **Rs 80.2 cr of revenue** at full deployment, against Rs 27.85 cr in FY26 and a Rs 57.5 cr Q1 FY27 run-rate.
- **The margin that matters is not the headline one.** The annual report's "EBITDA margin 62.3%" is EBITDA divided by *total income* (Rs 20.21 cr / Rs 32.44 cr). Measured against revenue from operations, and excluding other income, operating EBITDA was Rs 15.62 cr on Rs 27.85 cr = **56.1%**. Using 56.1%: Rs 80.2 cr of revenue gives about **Rs 45.0 cr of operating EBITDA**.

**Then the two costs that scale with the asset base, which is where the case thins.**

- **Depreciation.** FY26 depreciation of Rs 6.82 cr on average property, plant and equipment of Rs 112.7 cr (Rs 36.11 cr opening, Rs 189.38 cr closing) is an effective **6.05% a year** - about a 16-year life. Add Rs 105.39 cr of new machines plus the Rs 25.82 cr already in capital work-in-progress and PPE reaches roughly **Rs 320 cr**, implying depreciation of about **Rs 19.4 cr** a year once the fleet is in service, against Rs 6.82 cr in FY26.
- **Finance cost.** FY26 finance cost of Rs 3.88 cr on average total borrowings of Rs 59.05 cr is an effective 6.6%, and that rate does not capture the Rs 156.01 cr of *other current financial liabilities* the company attributes to "equipment financing arrangements". If the Rs 105.39 cr is funded on similar terms at roughly 9%, finance cost rises by about Rs 9.5 cr to **Rs 13.4 cr**. The 9% is an assumption and is flagged as such - the release states no funding plan.

**The bridge, with the assumptions visible.**

| line | Rs cr | source |
|---|---:|---|
| Revenue at 218 machines | 80.2 | Q1 FY27 revenue per machine x fleet |
| Operating EBITDA at 56.1% | 45.0 | FY26 operating margin ex other income |
| less depreciation | (19.4) | FY26 effective 6.05% on ~Rs 320 cr PPE |
| less finance cost | (13.4) | FY26 base plus ~9% on Rs 105 cr (assumed) |
| = PBT excluding other income | **12.2** | |
| PAT at a 25% tax rate | **9.2** | FY26 effective rate was 19.5%; 25% used as the normalised rate |

On 1.656 cr shares (equity capital Rs 331.15 lakh at Rs 2 face), that is **EPS of about Rs 5.55**; fully diluted for the 16.18 lakh outstanding warrants, about **Rs 5.06**. Add back other income at the FY26 level of Rs 4.60 cr and PAT reaches about Rs 12.6 cr, **EPS Rs 6.93 diluted**.

**The conclusion the arithmetic forces.** Nearly doubling the fleet roughly doubles revenue, but depreciation triples and finance cost more than triples, so **EPS does not double**. At the 2026-09-28 close of Rs 243.05 the forward PE on the Rs 6.93 case is about **35x** - essentially unchanged from the trailing multiple. This capex buys scale; on these inputs it does not by itself buy a re-rating. What would change that is revenue per machine rising rather than holding, or the funding coming as equity rather than as more current liabilities.

**Trishakti at the 2026-09-28 close of Rs 243.05.**

| measure | value | basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Market cap | Rs 392.1 cr | BSE scrip master, this run |
| FY26 EPS | Rs 4.67 | BSE detailed results, FY26 audited |
| PE on FY26 EPS | **52.0x** | 243.05 / 4.67 |
| Trailing-4-quarter EPS | Rs 6.74 | Q2-Q4 FY26 (0.98 + 1.50 + 1.65) + Q1 FY27 (2.61) |
| PE on trailing 4 quarters | **36.1x** | 243.05 / 6.74 |
| Net worth 31-Mar-2026 | Rs 44.75 cr | audited: share capital 3.31 + other equity 41.44 |
| Price to book | **about 8.8x** | 392.1 / 44.75, before any warrant conversion |
| FY26 ROCE | 11.83% | company's own ratio table |
| FY26 ROE | 21.62% | company's own ratio table |

*BSE's company header reports EPS 6.54, PE 37.16, PB 32.98 and ROE 88.72 for this scrip. The EPS and PE are close to the trailing-four-quarter figures computed above, but PB 32.98 and ROE 88.72 cannot be reconciled with audited net worth of Rs 44.75 cr and the company's own stated ROE of 21.62%. The audited figures are used above and BSE's header ratios are treated as unreliable for this scrip.*

**The one real listed comparator.** The dossier's automatic peer set is useless here - BSE files Trishakti under *Diversified Commercial Services*, which returns staffing, finance and alcohol companies. The genuine comparator is **Sanghvi Movers (BSE 530073)**, India's established listed crane-rental company, read from its BSE header this run:

| | Trishakti | Sanghvi Movers |
|---|---:|---:|
| Market cap (Rs cr) | 392 | 3,953 |
| PE | 36.1x trailing | **24.35x** (19.31x consolidated) |
| Price to book | ~8.8x | **3.64x** |
| Operating margin | 62.30% (on total income) | 49.18% |
| ROE | 21.62% | 14.96% |
| Net profit margin | 27.51% | 20.29% |

**So the re-rating case, stated honestly, is weak on multiples.** Trishakti already trades at a ~48% PE premium and a ~2.4x price-to-book premium to the incumbent peer, while earning its higher margins on a balance sheet levered 1.90x with a current ratio of 0.37x. The bull case cannot be "it is cheap"; it has to be "the fleet compounds at near-100% utilisation and revenue per machine holds", and the price already carries a good deal of that. The market cap of Rs 392 cr does sit inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where the three-year study found 5x runs concentrate, and the stock has not had a volume explosion - volume on 2026-09-28 was **0.4x** the 60-day median, which the same study says is neither good nor bad evidence (81% of 5x runs had a volume spike and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere).
ideas.red_flags:
- **The balance sheet is the main risk, and it is not in the borrowings line.** Total assets of Rs 289.10 cr at 31-Mar-2026 are funded by net worth of just Rs 44.75 cr, total borrowings of Rs 85.18 cr, and **Rs 156.01 cr of "other financial liabilities" inside current liabilities - up from Rs 8.54 cr, a rise of 1,727%**. This single line is larger than all borrowings combined and larger than three times net worth. The company attributes it to "increased current liabilities linked to equipment financing arrangements". Note 22 was not read in full this run, so what exactly it contains, when it falls due and on what terms is **unknown** - and it is the most important unknown about this company.
- **Current ratio fell from 1.09x to 0.37x** (-66%), the company's own disclosure. Current liabilities are roughly 2.7x current assets.
- **Cash and equivalents are Rs 0.58 cr**, down 48.4% from Rs 1.12 cr, against Rs 105.39 cr of equipment now on order.
- **Debt-equity rose from 1.26x to 1.90x**, debt service coverage fell from 1.58x to 1.43x, interest coverage 3.45x. The company describes the leverage as "a conscious trade-off" and says the current ratio is one it is "actively managing".
- **The board is seeking to raise the borrowing limit from Rs 400 cr to Rs 1,000 cr** (AGM resolution, item 4 in the notice). That is 2.5x the current cap and 22x FY26 net worth - an intention to lever much further.
- **Receivables.** Trade receivables rose 94.3% to Rs 20.19 cr. The company's own trade-receivables turnover of 1.82x implies about **201 days** of sales outstanding, and the company names receivables management "an explicit priority for FY27".
- **ROCE of 11.83% is below any plausible blended cost of this capital structure**, and roughly half management's own 22-25% aspiration. Statutory ROCE is the measured number; the aspiration is not.
- **Dilution at a price well below today's.** 16,18,000 warrants were issued at Rs 158.10 to promoters, promoter group and public (board 16-Jul-2025, EGM 13-Aug-2025), with only the minimum 25% (Rs 6.40 cr) received and 18 months to convert; equity shares were also allotted preferentially at Rs 158.10. Two warrant holders had converted by the date of the report. The close today is Rs 243.05.
- **Promoter holding has fallen**, from 68.97% (June 2026) to **67.26%** (02-Sep-2026 disclosure), having been 68.49% in December 2025. Whether the fall is dilution from warrant conversion by non-promoters or promoter selling was not established this run.
- **The headline EBITDA margin is flattered by other income.** Rs 4.60 cr of other income is 14.2% of total income; the stated 62.3% margin is on total income, and operating EBITDA on revenue from operations is 56.1%.
- **Two internal inconsistencies in the company's own FY26 annual report.** Its performance dashboard shows capex deployed of Rs 4,880 lakh in the FY26 column and Rs 21,000 lakh in the FY25 column, while the narrative on the facing page says FY26 deployed Rs 21,000 lakh and FY25 Rs 4,880 lakh - the row is transposed. And the release's fleet arithmetic (above) does not reconcile.
- **Related-party and remuneration detail could not be checked.** The annual report states there were no materially significant related-party transactions, but the Section 197(12) managerial-remuneration statement was **excluded from the dispatched report** and is available only on inspection at the registered office. So promoter salary against profit is unknown, not clean.
- **A material subsidiary that is a finance company.** Trishakti Capital Limited was a material subsidiary in FY26 under Regulation 16(1)(c) and ceases to be one in FY27. Its accounts were not read.
- **The price has already moved:** +61.8% over the 65-day scan window, +91.5% over six months, +65.5% over a year, and it sits 10.8% below the window high of Rs 272.5.
- **What is clean:** the statutory auditors expressed an **unmodified opinion** with no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer, and the secretarial audit report likewise.
- **The order study does not transfer to this filing.** The 1,245-filing study measured orders *received*, sized against a trailing year of sales, and found rarity predictive. This is a purchase order *issued*, so neither finding applies. For scale only: Rs 105.39 cr is **3.8x** FY26 revenue of Rs 27.85 cr and **26.9%** of market cap. The count of Trishakti's own prior order or capex announcements could not be established - BSE's per-scrip announcement endpoint returns "No Record Found!" for scrip 531279 (measured three times this run), and the company has no NSE symbol, so the NSE archive covers it either.
ideas.verify:
1. **Note 22, "other financial liabilities" - Rs 156.01 cr.** The single most valuable missing fact. It is the largest item on the balance sheet, it grew 18-fold in one year, and it sits in *current* liabilities against Rs 0.58 cr of cash. Whether it is supplier credit from equipment vendors, finance-lease obligations, or something with a near-term maturity decides whether the fleet is funded or merely deferred. It needs the full FY26 financial statements notes, which this run did not read.
2. **How the Rs 105.39 cr is being paid, and when the 60 machines arrive.** The release states neither a funding source nor a delivery schedule. A quarter-by-quarter delivery profile is what turns the model above from a full-deployment number into an FY27 number. The Q2 FY27 earnings call and any subsequent Reg 30 disclosure on financing would settle it.
3. **Whether rental yield per machine is holding as the fleet doubles.** The whole case rests on Rs 36.8 lakh per machine-year. The Q2 FY27 result against the disclosed fleet count is the direct test, and it arrives within weeks.
4. **Utilisation, independently.** "Near 100%" is management's figure and is not separately verifiable from the filings. Customer or dealer checks, or the mix of machines on hire disclosed in an investor presentation, would corroborate it.
5. **Whether the receivable is collectible.** About 201 days of sales outstanding with Tier-1 names (L&T, Adani and Reliance are the relationships the annual report claims) should not take 200 days. An ageing schedule from the notes, and confirmation of those customer relationships, are both ground work.
6. **The Rs 400 cr to Rs 1,000 cr borrowing limit.** Whether shareholders approved it, and what the board intends to draw, would materially change the leverage picture.

- **The composition, terms and maturity of the Rs 156.01 cr of other current financial liabilities.** Note 22 was not read.
- **Delivery schedule for the 60 XCMG machines, and therefore how much of the Rs 80 cr revenue case lands in FY27 rather than FY28.**
- **Funding source for the Rs 105.39 cr.** Not stated in the release.
- **The fleet count that reconciles.** 155-158 plus 60 is 215-218; the release says 230 and separately targets 200+. Which is right is unknown.
- **Prior order and capex announcement count**, hence the rarity test: BSE's per-scrip announcement endpoint returns "No Record Found!" for scrip 531279 and there is no NSE listing.
- **Managerial remuneration against profit.** The Section 197(12) statement was excluded from the dispatched annual report.
- **Why promoter holding fell from 68.97% to 67.26%** between June and September 2026 - dilution or sale.
- **Trishakti Capital Limited's accounts**, and what a finance subsidiary does inside an equipment-rental group.
- **Whether the Rs 4.60 cr of other income recurs.** It is 14.2% of total income and 60% of PAT.
- **No investor presentation or concall transcript was read.** BSE's per-scrip announcement feed does not serve this scrip, so only the FY26 annual report, the day's press release and the BSE results series were available. The Q1 FY27 fleet and order-book figures quoted here are the company's own, as restated in today's release, not read from the transcript itself.
- **Q1 FY27 EBITDA**, and therefore whether the 56.1% operating margin held into FY27. The quarterly filing in the BSE series gives revenue, other income and PAT but not the expense split.
ideas.confidence: low: the trigger is verified from the filing itself and it is large - Rs 105.39 cr is 3.8x a trailing year's revenue and 26.9% of market cap - on a company whose revenue rose 85.7% in FY26 and 252% in Q1 FY27 at near-100% utilisation, inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where the three-year study found 5x runs concentrate, and with an unmodified audit opinion. Three things hold the confidence down. First, the model's own arithmetic: doubling the fleet roughly doubles revenue but triples depreciation and finance cost, so the forward PE stays near 35x and the multiple does not compress on its own. Second, the funding: Rs 156.01 cr of other current financial liabilities against Rs 0.58 cr of cash, a current ratio of 0.37x and a request to lift the borrowing limit to Rs 1,000 cr - and note 22, which would explain it, was not read. Third, the stock has already risen 91.5% in six months and trades at a 48% PE premium and 2.4x the price-to-book of Sanghvi Movers, the established peer. This is filed as research on a verified trigger with the balance-sheet question open, not as a conclusion.

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying.** The card said there was no ValuePickr thread. One now exists: a dedicated thread opened on 17-Sep-2026, 11 days before this card. It has **a single post and no replies**. The author (basumallick) signs off with the disclaimer of a SEBI-registered research analyst and PMS firm, so it is professional research rather than retail discussion. The post is balanced. It describes a smaller, younger-fleet Sanghvi Movers with 100% utilisation, and it gives about as much space to leverage, supplier credit, roughly 200 debtor days and staff turnover in the company-secretary role. There are two earlier mentions in broad threads. The longer one is a January 2026 note (kdjolly) built mainly from a management video and the Q3 call. Nobody on the forum has yet discussed the 28-Sep-2026 XCMG purchase order.

### Threads
| Thread | Kind | Posts | Active | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trishakti Industries Ltd | dedicated | 1 | 2026-09-17 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/trishakti-industries-ltd/224648) |
| Smallcap hunter - dark horses with triggers | mention | 1 | 2026-01-21 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/smallcap-hunter-trying-to-find-the-dark-horses-with-triggers/47673/889) |
| The anti-portfolio | mention | 1 | 2026-06-06 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/the-anti-portfolio/28464/813) |

### Points members raise
| Bull case raised | Bear case raised |
|---|---|
| The fleet is all new, so there is little downtime, 100% utilisation and 56% operating margin. A younger fleet than Sanghvi Movers is an edge with large clients (basumallick) | Debt-equity is 1.9x. With supplier credit on equipment added, external liabilities of about Rs 231 cr are more than 5x net worth (basumallick) |
| Entry barriers: Rs 5-50 cr per crane, 3-6 month OEM waiting lists, strict vendor approval at blue-chip clients, and scarce skilled operators (basumallick) | About 200 debtor days against Sanghvi's 92, despite the claim of Tier-1-only clients (basumallick, kdjolly) |
| Management raised the fleet target from 150 to 200+ and deployed Rs 210 cr in FY26 against Rs 100 cr planned; revenue guidance is Rs 60-65 cr for FY27 (basumallick, kdjolly) | 48% of the fleet serves renewables, so a policy change would hit hard. Infrastructure spending depends on the government's purse (basumallick) |
| New machines are under OEM warranty for about 3 years, which keeps maintenance costs low (kdjolly, citing the Q3 call) | Utilisation is already maxed out. The UAE/Saudi move stretches management bandwidth. Three company secretaries in two years (basumallick). A capital-heavy business tied to infrastructure growth (vikas_sinha) |

### New verified data from the forum
| Data point | Primary source that confirms it |
|---|---|
| **What makes up the Rs 156.01 cr of "other financial liabilities"** (the card's biggest unknown; Note 22 was unread). **Rs 146.10 cr is "Expenses Payable on account of Capital Goods"**, nil a year earlier. That means the FY26 machines were largely bought on supplier credit, not paid up front. The rest: advance from others Rs 4.99 cr, cheques issued beyond the bank balance Rs 1.61 cr, customer advances for crane mobilisation Rs 1.04 cr, and smaller items. **The note gives no due date or interest terms** for the Rs 146.10 cr, so the maturity question remains open. | [FY26 annual report, Note 22 (standalone) / Note 21 (consolidated)](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/bb004478-d702-4fbf-863b-3ec7ab9f42ef.pdf) |
| **Revenue guidance**, not on the card: FY27 **Rs 60-65 cr**, FY28 **Rs 90-100 cr**, with EBITDA above 60% and a fleet of 200+ by FY27. On the Q1 call, management guided a 60-65% EBITDA margin and a 25-30% PAT margin on the Rs 70-72 cr executable order book. | [Q1 FY27 investor presentation, BSE 23-Jul-2026](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/810e0df6-a0c8-4fc8-b16c-86171d0dabe7.pdf); [Q1 FY27 call transcript, BSE 28-Jul-2026](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/8b86b991-eec6-4faa-8ef4-f095d8dbfa49.pdf) |
| **The capex programme**: Rs 400 cr over FY25-FY27, of which about **Rs 270 cr is done** (including GST) and **Rs 130-140 cr remains**. The MD said the remainder could be finished with just a few wind-energy machines. | Q1 FY27 call transcript |
| **The named client roster**: L&T, Reliance, RVNL, ONGC, ITD Cementation, Adani Group, KEC International, Jindal Group, Tata Steel and NCC. | Q1 FY27 investor presentation |
| **Promoter loans have been cleared, not added.** Unsecured loans from promoters and the promoter group were **Rs 3.86 cr at 31-Mar-2025 and nil at 31-Mar-2026**. Loans from the promoter-linked companies Starlight Capital (Rs 1.82 cr) and Starmax Investment (Rs 1.05 cr) outstanding at FY25 were also nil at FY26. A special resolution allowed warrants to be issued "by utilization of existing unsecured loan". | FY26 annual report (borrowings note; related-party note; secretarial audit report) |
| **Management on receivables**: payments from the core business come in under 60 days, and the MD said the cycle will be "streamlined" in FY27. This is management's statement, not a measured figure. The card's 201-day figure is the company's own ratio. | Q1 FY27 call transcript |

### Claims on the forum not verified
- A preferential issue at Rs 86 in October 2024 — kdjolly. The linked BSE PDF is a scanned image, and no text could be extracted this run.
- "Three company secretaries have been appointed in the last 2 years" — basumallick. The appointment and resignation filings were not counted this run.
- Promoter unsecured loans of about Rs 10-12 cr, and a secured-loan D/E of about 0.7x — kdjolly, citing a management video. The video was not a filing and was not used.
- The legacy business was exited after a family settlement in 2025 (basumallick), or after a 2019-20 family separation with control taken in FY23 (kdjolly). The two members disagree with each other, and no settlement filing was read.
- Port equipment (reach stackers) from 1-Apr-2026 — kdjolly. This was not found in the Q1 FY27 presentation or transcript.
- A Rs 1 trillion Saudi infrastructure pipeline and a crane-rental market above US$1 bn — basumallick, attributed to management. Management's industry figures were not checked.

### Where the forum disagrees with the filings
- **"Part of it is loans from the promoter"** (basumallick, on the 1.9x debt-equity). At 31-Mar-2026 the annual report shows **nil** unsecured loans from promoters or promoter-group entities. The 1.9x reflects total borrowings of Rs 85.18 cr, none of which is from the promoters.
- **"Internal accruals are the primary engine"** for the capex plan, and the company is cash-flow positive (kdjolly, from the Q3 call). The FY26 balance sheet shows the fleet was funded mainly by **Rs 146.10 cr of unpaid capital-goods payables** plus Rs 85.18 cr of borrowings, against a net worth of Rs 44.75 cr.
- **Capex plan period**: "FY25-FY28" (kdjolly) versus **FY25-FY27** in the Q1 FY27 presentation.

ideas.name: Recode Studios Ltd
ideas.industry: Personal Care — colour cosmetics brand (asset-light, outsourced manufacturing)
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME (not NSE Emerge) Ludhiana colour-cosmetics brand listed 12-May-2026 at ₹158; FY26 revenue ₹79.95 cr (+67%), PAT ₹11.22 cr (+261%); stock ₹448.55 (+184% vs issue) at ~42x FY26 EPS; H2 results re-filed for 'typographical errors', three independent directors, the co-founder COO and the CS left within 7 weeks of Jul–Aug 2026
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Ludhiana company that sells make-up under its own "Recode" brand (350+ SKUs: foundation, primer, setting spray, kajal, lipsticks, brushes). It makes nothing itself — products come from contract manufacturers in India and from Germany/Thailand; it brands, markets and distributes them. It became known after Shark Tank India season 2 (Jan-2023).
- **Where it is listed:** **BSE SME only** (scrip 544755, symbol RECODE, ISIN INE2B6701015). It is *not* on NSE Emerge — the shareholding filing says "NSE Symbol: NOTLISTED" and RECODE is absent from NSE's 25- and 28-Sep bhavcopies.
- **Growth is real on paper:** revenue ₹22.4 cr (FY23) → ₹79.95 cr (FY26); profit ₹0.69 cr → ₹11.22 cr. Gross margin rose from 48% to 62% and EBITDA margin from 6% to 21%.
- **But the best quarter was the one the IPO was priced on.** Subtracting the audited H1 from the prospectus's 9-month accounts gives Oct–Dec 2025 at a 36% EBITDA margin; Jan–Mar 2026 (after the prospectus cut-off) fell to 14%, and receivables jumped ₹5.4 cr in that one quarter.
- **Reporting is sloppy:** the half-year results were re-filed four days later (H2 PAT ₹557 → ₹734 lakh, H1 ₹512 → ₹388 lakh); the press release still carries the wrong numbers; the signed auditor's CARO report contains the drafting note "The highlighted conclusions in this draft must be agreed … before the report is signed"; director pay differs between two sections of the same annual report.
- **Governance churn right after listing:** all three independent directors resigned (13-Jul, 5-Aug, 17-Aug-2026), co-founder/promoter Rahul Sachdeva quit as COO (24-Aug) and was replaced by the MD's son, the CS left (31-Aug). The previous statutory auditor also resigned during FY26.
- **Price:** ₹448.55 = ₹477 cr market cap = **42.5x FY26 EPS on post-IPO shares**, ~6x EV/sales — the stock is up 184% from the ₹158 issue price and 157% from its June low, with seven sessions closing up ~5% in a day. Management guides ≥50% growth in FY27; even hitting that at FY26 margins gives ~28x.

### 1. The business
- Incorporated 16-Jun-2021; took over the "Recode" brand from promoters' partnership firm M/s Lush Looks (2018). Promoters: Dheeraj Bansal (CMD), Karan Bansal (WTD & CEO), Shelly Bansal (WTD), Shalini Trehan (NED), Preeti Trehan, Rahul Sachdeva; 10 promoter-group holders in total.
- 156 employees (Mar-2026), 22–23 stores (3 COCO, 19 FOFO), 6 warehouses, 7 mall kiosks (Aug-2026), first NewU (Dabur's H&B chain) store Aug-2026, Nykaa Now quick-commerce Sep-2026. Management said on 3-Jun-2026 that the FOFO franchise model is "closed for the time being" in favour of dark stores.
- 9M FY26 top customer = 15.94% of net sales, top-10 = 39.4% (names withheld; management calls Nykaa a B2B customer that "buys upfront" under a sale-or-return model). Top-10 suppliers = 87.4% of purchases, top-1 = 21.6%.

**Channel mix (share of net product sales)**

| Channel | FY24 | FY25 | 9M FY26 (RHP) | FY26 (deck) |

| Online (own site + marketplaces) | 36.4% | 42.9% | 44.75% | 43.87% |
| B2B (Nykaa, retailers, MUAs, institutions) | 51.5% | 31.8% | 30.43% | 30.73% |
| FOFO stores | 11.2% | 23.5% | 23.90% | 24.50% |
| COCO stores | 0.9% | 1.9% | 0.92% | 0.91% |

**Product mix (gross sales, ₹ lakh, FY26 annual report note 19)**

| Category | FY25 | FY26 | Growth |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Face make-up | 2,443.29 | 5,296.63 | +117% |

### 2. Growth (₹ lakh; audited FY26 annual report, FY23–24 from the prospectus)

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

*FY25 PAT is ₹311.18 lakh in the audited FY26 comparatives but ₹330.29 lakh in the prospectus's restated statements.

**Half-years and derived quarters (₹ lakh)**

†Q3 = prospectus 9M (Apr–Dec 2025, restated) − audited H1; Q4 = audited FY26 − 9M. Both statements were signed by the same auditor (RMSG & Associates). H1 FY25 = FY25 − H2 FY25.

### 3. Cash and balance sheet (₹ lakh)
| | Mar-23 | Mar-24 | Mar-25 | Dec-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Trade receivables | 333.06 | 593.92 | 808.96 | 997.94 | **1,537.95** |
| Receivable days (on revenue) | 54 | 59 | 62 | 48 (ann.) | **70** |
