- FY26 OCF was 39% of PAT; free cash flow ₹251 lakh (433.78 − 182.82 capex). The 9M OCF (₹597 lakh) was higher than the full-year figure, so Jan–Mar 2026 consumed ~₹164 lakh of operating cash (different statement sets; indicative).
- Borrowings pre-IPO were ~20 small unsecured business loans from banks and NBFCs at 12–18% plus an Axis Bank working-capital line. Short-term borrowings rose from ₹195 lakh (Dec-25) to ₹504 lakh (Mar-26).
- Quarterly stock statements to Axis Bank differed from the books every quarter (e.g. Jun-25: books ₹1,418 lakh vs ₹1,081 lakh reported; Mar-26: ₹2,139 vs ₹1,910) — yet CARO clause (ii)(b) calls the reconciliation "not applicable".

### 4. IPO and use of money
- 28,22,400 shares at ₹158 (band ₹150–158): 25,03,200 fresh (₹39.55 cr) + 3,19,200 offer-for-sale (₹5.04 cr; 1,06,400 each by Rahul Sachdeva, Preeti Trehan, Karan Bansal). Lead manager Seren Capital; market maker Asnani Stock Broker. Post-issue shares 1,06,44,344. The prospectus puts the weighted average cost of promoters' secondary acquisitions at ₹97.97 per share (after the bonus).
- Pre-IPO: 1:780 bonus on 15-Dec-2025 (10,424 → 81,41,144 shares).

| Object (CARE monitoring report) | Planned ₹ cr | Used to 30-Jun-26 | Unused |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Working capital | 19.50 | 12.16 | 7.34 |
| Ludhiana warehouse (land ₹2.29 cr paid) | 5.74 | 2.45 | 3.29 |
| Marketing & advertising | 5.41 | 2.60 | 2.81 |
| General corporate purposes | 2.96 | 0.00 | 2.96 |
| Issue expenses | 5.94 | 5.54 | 0.40 |
| **Total** | **39.55** | **22.75** | **16.80** |

- CARE flagged a deviation: ₹0.08 cr of the OFS sellers' issue costs were paid from fresh-issue money (management says cheques for ₹7.50 lakh had been received). The utilisation table filed with the 30-May results lists different object heads ("plant & machine" ₹540.90 lakh, GCP ₹976.36 lakh, total ₹3,467.26 lakh) from the prospectus's.
- Jul-2026: bought 33% of Aflairza Professionals (Ahmedabad make-up brand) for ₹8.32 cr at ₹285/share (half secondary from its founders, half fresh). That values 100% at ~₹25.2 cr against predecessor-firm sales of ₹8.22 cr (FY26, +6% YoY); its profit was not disclosed. The target was converted from a partnership into a company on 16-May-2026. Phase II (to 51%) depends on milestones and is due by Feb-2027. The MD&A and an X post call it a "51% stake acquisition"; only 33% has been bought.

### 5. Ownership (pre-listing SHP, 11/12-May-2026)

|---|---:|---:|
| Promoter group (10 individuals) | 69,20,670 | 65.02% |
| — Shalini Trehan | 12,90,993 | 12.13% |

ideas.model:
**Revenue model.** There is no single physical unit here: this is a brand that outsources production. Revenue = channels (own website ~33% of sales, marketplaces ~12%, FOFO/B2B/Nykaa ~55%) × stores/reach × product mix. The company does not disclose volumes, store-level sales or SKU counts. The only disclosed drivers are store/kiosk counts, "engaged sessions" (53.5 lakh in 9M FY26 vs 59.7 lakh in FY25) and return on ad spend (5.23x 9M FY26 vs 5.27x FY25 and 7.74x FY23 — falling).

**Guidance arithmetic (management: "at least 50% growth in FY27", EBITDA margin "more or less where it currently is"):**

| ₹ cr | FY26 actual | FY27 at guidance | Arithmetic |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Revenue | 79.95 | 119.9 | 79.95 × 1.5 |
| EBITDA | 16.54 | 24.8 | 119.9 × 20.7% |
| PAT | 11.22 | 16.8 | 119.9 × 14.0% (FY26 PAT margin) |
| EPS (1,06,44,344 sh) | 10.55 | 15.8 | 16.8 cr ÷ 1.064 cr sh |
| P/E at ₹448.55 | 42.5x | 28.4x | |

Aflairza is excluded (a 33% associate; FY26 sales of ₹8.22 cr; profit not disclosed). ESOP dilution (up to 2.8%) is also excluded.

**Cross-checks and seasonality.**
- H1 (Apr–Sep) is seasonally weak for colour cosmetics (heat and humidity); management says Oct–Dec is the strongest quarter. H1 FY26 revenue was ₹36.94 cr, so +50% means H1 FY27 ≈ ₹55.4 cr (results due by 14-Nov-2026).
- FY26's 20.7% EBITDA margin blends a 16% H1, a 36% Q3 and a 14% Q4. The margin that persisted *after* the IPO pricing period is the 14% Q4 figure. At 14% EBITDA and ~9% PAT on ₹120 cr, EPS would be ~₹10 and P/E ~44x.
- Marketing (advertisement ₹644 lakh + social media ₹539 lakh) was 14.8% of FY26 revenue (18.7% with commissions). Management says it spends "20% of revenue" and will reinvest any margin gains into advertising.
- No credit-rating report was found, so there is no third-party cross-check of revenue expectations.

| P/E, FY26 | **42.5x** | PAT ₹1,122.48 lakh ÷ 1,06,44,344 post-IPO shares = EPS ₹10.55 |
| P/E on reported EPS ₹13.79 | 32.5x | pre-IPO share count (81.4 lakh) — flatters |
| EV/Sales, FY26 | 6.0x | EV ₹482.3 cr = mcap + Mar-26 debt ₹6.19 cr − cash ₹1.32 cr |
| EV/Sales with unspent IPO cash | 5.8x | EV less ₹16.80 cr in the monitoring account (30-Jun) |
| EV/EBITDA, FY26 | 29.2x | EBITDA ₹16.54 cr |
| P/B (Mar-26 book ₹20.0 cr, pre-IPO) | 23.9x | as filed |
| P/B (pro forma ≈₹53.6 cr) | ~8.9x | ₹20.0 + ₹39.55 fresh − ₹5.94 issue costs (approximation) |
| Dividend yield | 0.06% | ₹0.25 per share (2.4% payout) |

BSE's own header shows EPS 5.33 and P/E 84.2. ₹5.33 equals the H2 FY26 PAT *as first filed* (₹567.39 lakh, later corrected to ₹734.32 lakh) divided by post-IPO shares. BSE's figure therefore appears to rest on one erroneous half-year; do not use it.

**Listed peers (28-Sep-2026 closes; P/E = close ÷ BSE header TTM EPS)**

| Company | Mcap ₹ cr (BSE) | Close ₹ | EPS basis | P/E | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| Recode Studios (RECODE, BSE SME) | 477 | 448.55 | FY26, post-IPO shares | 42.5x | growth +67%, 21% EBITDA margin |
| Honasa Consumer (Mamaearth) | 15,209 | 466.50 | consolidated 7.65 | 61.0x | main board |
| FSN E-Commerce (Nykaa) | 93,376 | 326.00 | consolidated 0.91 | ~358x | retailer and Recode's likely largest customer |
| Ravelcare (RAVEL, BSE SME; also a Shark Tank cosmetics brand) | 69 | 101.00 | 2.84 (BSE header) | 35.6x | smaller SME peer |
| Emami (reference, mature FMCG) | 17,067 | 388.70 | consolidated 17.18 | 22.6x | |

**At the IPO**, the ₹158 price was 38.9x FY25 restated EPS (₹4.06, Recode's own RHP peer table) and ~10.7x annualised 9M FY26 EPS (₹11.13 × 365/275 = ₹14.77, both on pre-IPO shares). The stock now trades at 3x that issue price. At 42.5x FY26 earnings, the market is already paying for the guided 50% growth *and* for FY26's peak margins holding. The re-rating case, in one sentence: if H1 FY27 shows ≥50% growth with ≥20% EBITDA margin and receivable days back under 60, the multiple can hold on a ₹15–16 EPS; if not, the multiple rests on a quarter (Oct–Dec 2025) that has not repeated.

ideas.name: Riyaasat Lifestyle Ltd
ideas.industry: Textiles & Apparel — ethnic wedding/festive wear, own stores (Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Mumbai)
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME ethnic-wear retailer listed 1-Jul-2026 at ₹106 (opened −20%), ₹83.19 on 28-Sep after two ~20% up-days with no filing; FY26 revenue ₹33.37 cr (+35%), PAT ₹5.19 cr (+9%), but inventory ₹41 cr (123% of sales) not kept in the accounting system, OCF −₹3.19 cr, debt ₹41 cr after a ₹25.5 cr Mumbai auction property, and IPO objects varied within 2 months of listing
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** an Ahmedabad family business that designs and sells wedding and festive ethnic wear (sherwanis, lehengas, Indo-western, kurta sets) through its own stores. Legal name **Riyaasat Lifestyle Ltd** (CIN now L18100GJ2021PLC126637, incorporated 23-Oct-2021). Promoters: Gaurang R. Galiya (MD), his father Ramanbhai (WTD) and mother Sobhanaben (director).
- **Where it is listed:** **BSE SME only** — scrip **544804**, symbol RIYAASAT, ISIN INE0KYI01012, group M. Not on NSE: the pre-listing shareholding filing says "NSE Symbol: NOTLISTED" and RIYAASAT is absent from NSE's 28-Sep bhavcopy. (The 5-Sep board outcome letter wrongly heads itself "NSE SYMBOL: RIYAASAT".)
- **IPO:** 28,48,800 fresh shares at ₹106 = ₹30.20 cr, listed 1-Jul-2026. It opened at ₹84.80 (−20%), fell to ₹53.02 (13-Aug), and closed ₹83.19 on 28-Sep (−21.5% vs issue) after two back-to-back ~20% up days (25 and 28-Sep) with no price-sensitive filing.
- **Growth on paper is modest, profit is lumpy:** revenue ₹20.93 cr (FY23) → ₹33.37 cr (FY26); PAT ₹1.32 cr → ₹5.19 cr. FY26 revenue +34.6% but PAT only +8.6%. The business is extremely seasonal: H1 FY26 was a **loss of ₹4.89 cr** and H2 a profit of ₹10.08 cr (same pattern in FY25: H1 loss ₹6.27 cr, H2 profit ₹11.05 cr).
- **The core problem is inventory.** Stock rose from ₹5.27 cr (Mar-23) to **₹41.05 cr (Mar-26) = 123% of a year's revenue**. The FY26 P&L took a ₹19.18 cr credit for inventory build-up; purchases were ₹22.47 cr against revenue of ₹33.37 cr, yet reported gross margin is 85%. The audited notes say **"Inventory is not maintained in the accounting system (Tally Prime)"**; the auditor said it could not comment on physical verification; and stock statements given to banks did not agree with the books.
- **Cash does not follow profit:** operating cash flow was negative in 3 of 4 years; cumulative FY23–FY26 OCF −₹5.55 cr against cumulative PAT +₹15.38 cr.
- **Debt jumped to buy real estate:** a Santacruz (W), Mumbai building bought at a Standard Chartered bank auction for ₹25.51 cr (bid 21-Mar-2025) took gross block up by ₹29.51 cr; borrowings went from ₹8.87 cr to **₹41.36 cr** (D/E 2.26x) in FY26. Within two months of listing the company sought to vary IPO objects: ₹13.53 cr of the ₹30.20 cr (working capital ₹9.50 cr + GCP ₹4.03 cr) was already spent by 1-Sep, none of the ₹12.47 cr store capex, and the Mumbai store money is to go into the same Santacruz building where it has won another SARFAESI e-auction (Religare Finvest) for the basement, 3rd and 4th floors — price not disclosed.
- **Price:** ₹83.19 = ₹89.38 cr market cap = **17.2x FY26 EPS on post-IPO shares**, EV/EBITDA ~12.8x on the March-2026 balance sheet. Not expensive on the headline numbers — but the headline numbers rest on an inventory figure that the audit trail does not support well.

### 1. The business
- Product mix (RHP, top-5 products, ₹ lakh, 10M to 31-Jan-2026): lehenga choli 587.71 (21.1%), sherwani 454.68 (16.3%), Indo-western 319.55 (11.5%), kurta set 315.23 (11.3%), suit/tuxedo 172.75 (6.2%). Manufacturing revenue 25.6% / trading revenue 74.4% of 10M FY26.
- Stores (RHP): 6 EBOs — 4 Ahmedabad (Time Square C.G. Road, Ten-11, Iscon Arcade, Stellar Sindhubhavan 9,419 sq ft), 1 Vadodara, 1 Mumbai. Top-2 stores = 54.8% of 10M FY26 revenue (Time Square ₹825 lakh, Santacruz ₹701 lakh). Online only 2.9%.
- 177 employees at 31-Jan-2026 (RHP) / 190 permanent (FY26 annual report); only 12 enrolled in EPF (₹40,000 deposited for Jan-2026) and 32 in ESIC.
- The RHP's own chapters disagree on the Mumbai store: the business overview lists a Santacruz showroom as **owned**, the property table lists the Santacruz "Rhiday" building as **Workshop 3 (owned)** and a leased Goregaon showroom as store 6, and risk factor 19 says **all** stores are leasehold.

| COGS (materials + purchases ± stock change) | 1,069.89 | 579.73 | 551.96 | 501.91 | 490.97 |

| EBITDA (PBT + finance + D&A − other income) | 180.95 | 535.01 | 642.24 | 768.32 | 1,018.72 |
| EBITDA margin | 8.6% | 23.4% | 25.9% | 27.6% | 30.5% |

*FY25 PAT ₹478.24 lakh audited (₹486.64 lakh restated in RHP; the ₹8.40 lakh gap is prior-year tax).

ideas.model:
**Physical model (what the documents allow).** Revenue driver = store sales. The RHP gives store-level revenue only for the top two stores; it gives no footfall, bills, average ticket or sales per sq ft, so a physical build is limited.

| Unit | Figure | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Stores (EBOs) | 6 | RHP p154 |
| Total showroom area | ~26,500 sq ft | RHP objects chapter |
| 10M FY26 revenue | ₹2,786.98 lakh | RHP restated |
| Revenue / sq ft (10M, annualised ×12/10) | ~₹12,600 | derived: 2,786.98 lakh ×1.2 ÷ 26,500 |
| Planned new stores (post-variation) | Santacruz expansion + Ahmedabad (Sigma, 9,000 sq ft) + Hyderabad + Bengaluru | Postal ballot notice |

**FY27 arithmetic (illustrative, not a forecast).** If FY27 revenue grows at FY26's +34.6% → ~₹44.9 cr; at FY26's 15.6% PAT margin → PAT ~₹7.0 cr → EPS ~₹6.5 on 1,07,44,478 shares → ~12.8x at ₹83.19. If revenue grows at the FY24–FY25 pace (~9%) → ~₹36.4 cr, PAT ~₹5.7 cr, EPS ~₹5.3 → ~15.8x. Finance cost will rise (₹307.59 lakh in FY26 vs ₹77.65 lakh in FY25) and the Santacruz building adds ~₹0.8–1 cr of depreciation a year at FY26's rate (₹68.52 lakh charged on the building in its part-year), so the margin assumption is generous.

**Management guidance:** none quantified in any filing read. No credit rating exists (the Large-Corporate disclosure says "Not Applicable").

ideas.verify:
- **Is the ₹41 cr of inventory real and saleable?** A store visit (Time Square, Sindhubhavan, Santacruz) comparing racks and godown stock with ~₹41 cr at cost; ask for the bank's stock-audit report.
- **Mumbai property:** the Santacruz building's use (store vs workshop), the price and funding of the Religare-auction floors, and whether the Bawree Fashion/SCB auction left any encumbrance or dispute — MahaRERA/sub-registrar records.
- **Store economics:** footfall and sales per store after the Oct–Jan 2026–27 wedding season; the H1 FY27 result (due by mid-Nov 2026) will show whether the H1 loss pattern repeats at a larger cost base.
- **Who the FPIs are:** beneficial owners of Fivex, North Star Opportunities, Kingsman, Craft Emerging Market and Nexpact, and whether they are still holding (next SHP).

updates.title: Second Santacruz auction purchase: ₹15.50 cr for the Religare SARFAESI floors
updates.body:
Reg 30 filing 30-Sep-2026 18:46 IST: the company was the successful bidder in Religare Finvest's SARFAESI e-auction for the secured property at Plot 9, Swami Vivekanand Road / 8 Tank Road, Santacruz (W), Mumbai — the basement, 3rd and 4th floors of the same building bought from Standard Chartered's auction for ₹25.51 cr in FY26. Sale Certificate dated **22-Sep-2026**, received 30-Sep; consideration **₹15,50,00,000**. Not a related-party transaction, per the filing.

| Against the card | ₹ cr | Working |
|---|---:|---|
| Price vs FY26 revenue (₹33.37 cr) | **46.4%** | 15.50 ÷ 33.37 |
| Price vs Mar-26 net worth (₹18.28 cr) | 84.8% | 15.50 ÷ 18.28 |
| Mar-26 borrowings already on the book | 41.36 | card §3 |
| IPO money re-routed to Santacruz by the postal ballot | 5.23 | ₹523.28 lakh |
| Balance whose funding the filing does not state | **10.27** | 15.50 − 5.23 |

The card listed this price as unknown; it is now known and it is larger than the whole unspent store-capex object (₹12.47 cr). The filing says nothing about how the ₹10.27 cr beyond the re-routed IPO money is paid for (debt was 2.26x equity at Mar-26). Dates to note: the Sale Certificate is dated 22-Sep, the two ~20% up-days were 25 and 28-Sep, and the company's price-clarification reply at 12:48 on 30-Sep said no price-sensitive information was pending; this disclosure followed at 18:46 the same day.

The stock closed +15.0% at Rs 1,652.10, a 65-day high, on 7.2x its 60-day median volume.
ideas.thesis:
**The filing, read.** The two-page disclosure (BSE, 29-Sep-2026 12:41 IST) states every field in the company's own words: awarding entity **System Integrator (Private)**; scope **"Supply of communication and Grid-protection solution as per the technical requirements"**; domestic; nature **"Supply, services and AMC"**; execution **by 31-12-2028**; size **INR 4,025 Lacs (inclusive of taxes)**; no promoter interest, not a related-party transaction; **"End-user: Indian Power Utility Sector"**. The filing notes the figure is reported gross, i.e. inclusive of indirect taxes, per the SEBI circular of 25-Feb-2025.

**What the business physically does.** Valiant Communications (founded 1993, New Delhi) manufactures communication, transmission, protection, synchronisation, cybersecurity and NAS/SAN storage equipment for power utilities and other critical infrastructure. From the FY2026 annual report and the Q1-FY27 business update, both filed with BSE:

- Product lines: teleprotection (distance protection), IEEE C37.94 line-differential protection communication, phasor measurement units (PMU), grid islanding and WAMS, GPS/GNSS/**NavIC** primary reference clocks and PTP 1588v2 timing, IP/MPLS routers and SDH/PDH multiplexers, network-isolation "kill switch" and PRP switches, ransomware-resilient NAS/SAN storage.
- **"Valiant's Communication and protection equipment has been successfully installed in over 6,000+ power substations globally"** (FY2026 annual report); installations in **110+ countries**, offices in India, USA and UK, 25+ distributors.
- Qualified as a **'Class 1 Local Supplier'** under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017, and registered as a **'Trusted Source'** by the National Security Council Secretariat.
- Revenue split FY2026: **domestic 85.78%, exports 14.22%** (annual report, Corporate Highlights).

The physical unit that drives revenue is a substation bay or a communication/protection node, but the company does not disclose units shipped. The disclosed driver is therefore the **order book**, which it publishes every quarter.

**The order book is the reason this filing is large.** The Q1-FY27 business update (BSE, 12-Aug-2026) prints the series directly:

| Quarter | Gross order book (confirmed), Rs lacs |
|---|---:|
| Q1 FY25 | 2,248 |
| Q2 FY25 | 1,834 |
| Q3 FY25 | 1,271 |
| Q4 FY25 | 10,195 |
| Q1 FY26 | 8,694 |
| Q2 FY26 | 7,667 |
| Q3 FY26 | 7,643 |
| Q4 FY26 | 6,892 |
| **Q1 FY27** | **6,420** |

Read that honestly: the confirmed book has **fallen every quarter since Q4 FY25**, from Rs 101.95 cr to **Rs 64.20 cr at 30-Jun-2026**, because the company has been executing faster than it has been replenishing. Today's Rs 40.25 cr award is **62.7% of that entire confirmed book**. It is the largest single order in the company's 760-day filing history that we could read.

**Order inflow since the book was last published**, each number taken from its own Reg 30 filing, all inclusive of taxes:

| Filed | Awarding entity / end-user | Scope | Execute by | Rs cr |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| 05-Aug-2026 | Large System Integrator; end-user **Power Grid Corporation of India** | Data storage servers with backup + GPS/NavIC time synchronisation (PGCIL VoIP) | 31-03-2027 | 10.71 |
| 08-Sep-2026 | Indian Power Utilities | Supply and commissioning of communication equipment | not stated in the excerpt read | 9.85 |
| 10-Sep-2026 | System Integrator (Private) | Supply of communication equipment | 30-09-2027 | 13.88 |
| **29-Sep-2026** | **System Integrator (Private); end-user Indian Power Utility Sector** | **Communication + grid protection, supply/services/AMC** | **31-12-2028** | **40.25** |
| | | | **Total** | **74.69** |

Rs 74.69 cr of announced inflow in 55 days, against **Rs 84.11 cr of FY2026 revenue**. Adding it to the Rs 64.20 cr book at 30-Jun-2026 and ignoring Q2 execution (Q2 results are not yet filed) gives roughly **Rs 138.9 cr of gross confirmed work** — the first time in this record that the book exceeds a year of sales.

**Why the end-user matters.** The 05-Aug-2026 filing names **Power Grid Corporation of India** as end-user and the company's own update calls it *"VCL's strategic order into the Data Center application"*, built on equipment already commissioned at THDC Limited. The FY2026 annual report names **Smart Grid and RDSS** (the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme) as the lead domestic opportunity driver. RDSS smart metering is the single best-performing basket in this repo's government study — 8 names, 12.0x basket median against 3.2x for the market from 30-Jun-2021, 100% made 5x. Valiant is not a smart-meter maker; it sells the communication and protection layer that the same substation-digitisation spend buys. That is an adjacency, not membership, and the note treats it as such.

| Quarter | Revenue Rs cr | EBITDA Rs cr | PAT Rs cr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY25 | 13.60 | 4.61 | 2.92 |
| Q2 FY25 | 12.68 | 4.44 | 2.78 |
| Q3 FY25 | 8.09 | 0.70 | -0.01 |
| Q4 FY25 | 16.02 | 5.89 | 3.82 |
| Q1 FY26 | 18.12 | 6.68 | 4.46 |
| Q2 FY26 | 20.06 | 7.42 | 4.99 |
| Q3 FY26 | 21.94 | 8.23 | 5.54 |
| Q4 FY26 | 23.99 | 10.02 | 6.67 |
| **Q1 FY27** | **25.14** | **11.63** | **8.08** |

Q1 FY27 against Q1 FY26: revenue **+38.7%**, PAT **+81.2%**. The EBITDA margin the company prints for Q1 FY27 is **46.26%**, against 36.85% a year earlier. Nine consecutive quarters of sequential revenue growth since the Q3 FY25 trough.

**Forward revenue, three ways.** Q1 FY27 actual plus three quarters at a stated sequential rate:

| Sequential growth | FY27 revenue Rs cr | PAT at 28% | PAT at 32% | EPS at 32% | PE at Rs 1,652.10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% (Q1 run-rate held) | 100.6 | 28.2 | 32.2 | 27.5 | 60.0 |
| +5% a quarter | 108.4 | 30.3 | 34.7 | 29.7 | 55.7 |
| +10% a quarter | 116.7 | 32.7 | 37.3 | 31.9 | 51.7 |

The 28-32% PAT-margin band is taken from the last four measured quarters (FY26 full year 25.8%; Q4 FY26 27.8%; Q1 FY27 32.1%) and is an assumption, not guidance — **the company gives no revenue or margin guidance in any document read this run.** Share count 1.169 cr (paid-up capital Rs 1,169 lacs at Rs 10 face value, Q1 FY27 filing); 3,50,000 warrants remain outstanding, so the fully converted count is 1.204 cr.

**Cross-check against the order book.** Rs 138.9 cr gross confirmed work, less roughly 18% indirect tax, is about Rs 117.7 cr net. Spread over the stated execution windows (Rs 10.71 cr by Mar-2027, Rs 13.88 cr by Sep-2027, Rs 40.25 cr by Dec-2028) it supports the Rs 100-117 cr FY27 range above only if the older book converts quickly; the Dec-2028 order mostly lands in FY28 and FY29. **The Rs 40.25 cr order is an FY28-FY29 revenue event, not an FY27 one**, and the filing says so.

**What the order study says about this filing.** The 1,245-filing study in this repo (runbook 144c) measured two things that work:

| Test | This filing | What the study measured |
|---|---|---|
| Order / trailing year of sales | Rs 40.25 cr / Rs 84.11 cr = **47.9%** | The 25-50%-of-sales bucket reached 2x within two years **35.7%** of the time, against 21.4% for orders under 10% |
| Prior order filings in two years | **12** (13 including this one, read from BSE 30-Aug-2024 to 29-Sep-2026) | A first-filing-in-two-years reached 2x 30.4% and 5x 3.5%; a filer with **8 or more prior filings reached 2x only 17.3% and 5x never** |
| Market cap | Rs 1,931.7 cr | The Rs 300-7,500 cr band is where 5x runs happened; nothing above Rs 25,000 cr produced one in three years |

So the two halves of the test disagree, and the disagreement is the point: **the size is in the best bucket, the rarity is in the worst one.** Valiant files orders regularly — 13 in 760 days. On the study's rarity dimension alone this is a serial filer, and serial filers produced no 5x in three years.

**The re-rating case, in one sentence.** If the Rs 138.9 cr gross book converts at the Q1 FY27 margin, the forward PE falls from 76 to the 52-60 range on FY27 and lower on FY28 — the stock is not cheap on any of those numbers, and the case is that earnings grow into the multiple rather than that the multiple is wrong.

| | Rs cr |
|---|---:|

**Ownership.** Promoter holding from the BSE shareholding filings: 40.70% (13-Oct-2025 and 04-Dec-2025), 40.62% (Dec-2025 and Mar-2026), **39.75%** (07-May-2026), **39.64%** (30-Jun-2026). The May step down is arithmetically consistent with dilution, not selling: 2,50,000 shares were allotted on 07-May-2026 on warrant conversion, taking paid-up capital from Rs 1,144 lacs to Rs 1,169 lacs, and a constant promoter block of ~0.4644 cr shares moves from 40.6% to 39.7% on that count alone. The absolute promoter share count was not read this run, so this is a consistency check, not a proof.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Serial filer.** 13 order filings in 760 days. On the rarity half of the order study this is the bucket that reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and 5x never. This is the single biggest argument against reading today's filing as a step change.
- **The confirmed order book has been shrinking for five straight quarters** — Rs 101.95 cr (Q4 FY25) to Rs 64.20 cr (Q1 FY27), the company's own disclosure. Today's order reverses the direction; one order does not establish a trend, and the Q2 FY27 update (due with the November results) is the first honest test.
- **The customer is an intermediary, not the utility.** Today's award, and the 10-Sep and 27-Feb ones, come from a **"System Integrator (Private)"** whose name the company does not disclose. Valiant is a sub-supplier. That means no visibility on who the integrator is, what its own contract terms are, or what happens if the prime contract slips — and it means concentration risk that cannot be measured from the filings.
- **The pipeline figures are not orders and the company says so.** Beside the Rs 64.20 cr confirmed book, the Q1-FY27 update prints "L1 Status + Advanced Opportunities (approx) Rs 6,048 lacs" and "Forthcoming Business Opportunities (estimated) Rs 12,250 lacs", with an explicit note that these *"may change ... and should not be construed as confirmed orders"*. Treat only the Rs 64.20 cr as an order book.
- **Valuation.** Trailing PE 76.4 against the one available peer at 46.8; PB 35.3; the stock is +155.6% over one year, +44.6% in a month, and closed today at its 52-week high. Any disappointment is being priced off a high base.
- **A volume explosion is not evidence.** 7.2x the 60-day median today. The repo's own three-year study found 81% of 5x runs had a 10x volume day near the base — and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere.
- **Dilution above the current holders.** 6,00,000 warrants were issued at Rs 768 to the **non-promoter** category in the previous financial year; 2,50,000 converted on 07-May-2026 and **3,50,000 remain outstanding**. Who holds them is not stated in any document read this run.
- **Auditor and related party:** the FY2026 annual report lists revenue recognition as a key audit matter (Rs 8,411.37 lacs, "significant according to size of the Company") and states related-party transactions were at arm's length in the ordinary course with none requiring shareholder approval. No qualification or auditor change was found in the text read. The consolidated FY26 profit in the Directors' Report (Rs 2,418.07 lacs) is higher than the standalone Rs 2,166 lacs in the results; the subsidiaries (Valiant Communications UK, Valcomm USA, Valiant Infrastructure) account for the difference and their individual accounts were not read.
- **No concall, no investor presentation beyond the quarterly business update** was found in the 240-day filing list. The business update is a company-written document, not an audited one.
ideas.verify:
1. **Who the "System Integrator (Private)" is.** Three of the last four orders come from an unnamed private integrator. Identifying it — from a tender portal award, a PGCIL/state-transco EPC package list, or the integrator's own filings if listed — would say whether this is one relationship or several, and whether the Rs 40.25 cr is a slice of a much larger substation package. 4. **Who holds the 3,50,000 outstanding warrants** at Rs 768, and the identity of the "public category investors" in the preferential issue. The postal-ballot voting results of 13-Mar-2026 and the preferential-issue committee minutes would say; neither was read this run.

ideas.name: Indo Borax & Chemicals Ltd
ideas.trigger: filing: DEAL - Indo Borax filed a Reg 30 disclosure on 29-Sep-2026 15:44 IST that it has COMPLETED the acquisition of 2,38,44,000 equity shares of Kronox Lab Sciences Ltd (BSE 544187), 64.26% of Kronox's paid-up capital, for Rs 246.12 cr at Rs 103.22 per share, funded by a Rs 225 cr loan availed on 23-Sep-2026. A mandatory open offer for a further 25.79% follows.
ideas.thesis:
**The filings, read.** Three documents, all Reg 30, all filed by Indo Borax itself:

1. **20-Aug-2026 (board outcome).** The board approved a share purchase agreement among Indo Borax (the Purchaser), **Zenrock Chemicals Private Limited**, and the three selling promoters of Kronox — **Mr Ketan Vinodchandra Ramani, Mr Pritesh Vinodchandra Ramani, Mr Jogindersingh Gianchand Jaswal** — for **2,38,44,000 equity shares** of Rs 10 face value, **64.26%** of Kronox Lab Sciences Limited, at **Rs 103.22 per share**, aggregate **Rs 2,46,11,77,680**. The filing adds a footnote: the per-share price **including the consultancy fees payable by the target to each seller** under transition-support arrangements, computed per Regulation 8(7) of the SAST Regulations, is **Rs 105.87**.
2. Same filing, item 2: because control and more than 25% of voting capital pass, Indo Borax **with Zenrock as a person acting in concert** must make a **mandatory open offer for up to 95,70,000 shares, about 25.79%** of Kronox, at a price determined under the SAST Regulations.
3. **24-Sep-2026.** The company "has availed funding of **Rs 225 crore** ... from a lending institution on 23rd September, 2026 for the purpose of financing the acquisition of equity shares of Kronox Lab Sciences Limited". The lender is not named and no rate or tenor is stated.
4. **29-Sep-2026 (today).** "the said acquisition ... has been completed today, i.e., on September 29, 2026."

The accompanying press release (20-Aug-2026) adds that the erstwhile Kronox promoters **retain 9.95%** and provide transition support, and quotes MD & CEO Suresh Kalra on "expansion, diversification, premiumisation, and margin improvement".

**What each business physically does.**

- **Indo Borax & Chemicals** (Mumbai-registered, plant at Pithampur) is one of India's leading makers of **boron-based chemicals** — boric acid and derivatives. The FY2026 annual report describes a new **Boron Oxide facility at Pithampur with a planned capacity of 4,000 MTPA**, "enabling us to move further up the value chain into higher-margin Boron chemistry products", and states an ambition to be a "Boron chemistry company of global relevance".
- **Kronox Lab Sciences** (incorporated 2008, Vadodara, listed 2024) manufactures **high-purity specialty fine chemicals** for diversified end-user industries, across multiple manufacturing units in Gujarat.

Both are inorganic-chemistry businesses selling purified salts; the overlap is real, and the stated logic — export reach and margin — is plausible. Neither company has published a synergy number, and this note does not invent one.

**The measurable fact this filing creates.** Indo Borax has bought 64.26% of a listed company for Rs 246.12 cr. What that stake is worth is not a matter of opinion — Kronox trades, and the BSE bhavcopy prices it:

| | Rs |
|---|---:|
| Kronox close, 29-Sep-2026 | 217.20 |
| Kronox close, 19-Aug-2026 (day before the SPA was announced) | 155.30 |
| SPA price per share | 103.22 |
| SPA price incl. consultancy fees (SAST Reg 8(7)) | 105.87 |

| | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Kronox market cap at today's close (3.7106 cr shares) | 805.9 |
| The 64.26% stake, marked to today's close | 517.9 |
| What Indo Borax paid | 246.12 |
| **Difference** | **+271.8** |
| As a share of Indo Borax's own market cap (Rs 1,572.1 cr) | **+17.3%** |

Against the pre-announcement close of Rs 155.30 the stake is worth Rs 370.4 cr and the gap is Rs 124.3 cr. Either way, **control of Kronox changed hands well below the traded price** — Rs 103.22 against Rs 155.30 the day before the announcement, a 33.5% discount, and against Rs 217.20 today, a 52.5% discount. That is unusual: control normally carries a premium. **Why the sellers accepted it is not explained in any document read this run**, and it is the first thing on the verify list.

**The SPA multiple.** Rs 246.12 cr for 64.26% values Kronox at **Rs 383.0 cr**, which on Kronox's own audited FY2026 numbers is **13.8x PAT** and **3.78x sales**. Kronox's traded multiple, from the BSE header the same day, is **28.21x**.
ideas.model:
**Kronox, from its own BSE results filings** (Rs cr):

| Period | Revenue | PAT | EPS Rs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2025 (Apr-24 to Mar-25) | 100.19 | 25.31 | 6.91 |
| FY2026 (Apr-25 to Mar-26) | 101.22 | 27.66 | 7.51 |
| Q1 FY26 (Jun-25) | 24.29 | 6.28 | 1.70 |
| Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) | 28.39 | 7.30 | 2.00 |

Revenue was **flat** between FY25 and FY26 (+1.0%); PAT grew 9.3% on margin. Q1 FY27 revenue +16.9% YoY, PAT +16.2%. Net margin 27.3% in FY26. Finance cost near zero (Rs 1.14 cr for the full year) — Kronox is effectively debt-free.

**Indo Borax, standalone, from its own filings** (Rs cr):

| Period | Revenue | PAT | Finance cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2025 | 175.26 | 41.88 | n/a |
| FY2026 | 215.45 | 49.74 | 0.66 |
| Q1 FY26 (Jun-25) | 53.57 | 10.04 | 0.00 |
| Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) | 70.36 | 16.26 | 0.49 |

FY26 revenue **+22.9%**, PAT **+18.8%**; Q1 FY27 revenue **+31.3%** YoY, PAT **+62.0%**. FY26 effective tax rate, from the results, **24.4%** (tax Rs 160.70 lacs on PBT Rs 658.10 lacs, as filed in Rs lacs). Finance cost of Rs 0.66 cr on Rs 215 cr of revenue means the company went into this deal **essentially debt-free**, with Rs 14.72 cr of other income in FY26 pointing to a sizeable treasury.

**What the deal adds, and what it costs. Show the arithmetic.**

| Line | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Kronox FY2026 PAT | 27.66 |
| Attributable to Indo Borax at 64.26% | **17.77** |
| Kronox Q1 FY27 PAT annualised, attributable | 18.76 |
| Interest on Rs 225 cr at 8.5% / 9.5% / 10.5% | 19.1 / 21.4 / 23.6 |
| The same after tax at Indo Borax's measured 24.4% rate | **14.4 / 16.2 / 17.8** |
| **Net first-full-year effect on consolidated PAT** | **+3.4 / +1.6 / -0.1** |

**The rate is not disclosed** — the 8.5-10.5% band is an assumption, stated as one. Within it, the acquisition is **roughly earnings-neutral in its first full year**. The purchase price carries an attributable earnings yield of 17.77 / 246.12 = **7.2%**, against an after-tax cost of debt of 6.4-7.9% on the borrowed portion. This is not an accretion story on year-one numbers.

Two further points the arithmetic forces:

- **FY2027 consolidates only half a year.** Completion was 29-Sep-2026, so roughly H2 FY27 carries Kronox. Consolidation brings **100% of Kronox's revenue** (Rs ~101 cr a year) into the top line with **35.74% shown as minority interest** below.
- **The open offer is a second, larger cheque and its price is unknown.** Up to 95,70,000 shares at a SAST-determined price. At the SPA price of Rs 105.87 that is Rs 101.3 cr; at today's traded Rs 217.20 it would be Rs 207.9 cr. **The public announcement stating the offer price was not read this run** (see the X section — a figure circulating there is recorded as unverified). If fully taken up the holding rises to about 90.05%, lifting attributable FY26 PAT to Rs 24.9 cr but adding the funding cost of another Rs 100-200 cr.

**What the study says about a filing like this.** The repo's order study (runbook 144c) measures **order** filings, and this is an acquisition, so its buckets do not apply directly. Two of its findings do:

| Test | Indo Borax |
|---|---|
| Market cap band where 5x runs happened (Rs 300-7,500 cr) | Rs 1,572.1 cr — inside it |
| Volume explosion as evidence | 5.6x the 60-day median today, +2.5% close. The study found 81% of 5x runs had a 10x volume day near the base and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere. It is not evidence |

The deal's size against sales is the honest scale marker: **Rs 246.12 cr paid against Rs 215.45 cr of FY2026 revenue** — the company has spent more than a year's turnover, most of it borrowed, on a single transaction.
ideas.valuation:
**Trailing, measured at the 29-Sep-2026 close of Rs 489.90.**

| | Indo Borax | Kronox (the target) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Close 29-Sep-2026, Rs | 489.90 | 217.20 |
| Shares, cr | 3.209 | 3.711 |
| Market cap, Rs cr | 1,572.1 | 805.9 |
| Trailing 4-quarter PAT, Rs cr | 55.96 | 29.19 |
| Trailing EPS, Rs | 17.44 | 7.70 |
| **Trailing PE** | **28.1** | **28.2** |
| BSE header same day (PE / PB / ROE / NPM) | 28.09 / 5.00 / 17.80 / - | 28.21 / 10.45 / 37.03 / 25.73 |

Our trailing-PAT arithmetic reproduces both BSE headers to the second decimal, which is the check that both share counts are right.

**The two companies trade at the same multiple, and Indo Borax bought control of the other at 13.8x.** That is the whole valuation argument in one line. It does not follow that the market is wrong — a 64.26% stake in a subsidiary is not the same asset as a free float, minority interest sits below the line, and Rs 225 cr of new debt now sits above it.

**A crude sum of the parts**, stated as arithmetic and not as a target:

| | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Indo Borax standalone, at its own trailing PE 28.1 on standalone TTM PAT Rs 55.96 cr | 1,572 |
| Kronox stake at market (64.26% of Rs 805.9 cr) | 518 |
| Less acquisition debt | (225) |
| Less the residual cash paid from own funds (246.12 - 225) | (21) |
| Sum | 1,844 |
| Current market cap | 1,572 |

The Rs 272 cr difference is exactly the mark-to-market gap on the stake, and it assumes the market's own price for Kronox is the right one. If the traded price of Kronox is what the control block is actually worth, the market has not yet marked it into Indo Borax; if the Rs 103.22 the sellers accepted is closer to fair value, there is no gap at all. **This note cannot tell you which, and does not pretend to.**

**Peers.** No peer table was built. BSE classifies Indo Borax under Commodity Chemicals and Kronox under Specialty Chemicals, and the site's industry index for either returns a list too heterogeneous (bulk commodity chemicals against high-purity fine chemicals) to compare multiples honestly from the files read this run.

**Balance sheet.** Before this deal Indo Borax carried essentially no debt (FY26 finance cost Rs 0.66 cr) and meaningful other income (Rs 14.72 cr in FY26). It now carries **Rs 225 cr** of acquisition debt against FY26 PAT of Rs 49.74 cr — about 4.5x one year's standalone profit. The specific balance-sheet lines (cash, borrowings, receivables at 31-Mar-2026) could not be extracted: the annual-report PDF's financial statements are an image-quality scan whose OCR output is unusable for those tables, and this note does not guess at numbers it could not read.

**Ownership, and the fact behind it.** Indo Borax's own promoter holding moved **50.80% (Jun-25, Sep-25, Dec-25) -> 30.80% (Mar-26) -> 38.41% (Jun-26)**. The FY2026 annual report names **Zenrock Chemicals Private Limited** as Acquirer, with India Special Assets Fund III, ISAF III Onshore Fund and Special Situation India Fund as Purchasers, undertaking an open offer for up to 83,43,400 shares (26%) of Indo Borax, and SAST Reg 29(2) disclosures for Zenrock were filed in May 2026 with a post-offer advertisement on 04-May-2026. **Indo Borax itself changed control earlier in 2026**, and the Kronox acquisition is the new owner's first major move. That is the frame the whole idea sits in.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Rs 225 cr of new debt on a company that had none.** FY26 finance cost was Rs 0.66 cr. The lender, the rate and the tenor are all undisclosed. On the 8.5-10.5% band used above, the after-tax interest alone eats between 81% and 100% of the attributable Kronox profit in a full year.
- **The deal is roughly EPS-neutral in year one on the numbers as filed.** The case rests on Kronox growing, on synergies neither company has quantified, and on the debt coming down — none of which is in a document yet.
- **Control bought at a large discount to the traded price, with no explanation on file.** Rs 103.22 against a Rs 155.30 close the day before the SPA and Rs 217.20 today. A control block sold 33-52% below market is an anomaly. Possible readings — an illiquid stock whose screen price is not a clearing price, seller-specific circumstances, terms in the SPA not in the public filing — cannot be told apart from what was read. Treat the Rs 272 cr paper gap with that caveat.
- **The open offer is an unpriced obligation.** Up to Rs 101 cr (at the SPA price) to Rs 208 cr (at today's price) of further cash, and the public announcement was not read this run. How it is funded is unknown.
- **Kronox's revenue was flat FY25 to FY26** (Rs 100.19 cr to Rs 101.22 cr). Profit grew on margin, not volume. Q1 FY27 turned up (+16.9%), one quarter.
- **The sellers stay involved.** The erstwhile promoters keep 9.95% and are paid **consultancy fees** for transition support — fees large enough to move the SAST-computed per-share price from Rs 103.22 to Rs 105.87, i.e. about Rs 6.3 cr in aggregate across 2,38,44,000 shares. A related-party arrangement with departing sellers is worth watching in the FY27 accounts.
- **A change of control in the acquirer itself, eight months old.** Zenrock Chemicals and three funds took control of Indo Borax in H1 2026; promoter holding is 38.41%, down from 50.80% a year ago. New owners doing debt-funded M&A within months is a pattern that can go either way, and there is no track record yet to judge.
- **The stock has already moved:** +113.4% over one year, +102.1% over six months, +28.9% over three months, closing today Rs 24.60 below its 52-week high of Rs 514.50. Volume today 5.6x the 60-day median — an alarm bell, not evidence.
- **No balance sheet, no rating report, no concall.** The annual report's financial statements could not be read (scan quality); no credit-rating filing appears in the 240-day announcement list.
ideas.verify:
1. **The open offer's public announcement and its price.** It determines a cash obligation of roughly Rs 100-208 cr and is filed with the exchanges by the manager to the offer. Reading it — the detailed public statement and the letter of offer — is the single most valuable next step, and it will also state how the offer is being funded (escrow, bank guarantee, the lender).
2. **The terms of the Rs 225 cr facility.** Lender, rate, tenor, security, covenants. The filing gives none of it. A rating rationale on the facility, if one is issued, would carry all of it plus the rating agency's own view of the combined entity's cash flows.
3. **Why the sellers accepted Rs 103.22.** The share purchase agreement is not public, but the letter of offer must set out the negotiated price and the SAST computation, and Kronox's own liquidity (55,296 shares traded today; 12,919 on 19-Aug-2026) may be much of the answer. Whether the screen price of a thinly traded 2024 listing is a clearing price for a control block is exactly the question.
4. **Kronox's plant-level economics.** Multiple units in Gujarat, high-purity fine chemicals, 27% net margin on flat revenue. What its capacity and utilisation are, and whether the Rs 101 cr revenue ceiling is demand or capacity, would need Kronox's own annual report and a site or customer check. None of that was read this run.
ideas.unknowns:
- Open offer price and its funding. Not read.
- Interest rate, tenor, security and lender of the Rs 225 cr facility.
- Indo Borax's balance sheet at 31-Mar-2026 (cash, investments, borrowings, receivables) — the annual report's statements are an unreadable scan.
- Any quantified synergy. Neither company has published one.
- Kronox's capacity, utilisation, customer concentration and export share.
- The aggregate consultancy fee to the selling promoters, its schedule and its accounting treatment. Rs ~6.3 cr is implied by the Rs 103.22 / Rs 105.87 gap across 2,38,44,000 shares; the filing does not state the amount directly.
- Whether the Pithampur 4,000 MTPA Boron Oxide facility is commissioned, and its capex and funding.
- Whether any part of the Rs 246.12 cr was paid in escrow or in tranches before 29-Sep-2026.
ideas.confidence: medium: every number in the trigger - 2,38,44,000 shares, 64.26%, Rs 103.22, Rs 246,11,77,680, Rs 225 cr of debt, completion today - is read field-by-field from Indo Borax's own Reg 30 filings, and both companies' financials come from their own BSE results, so the arithmetic is solid. What keeps it from high is that the two numbers the idea turns on are missing: the open-offer price and the cost of the Rs 225 cr. On the filed numbers the deal is roughly earnings-neutral in year one, and the Rs 272 cr mark-to-market gap rests on a traded price for a thinly held 2024 listing that the selling promoters themselves accepted 52% below.

Against the card: FY27 at ₹255 cr midpoint is +18.4% on FY26; Q1 FY27 was already ₹70.36 cr (+31.3%), so the guidance implies Q2–Q4 of ₹180–190 cr = +11.6–17.8% on the ₹161.88 cr of Q2–Q4 FY26 (215.45 − 53.57). That is slower than the Q1 pace, which management attributes to seasonality.

ideas.thesis:
**The decision, and how we read it.** On 30-Sep-2026 the Union Cabinet approved the **Green Energy Corridor Phase-III** scheme "for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems" (PIB release PRID 2316948, Cabinet). This repo's own `govt.py`, running from GitHub Actions at 18:56 IST that evening, opened the release body and recorded the outlay as **Rs 1,86,405 crore** with decision verb "approves" — the figure is our builder's parse of the PIB body, not a press summary, and it is the one number here traceable to a primary document read by this pipeline.

**What could not be read, and is therefore labelled.** `pib.gov.in` and `pmindia.gov.in` are both blocked by this sandbox's egress proxy, so the release body itself could not be opened this run. A web search of the official release returns a split of **Rs 1,36,378 cr for intra-State transmission and Rs 50,000 cr for 50 GWh of BESS, with Central Financial Support of Rs 54,082 cr, targeted at FY2032-33, enabling evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable energy**. Those sub-figures are a search summary of the official release, not a document we opened, and they do not quite reconcile: 1,36,378 + 50,000 = 1,86,378, against the 1,86,405 our builder read, a Rs 27 cr gap. The note uses the split only as context and flags it as unverified.

**Why this release and not the others.** `govt.py` kept **7 releases on 30-Sep-2026** (4 distinct, each duplicated in the file). Three of the four are not order-book events and the note discards them: MSP for Rabi crops (Rs 8.36 lakh crore), the Rs 5,547.99 cr PSS procurement of pulses and oilseeds, and a Rs 1,789.52 cr Delhi real-time traffic management scheme. The first two are **farmer price support — a household/producer subsidy, which is exactly the shape of PM Surya Ghar, the one basket in this repo's study that UNDERPERFORMED the market (1.8x against 2.0x)**. And the theme mapper tagged both of them "shipbuilding", a plain false positive, so their mapped company lists are meaningless and were ignored. GEC-III is the only one of the four whose money becomes a transmission order book.

**What the business physically does.** Jyoti Structures (incorporated 1974, Mumbai) describes itself in its own press releases as "a leading infrastructure and **power transmission** engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) company". From the FY2025-26 annual report and its own Reg 30 filings:

- Transmission towers are fabricated and galvanised in-house: **Nashik total manufacturing capacity approximately 72,000 MT per annum**, with a second Nashik unit whose stated milestones include "enhanced capability for execution of the prestigious **800 kV HVDC transmission project awarded by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited**". A Raipur factory and an Igatpuri testing station and R&D centre are also disclosed.
- Delivery is documented, not asserted: it filed **completion and commissioning of the 400 kV Gadag-II transmission line in Karnataka** (04-Mar-2026) — an intra-State line, which is the exact asset class GEC-III funds — and **completion and charging of a 400 kV multi-circuit LILO of Pirana (Torrent Power) to Pirana (POWERGRID)** (23-Feb-2026).
- International: a **Sri Lanka power transmission project** (press release 14-May-2026).
- The physical unit that drives revenue is a tonne of fabricated tower steel and a kilometre of line erected. The company publishes capacity in MT but **not utilisation, and not tonnes shipped**, so the tonnage model cannot be closed from the documents.

**The materiality link, in the company's own words.** The FY2026 annual report's outlook section names both components of GEC-III without being asked to: *"Green Energy Corridors, interstate transmission system expansion, smart grid deployment, and modernization of aging transmission assets are expected to generate significant EPC opportunities"*, and separately *"Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and smart grid solutions, which are expected to improve network reliability, operational efficiency and renewable energy integration"*. That is the playbook's test for a government-lane idea — the programme is material to this company by its own disclosure, not merely because it operates in the sector.
ideas.model:
**The order book is the disclosed driver.** From the FY2025-26 annual report, section "Operational Performance and Orders Book":

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Opening order book at 1-Apr-2026 | **Rs 2,274 cr** |
| FY26 total income | Rs 772.44 cr |
| **Order book / FY26 income** | **2.94x** |
| Aggregate total income, Resolution Plan (Nov-2021) to 31-Mar-2026 | Rs 1,974 cr |
| Major FY26 orders: turnkey EPC, 765 kV & 800 kV AC and HVDC lines + 765 kV substations | Rs 639.08 cr |
| Nashik fabrication capacity | ~72,000 MT per annum |

Note the second line against the third: the company has booked **Rs 1,974 cr of income in the four and a half years since its Resolution Plan**, and is carrying an order book of **Rs 2,274 cr**. The book is larger than everything it has billed since emerging from insolvency.

**Measured results.** From the BSE detailed-results feed and the company's own results press releases (standalone):

| Period | Total income Rs cr | EBITDA Rs cr | EBITDA % | PBT Rs cr | Net profit Rs cr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2024-25 | 504.50 | 44.28 | 8.78 | 35.66 | 35.81 |
| FY2025-26 | 772.44 | 69.97 | 9.06 | 54.72 | 56.04 |
| **Growth** | **+53.1%** | **+58.0%** | +28 bps | **+53.4%** | **+56.5%** |
| Q1 FY2025-26 | 162.40 | 13.14 | 8.09 | 10.24 | 11.16 |
| **Q1 FY2026-27** | **255.18** | **24.97** | **9.79** | **19.27** | **19.46** |
| **Growth** | **+57.1%** | **+90.0%** | **+169 bps** | **+88.2%** | **+74.4%** |

Revenue from operations (excluding other income) grew from Rs 156.16 cr to **Rs 251.46 cr, +61.0% YoY** in Q1 FY27. Margin is expanding at the same time as revenue, which is the combination the repo's earnings study found in 73.9% of its 5x runs (profit doubling) against 8.8% of the also-rans.

**One accounting feature to understand before reading the EPS.** Net profit **exceeds** PBT in both FY26 (Rs 56.04 cr vs Rs 54.72 cr) and Q1 FY27 (Rs 19.46 cr vs Rs 19.27 cr). A company that emerged from insolvency carries accumulated losses, so cash tax is minimal and a deferred-tax credit can push reported PAT above PBT. **This means the headline earnings are not fully taxed earnings**, and a normalised tax rate would cut them materially. No document read this run states the remaining carried-forward loss, so the size of that cushion is unknown.

**Forward revenue, from the disclosed book.** Rs 2,274 cr of order book against a Q1 FY27 run-rate of Rs 255.18 cr a quarter (Rs 1,021 cr annualised) is **2.2 years of work at the current pace**. Three arithmetic cases, with the quarterly run-rate held or grown:

| Sequential growth | FY27 total income Rs cr | Net profit at 7.0% | Net profit at 7.6% | EPS at 7.6% Rs | PE at Rs 8.91 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% (Q1 run-rate held) | 1,021 | 71.5 | 77.6 | 0.65 | 13.7 |
| +5% a quarter | 1,100 | 77.0 | 83.6 | 0.70 | 12.7 |
| +10% a quarter | 1,184 | 82.9 | 90.0 | 0.75 | 11.8 |

The 7.0-7.6% net margin band is the measured FY26 (7.26% of total income) and Q1 FY27 (7.63%) outcome and is an assumption carried forward, **not guidance — the company issues none in any document read this run**. Share count 119.365 cr (1,193,651,437 shares, from the 30-Jun-2026 shareholding filing). These cases assume the same lightly-taxed profit; they are not normalised.

**What the order study says about this name.** Jyoti filed **5 order-type disclosures in the 760 days to 2026-09-24** (23-Jan-2025 PowerGrid notification of award, then "Intimation on New Project Order" on 25-Feb-2025, 15-Oct-2025, 30-Mar-2026 and 13-May-2026; BSE read complete, 158 filings). The study measured the two ends: a company filing its **first** order in two years reached 2x 30.4% of the time and 5x 3.5%; one with **8 or more** prior filings reached 2x 17.3% and 5x **never**. Five puts Jyoti between the measured extremes, and the study gives no bucket for exactly five — so the honest statement is that it is neither the rare filer the study rewards nor the serial bidder it penalises. Market cap Rs 1,063.5 cr sits inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where every 5x run in three years occurred.

Our arithmetic and BSE's header agree to within a rounding step, which is the check that the 119.365 cr share count is right.

**PB of 6.96 against ROE of 42.10 is the tension in this name.** Both are BSE's own header figures for 2026-10-04. A 42% return on equity on a post-insolvency balance sheet reflects a very small equity base relative to the revenue it turns, not a durable franchise return — and it is the same lightly-taxed profit noted above. The book value this PB is measured against is small for the same reason.

**The re-rating case, in one sentence.** The stock is 41% lower than a year ago while total income grew 53% and the order book is 2.9x revenue; if the Rs 2,274 cr book converts at the Q1 FY27 margin the trailing 17x becomes roughly 12-14x forward, and GEC-III adds Rs 1.36 lakh crore of intra-State transmission tendering to the pipeline it bids into.

**Peers: not available.** The site's industry index for "Heavy Electrical Equipment" returned Kamdhenu, Commercial Syn Bags, Nelcast, Hariom Pipe, Bharat Wire Ropes, GRP, R M Drip and Borosil Scientific — companies matched by market cap, not by business. **No honest peer multiple table could be built from the files read this run**, and the note does not invent one. The listed transmission-EPC comparables (KEC International, Kalpataru, Transrail, Skipper, Bajel) sit outside the Rs 200-2,000 cr universe and were not priced this run.

**Balance sheet.** The FY26 annual report names "non-fund-based limits, working capital management" first in its risk list, and the company filed an initial disclosure as a **"Large Corporate"** (14-Apr-2026), the SEBI category for entities with substantial outstanding long-term borrowing. A **Rights Issue II** was in progress in June 2026, with monitoring-agency reports filed for the quarter ended 31-Mar-2026 and again on 04-Aug-2026. **The specific debt, cash and receivable figures at 31-Mar-2026 were not extracted this run** and are listed under unknowns rather than estimated.

**Ownership - the single most unusual fact here, and a correction.** The dossier builder reported "promoter 100.0%" for every quarter. **That is a parser error and it is wrong.** Reading the 30-Jun-2026 shareholding XBRL page directly, the row the regex matched is **"(B) Public — 201,951 holders, 1,193,651,437 shares, 100.00%"**. Jyoti Structures has **no promoter**: the float is 100% public across 201,951 shareholders, with 8,500 shares (0.00%) in the non-promoter-non-public category. The Resolution Plan extinguished the former promoter group. Two consequences the note takes seriously: there is **no promoter skin in the game**, and the study's "promoter stake rose" signal (present in 15.2% of 5x runs) is structurally unavailable for this company. One block of **3,00,00,000 shares = 2.51%** appears in the same filing; the holder's identity is not established from any primary document read this run.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Lenders have taken the company to the NCLAT in contempt proceedings.** On 27-Feb-2026 Jyoti filed an "Intimation regarding appeal filed by lenders before NCLAT in contempt proceedings relating to disbursement of **non-fund-based limits**". For a transmission EPC contractor, non-fund-based limits are bank guarantees — the instrument required to bid and to draw advances. A dispute with lenders over their disbursement is close to existential for the order book, and it is the single biggest reason this idea is not high confidence. Further NCLT/NCLAT directions were filed on 18-Feb-2026 and 27-May-2026.
- **No promoter.** 100% public float, post-insolvency. Nobody is underwriting the equity, and there is no promoter whose buying would signal anything.
- **Earnings are not fully taxed.** Net profit exceeds PBT in both FY26 and Q1 FY27. The accumulated-loss cushion from insolvency is not quantified in anything read this run; when it runs out, reported EPS falls at a normalised rate even if operations are unchanged.
- **Governance churn in a single quarter.** The Chief Executive Officer **resigned** (29-May-2026); the Chairman and Independent Director **died** (17-Jul-2026); an internal auditor, Bhushan Khot & Co, was **appointed on 30-Apr-2026 and removed on 04-Aug-2026**, having been appointed on the same day as a second internal auditor (K N B J & Associates); and a **corrigendum to the FY2025-26 Annual Report** was filed on 27-Jul-2026. Each is individually explainable; together, in four months, they are a pattern worth weighing.
- **Dilution in progress.** Rights Issue II was live in June 2026 with monitoring-agency reporting. The share count used in this note (119.365 cr, at 30-Jun-2026) may already be stale, and the EPS cases above would scale down accordingly. The issue's size, price and utilisation were not read this run.
- **Thin trading.** Median 60-day turnover Rs 31.9 lakh on a Rs 1,063 cr company; 408,920 shares traded on 2026-10-01. A single-digit share price with this float makes the quoted price easy to move and hard to transact in size.
- **GEC-III is an opportunity to bid, not an order.** The scheme runs to FY2032-33 and is implemented by State transmission utilities, which tender separately. Nothing in it is Jyoti's until a State utility awards it, and the repo's own study found the baskets' bases came **months** after the policy date — the defence names bottomed between September and November 2020. There is no reason to treat 30-Sep-2026 as a starting gun.
- **The transmission basket's measured history is the weakest of the strong ones.** 47 companies from the FY23 capex cycle, median 4.7x against 3.0x for the market, 49% made 5x — real outperformance, but a fraction of defence (17.4x) or RDSS smart meters (12.0x). And nearly every winner in every basket is now 30-90% below its peak.
- **No concall, no investor presentation, no credit-rating report** appears in the 240-day filing list. The only management narrative is a one-page results press release, which is company-written.
- **The 2.51% block is unattributed.** A named investor would be a data point; an unidentified 3 crore-share holder is not.

1. **The NCLAT non-fund-based-limits proceeding.** Its current status and what the lenders are actually withholding is the one fact that most changes this idea. The NCLAT order itself, and the contingent-liability and "going concern"/emphasis-of-matter notes in the FY26 audited accounts, would settle it. Neither was read this run.
2. **The remaining carried-forward tax loss.** It determines whether reported EPS is repeatable. It sits in the tax note of the FY26 financial statements.

ideas.confidence: low: the government decision is real and large, and the materiality link is unusually clean - Jyoti's own annual report names Green Energy Corridors and BESS as its demand drivers, it has commissioned an intra-State 400 kV line, and it carries a disclosed Rs 2,274 cr order book that is 2.9x FY26 income while the stock is 41% below a year ago. What holds this at low rather than medium is not the thesis but the balance sheet and the register: lenders are at the NCLAT in contempt proceedings over the non-fund-based limits an EPC contractor cannot bid without, the company has no promoter at all, reported profit exceeds PBT because insolvency losses shelter it, a rights issue is diluting, and the CEO left, the chairman died and an internal auditor was removed inside four months.

ideas.trigger: govt: Green Energy Corridor Phase-III - the Cabinet approved GEC-III on 30-Sep-2026, outlay Rs 1,86,405 cr as parsed from the PIB body by our own govt.py, covering intra-State transmission AND Battery Energy Storage. ideas.thesis:
**Two things happened on 30-Sep-2026** and only together do they make an idea. The Cabinet approved **Green Energy Corridor Phase-III** — outlay **Rs 1,86,405 crore** as read from the PIB release body by this repo's `govt.py` — a scheme whose own title is "Development of Intra-State Transmission System **with Battery Energy Storage Systems**". And Solarworld filed a Reg 30 disclosure that its wholly owned subsidiary had received a purchase order for solar panels. The order is small. The BESS franchise behind it is not.

**The order, read.** From the filing (BSE, 30-Sep-2026 13:28 IST; event occurred 29-Sep-2026 18:06): **ZNShine Solarworld Private Limited**, a wholly owned subsidiary, received a purchase order from "a leading renewable energy player" (unnamed, domestic) for **96,000 solar panels, model G12R 625 Wp, at a unit price of Rs 7,812.50**, giving a **basic order value of Rs 75.00 crore and a total of Rs 78.75 crore including 5% IGST**. No execution period is stated beyond "as per terms and conditions mentioned in purchase order". Not a related-party transaction.

That filing is unusually complete, and it closes a physical model exactly:

| Step | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---:|
| Panels x wattage | 96,000 x 625 Wp | **60.0 MW** |
| Basic value / MW | Rs 75.00 cr / 60 MW | **Rs 1.25 cr per MW** |
| Playbook constant for non-DCR modules | — | Rs 1.3 cr per MW |

The realised price lands within 4% of the conversion constant this playbook carries for non-DCR modules — an independent check that the order is priced like a normal third-party module sale, not an inflated related-party print.

**Why the module order matters qualitatively more than Rs 78.75 cr suggests.** The FY2025-26 annual report discloses a **1.552 GW TOPCon module manufacturing facility commissioned at Roorkee, Uttarakhand, "producing high-efficiency modules of 600W-750W across the M10R, G12R and G12 formats"**. The order is for **G12R 625 Wp** — the exact format from that plant. The annual report also records ZNShine Solarworld as a wholly owned subsidiary transacting "sale of goods or materials" with the parent "pursuant to the Company's strategic backward integration initiative". So this is the step from captive backward integration to a **third-party module sale**, which is what turns a cost centre into a revenue line.

**What the business physically does** (all from the FY2025-26 annual report's own key-highlights page):

| Metric | Disclosed figure |
|---|---|
| Solar and renewable projects executed / under execution | 60+ |
| EPC portfolio installed | 348 MW DC |
| Ongoing solar EPC capacity | 1,809 MW DC |
| Module manufacturing (Roorkee, TOPCon) | 1.552 GW |
| Junction box manufacturing | 5 GW |
| **Ongoing BESS capacity** | **1,164 MWh** |
| BESS manufacturing facility | 3.4 GW |
| Solar cell facility | 2.4 GW "under development with proposed JV, targeted for commissioning by June 2027" |
| FY26 total income | Rs 14,160 mn (Rs 1,416 cr), up 157% YoY |
| FY26 PAT | Rs 1,204 mn (Rs 120.4 cr), up 56% YoY |

**The BESS franchise, from its own Reg 30 filings.** This is the part that connects to GEC-III, and every row is read from the filing itself:

| Filed | Awarding entity | Site | Capacity | Order value (excl. taxes) | Rs cr per MWh |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 2026-03-29 | NTPC Limited | Solapur Super TPS, Lot-1 | 132 MW / 264 MWh | 314.26 | 1.19 |
| 2026-03-30 | NTPC Limited | Solapur Super TPS, Lot-2 | 75 MW / 150 MWh | 176.91 | 1.18 |
| 2026-03-30 | NTPC Limited | Feroze Gandhi Unchahar TPS, Lot-2 | 50 MW / 100 MWh | 108.22 | 1.08 |
| | | **Total** | **257 MW / 514 MWh** | **599.39** | **1.17 avg** |

All three are BESS Engineering, Procurement and Construction, 15 months to completion of facilities, same bid document CS-0011-171B-9. **The annual report independently states "BESS EPC orders worth Rs 5.99 billion for NTPC's Solapur and Unchahar thermal power station projects"** — Rs 599 cr, against the Rs 599.39 cr sum of the three individual filings. The two sources agree, which is the check that nothing is double-counted.

Separately, a **Balance of System package for Block-IX (200 MWac)** of a 1,000 MW grid-connected solar PV project at Bikaner, Rajasthan, from **NTPC Renewable Energy Limited**, with three years of O&M, 19 months (filed 01-Apr-2026). The filing's size field states only "200 MWac"; the annual report prices it at **Rs 2.35 billion (Rs 235 cr)**.

**The GEC-III cross-check, and its limit.** GEC-III provides, per the search summary of the official release, **Rs 50,000 crore for 50 GWh of BESS** — an implied **Rs 1.00 cr per MWh**. Solarworld's three realised NTPC awards price at **Rs 1.08-1.19 cr per MWh**. The government's implied rate and this company's realised rate are within 17% of each other, which says the scheme is budgeted at something like the price at which this company actually builds. Its 514 MWh of awarded work is **1.03% of the 50 GWh** the scheme funds, and its 1,164 MWh of ongoing BESS capacity is 2.33%. **That is arithmetic about scale, not a forecast of market share** — nothing entitles this company to any share of a scheme whose tenders have not been issued.

**Measured results** (BSE detailed-results feed, standalone; the annual report's consolidated figures differ and are given separately):

| Period | Revenue Rs cr | Other income | Total income | PAT Rs cr | PAT / total income |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY2025-26 (Jun-25) | 68.31 | 13.74 | 82.05 | 16.57 | 20.2% |

| **FY2025-26** | **1,202.00** | 50.71 | 1,252.72 | **132.67** | 10.6% |
| **Q1 FY2026-27 (Jun-26)** | **143.96** | 13.23 | **157.19** | **16.22** | **10.3%** |

Q1 FY27 revenue is **+110.8% YoY** on Q1 FY26's Rs 68.31 cr — but PAT is **-2.1%**, Rs 16.22 cr against Rs 16.57 cr, because the margin on total income **halved from 20.2% to 10.3%**. Read the quarterly column before reading the growth rate: revenue runs 68 / 127 / 495 / 512 / 144 across five quarters. That is EPC percentage-of-completion recognition, and it means **no single quarter of this company tells you anything about a run-rate.** The annual figures are the only honest base.

**Order book and visibility** (FY2025-26 annual report):

| Component | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Solar EPC and O&M projects | 1,674 |
| EPC and BESS IPP-related projects | 1,139 |
| **Total order book** | **2,813** |
| FY26 total income (consolidated, per AR) | 1,416 |
| **Order book / FY26 total income** | **1.99x** |
| Order book / market cap | **2.58x** |

**Forward revenue, three cases.** Rs 2,813 cr of book, with the BESS packages contracted at 15 months and the BOS package at 19 months, implies the bulk converts across FY27 and FY28. Taking FY26 total income of Rs 1,416 cr as the base:

| FY27 revenue growth | FY27 total income Rs cr | PAT at 9.4% | PAT at 10.6% | EPS at 10.6% Rs | PE at Rs 125.90 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% | 1,416 | 133.1 | 150.1 | 17.32 | 7.3 |
| +20% | 1,699 | 159.7 | 180.1 | 20.78 | 6.1 |
| -20% | 1,133 | 106.5 | 120.1 | 13.86 | 9.1 |

The 9.4-10.6% margin band is the measured Q4 FY26 and FY26 outcome. **The company issues no revenue or margin guidance in any document read this run**, so all three columns are arithmetic on stated history, not forecasts. Share count 8.667 cr (market cap Rs 1,091.2 cr / close Rs 125.90, cross-checked below). Note the **-20% case still prints a single-digit PE**, which is the point of the valuation section.

**What the order study says about the trigger filing.** The Rs 78.75 cr purchase order is **6.6% of FY26 standalone revenue (Rs 1,202 cr), 5.6% of consolidated total income (Rs 1,416 cr), and 2.8% of the order book**. The study measured order size against a trailing year of sales: **under 10% of sales reached 2x within two years 21.4% of the time, against 35.7% for the 25-50% bucket.** So on the one dimension the study found predictive, **this order sits in the weakest bucket.** It is the trigger that put the name on the list, not the reason to look at it.

On rarity it does better: **7 order-type filings in the 760 days to 2026-10-01** (BSE read complete, 117 filings) — below the 8-or-more threshold at which the study found 2x odds of 17.3% and **no 5x at all**. Market cap Rs 1,091.2 cr sits inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where every measured 5x run occurred.

| | Solarworld |
|---|---:|
| Market cap | Rs 1,091.2 cr |

| Returns 1m / 3m / 6m / 1y | -13.2% / -32.0% / -27.5% / **-62.2%** |

Our trailing EPS of Rs 15.27 reproduces BSE's header **exactly**, which is the check that the 8.667 cr share count is right.

**The whole valuation argument in three lines.** A company with Rs 2,813 cr of disclosed order book, Rs 845 cr of net worth, 0.3x debt-to-equity and Rs 132 cr of trailing profit is quoted at **Rs 1,091 cr — 8.2x trailing earnings and 1.29x book**, at its 52-week low, having fallen 62% in a year. Either the market is pricing the de-rating of an IPO that came too expensive, or it is pricing something about the earnings that this note has found part of (see red flags), or both.

**Why the stock fell 62%: the part that is measurable.** The share was listed in **September 2025** (X search results give an IPO price band of Rs 333-351 and a Rs 490 cr issue; the prospectus was not read this run, so treat the band as unverified). The 52-week high of Rs 338.70 is consistent with a listing near that band. At Rs 125.90 the stock is **62.8% below its 52-week high**. A substantial part of the fall is therefore the de-rating of a 2025 listing rather than a deterioration disclosed quarter by quarter — but the margin halving in Q1 FY27 and the dispute awards below are disclosed deteriorations, and both post-date the listing.

**Peers: not built.** BSE classifies Solarworld under "Civil Construction", which mixes it with road and building contractors that share none of its economics. The comparable listed solar-EPC and BESS names (Sterling & Wilson, Waaree, Premier Energies, KPI Green) sit outside the Rs 200-2,000 cr universe and were not priced this run. **No honest peer multiple table could be built from the files read**, and the note does not invent one.

**Ownership.** Promoter holding **65.77%** at both 31-Mar-2026 and 30-Jun-2026, from 65.67% at 31-Dec-2025 — stable to marginally rising, no pledge disclosed in anything read this run. Managing Director Kartik Teltia (DIN 06610105) signs the Reg 30 filings personally.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Rs 219.33 crore of claims against a client, of which only 18.4% was admitted.** On 18-Sep-2026 Solarworld disclosed the outcome of two Dispute Adjudication Board proceedings it had **itself invoked** against **SJVN Green Energy Limited** on the GUVNL Phase XIII (100 MW) and Phase XIV (260 MW) solar EPC contracts at Mothara, Kutch:

| Case | Claim heads | Claimed Rs cr | Awarded Rs cr | % admitted | of which cash |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 MW (DAB/100MW/01/2026) | 12 | 56.51 | 13.77 | 24.4% | 5.79 |
| 260 MW (DAB/260MW/01/2026) | 8 | 162.83 | 26.50 | 16.3% | 2.09 |
| **Total** | 20 | **219.33** | **40.27** | **18.4%** | **7.88** |

  The claim heads are the diagnostic: *release of retention monies, overdue supply invoices, delay financing interest, site preservation and module insurance costs, loss of profit*. That is a working-capital dispute, and Rs 219 cr of it on a company with Rs 1,202-1,416 cr of annual revenue. Most of what was awarded is **retention released against bank-guarantee or surety-bond substitution, not cash** — Rs 32.39 cr of the Rs 40.27 cr. This is the single most important thing found this run and it is not in any press summary.
- **Margin halved in the latest quarter.** PAT fell to 10.3% of total income in Q1 FY27 from 20.2% a year earlier, with revenue up 110.8%. Whether that is mix (module supply at lower margin than EPC), the dispute provisions, or price competition in solar EPC is **not explained in any document read this run.**
- **The trigger order is in the weakest bucket the study measured.** Rs 78.75 cr is 5.6-6.6% of a year's sales — the under-10% bucket, 21.4% odds of a 2x against 35.7% for a 25-50% order.
- **The customer is unnamed.** "A leading renewable energy player". No concentration, credit or terms assessment is possible, and the execution period is not stated at all.
- **Interest coverage has moderated.** The annual report states the ratio moderated "consequent to increased borrowings to support project execution, manufacturing expansion and business growth". Debt-to-equity of 0.3x is comfortable in isolation; the direction is the point, and the absolute debt figure was not extracted this run.
- **Revenue is violently lumpy.** 68 / 127 / 495 / 512 / 144 across five quarters. Any growth rate quoted off one quarter is noise, and a reader who annualises Q1 FY27 gets Rs 629 cr against FY26's Rs 1,416 cr.
- **The 2.4 GW cell plant is a proposal, not a project.** The annual report says "under development **with proposed JV**, targeted for commissioning by June 2027". A proposed JV has no partner named and no signed agreement disclosed in anything read this run.
- **A 2025 listing at its all-time low.** Down 62.2% in a year, closing exactly at the 52-week low of Rs 125.90. Nothing in the price action suggests a base has formed; the repo's own study found winners' bases came months after their trigger and that nearly every past winner is now 30-90% below its peak.
- **GEC-III is not an order.** 50 GWh of BESS is a budget line to FY2032-33, tendered by State utilities and agencies that have issued nothing yet. Solarworld's claim on it is a track record, not a contract.
- **Thin trading.** Median 60-day turnover Rs 27.3 lakh; 46,466 shares on 2026-10-01.
