updates.body:
The card said no guidance was found. The Q4 FY26 earnings-call transcript (call 26-May-2026, filed 2-Jun-2026, before the card but not read for it) has it: 'my order book currently stands at about INR2800 crores. We hope to continue and achieve maybe 70%, 70%, 75% of this order book in the current year'; later, 'we would bare minimum try to achieve about 70% of that. So maybe close to INR2,000 crores in the current — in FY27'. Execution windows stated: BESS EPC 11–12 months, solar EPC 14 months. Margins: 'if the war situation subsides, we are hoping to maybe carry on our current margins'.

Against the card's model: ₹1,960–2,100 cr (70–75% of 2,800) is **+38% to +48% on FY26 consolidated total income of ₹1,416 cr** — above the card's +20% top case. At the card's measured 9.4–10.6% margin that is PAT of ₹184–223 cr, EPS ₹21.3–25.7 on 8.667 cr shares, 4.9–5.9x at ₹125.90. The card's caution stands: the quarterly series (68/127/495/512/144) shows how lumpy percentage-of-completion revenue is, and Q1 FY27 was only ₹157 cr of total income.

updates.title: AGM approves swapping the 1.2 GW Pandhurana cell project for a 2.4 GW plant at Rays Green, plus higher borrowing limits
updates.body:
13th AGM voting results (filed 1-Oct-2026): all seven resolutions passed. The four special resolutions: enhancement of borrowing limits under s.180(1)(c), creation of charges under s.180(1)(a), higher s.186 investment/loan/guarantee limits, and **variation of the IPO objects** (item 7). Against-votes were 132–175 shares per resolution; the promoter's 5,70,22,385 shares voted for everything except the re-appointment of Mangal Chand Teltia (father of the MD), where they abstained; public non-institution turnout was 31.6% of 2.34 cr shares.

What item 7 changes (AGM notice, figures the notice gives in ₹ million):

| | Pandhurana project (prospectus) | New project (approved) |
|---|---|---|
| Capacity | 1.2 GW TOPCon cell line, Pandhurana MP, via subsidiary Kartik Solarworld | 2.4 GW n-type TOPCon G12R cell plant, via **Rays Green** on MPIDC-leased land (lease 4-Mar-2025) |
| Total cost | ₹575.30 cr | **₹1,000 cr** |
| From IPO proceeds | ₹420 cr | ₹420 cr of unutilised proceeds: ₹100 cr equity in Rays Green + ₹320 cr loan to it |
| Other funding | — | ₹100 cr from Rays Power Infra Ltd; debt ₹480 cr (Bhadani Financers ₹230 cr sanction 15-Jul-2026, Bank of Maharashtra ₹250 cr sanction 30-May-2026) |
| Commercial production | — | June 2027 (P&M Oct-2026 to May-2027) |

So the 'proposed JV' the card could not name is Rays Green, co-funded by Rays Power Infra Ltd; the card's unknown on the partner is answered. The notice says the land is 'relatively flat', construction has begun, consent to establish is in hand and power is at a subsidised ~₹4.30/unit. Two things the reader should hold: (1) ₹320 cr of IPO money becomes a **loan to Rays Green**, not Solarworld's own asset, and the notice does not state Solarworld's resulting shareholding in Rays Green; (2) the Q1 FY27 presentation of 14-Aug-2026 still describes a '1.2 GW solar cell facility … June 2027'. With 132 shares against, the 10%-dissent exit-offer trigger described in the notice does not arise.

ideas.name: Manaksia Steels Ltd
ideas.industry: Iron & Steel — coated flat steel (GP, Alu-Zinc/Galvalume, colour-coated, CR), Haldia WB; Nigerian long-steel subsidiary
ideas.trigger: deep: deep-dive on request — Kolkata coated-steel maker; FY26 standalone revenue ₹1,053 cr (+80%) after a new 1.1 lakh-TPA Alu-Zinc line; Q1 FY27 PAT ₹22.4 cr (+253%) at 10.8% EBITDA margin; stock ₹46.55 (Mar-26) → ₹108.89; ~20% of sales and 63% of receivables are with promoter-family entities, mainly in Nigeria
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **Which company:** *Manaksia Steels Ltd* — NSE **MANAKSTEEL**, BSE **539044**, ISIN INE824Q01011, face value ₹1, 6,55,34,050 shares. It is one of the companies created when the old Manaksia Ltd was split up (the split took effect on 1-Oct-2013 and the Calcutta High Court approved it on 24-Mar-2014). Three listed sister companies are separate businesses: **Manaksia Ltd** (532932 / MANAKSIA; packaging, metals and Nigerian subsidiaries, ₹382 cr), **Manaksia Coated Metals & Industries** (539046 / MANAKCOAT; also makes coated steel, ₹1,350 cr) and **Manaksia Aluminium** (539045 / MANAKALUCO, ₹221 cr). Market caps are from the BSE scrip master of 5-Oct.
- **What it makes:** coated flat steel at Haldia port in West Bengal. Products are galvanised (GP), aluminium-zinc coated (Galvalume) and pre-painted colour-coated coils and sheets, plus cold-rolled coil, mainly for roofing and construction. Brands: Austrang, 5 Star Super Colour, 5 Star Superlume and 5 Star Super Sakti. A 100% Nigerian subsidiary, Federated Steel Mills, makes TMT bars and welding electrodes.
- **The step-up is real:** a ₹85 cr Alu-Zinc line (110,200 TPA) started commercial production in June 2025. Sales volume went from about 70,000 t to 124,000 t, and standalone revenue from ₹584 cr (FY25) to **₹1,053 cr (FY26, +80%)**. Steel prices then rose (Mumbai HR coil ₹54,760/t in Dec-25 → ₹71,990/t in Apr-26, Ministry of Steel), and EBITDA margin excluding other income jumped from ~5% to **11.8% in Q4 FY26 and 10.8% in Q1 FY27**. Q1 FY27 PAT was ₹22.38 cr, against ₹38.17 cr for the whole of FY26.
- **What the market pays:** at ₹108.89 (NSE close, 1-Oct-2026) the market cap is **₹714 cr**. That is **13.2x trailing standalone EPS** (₹8.27), 12.7x consolidated, 8.3x trailing EV/EBITDA and 2.1x book. The stock was ₹46.55 in Mar-2026, so it has more than doubled.
- **What a careful reader must weigh:** **about a fifth of revenue goes to companies controlled by the promoter family** (₹205 cr in FY26). Most of that is raw material, not coated steel: hot-rolled coil to Sumo Steels in Nigeria (owned through the promoters' private company Vajra Machineries; negative net worth of ₹23.5 cr at FY25) and aluminium and other inputs to MINL Nigeria. These related parties owe **63% of all trade receivables** and take about 72 days to pay, against about 10 days for everyone else. Shareholders have approved up to **₹600 cr** of such sales for FY27 (57% of FY26 revenue), with trade advances of up to 365 days allowed. Exports were 19% of revenue, and roughly 84% of that appears to be these two Nigerian related parties (arithmetic below).
- **Other points:** promoters hold 74.75% (the legal maximum) with no pledge. There are **no mutual funds or FPIs**, no earnings calls and no investor deck. Shares trade in the trade-for-trade segment (NSE series BE, BSE group T), and median BSE turnover is about ₹3.5 lakh a day. In June 2026 the company dropped CARE (which had reaffirmed A-/A2+ on 20-May-2026) and took an ICRA A/A1 rating; the annual report calls this an "upgrade".

### 1. Business and capacity (Haldia; per the 10-Aug-2026 Reg-30 filing)
| Line | Existing TPA | Utilisation (Aug-26) | Phase I add (by FY30, ₹375 cr) | Phase II add (by FY34, ₹425 cr + land) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cold-rolled (CR) | 80,000 | ~86% | +95,000 | +1,00,000 |
| Coated GL/GP (galvanised + Alu-Zinc) | 1,44,200 | ~75% | +31,000 | +1,00,000 |
| Colour-coated (CC) | 60,000 | ~100% | +90,000 (CCL-II, under erection) | +90,000 |

- The Alu-Zinc line (1,10,200 TPA) ran at ~90% in Q1 FY27, per the MD's statement. The existing colour line was raised from 48,000 to 60,000 TPA in FY26. CCL-II (~₹40 cr, ~90,000 TPA) was due "FY26" (the Aug-2025 forum post and the FY25 AR) and is now due in "FY27".
- **The capacity figures conflict:** the 25-Mar-2026 filing gave existing CR capacity as **1,20,000 TPA at ~82%**, with a 2,50,000 TPA addition (total 3,70,000) for **₹100 cr**. The 10-Aug-2026 filing gives **80,000 TPA at ~86%**, with +95,000 in Phase I. The company has not reconciled the two.
- **Product mix in FY26:** colour-coated 52.89% of *manufacturing* turnover, galvanised 21.75%, Alu-Zinc 13.92%. The CFO section, on *total* revenue, gives colour-coated 42.41% and galvanised 17.44%. **Exports:** 19% of revenue (23% in FY25), to Bhutan, Nigeria, UAE, Madagascar, Portugal, Romania and Ghana. East India was 56.4% of domestic sales (67.4% in FY25).
- **Realisation:** colour-coated about ₹76,000/t and GP/Alu-Zinc about ₹77,800/t (FY26 averages). Revenue ÷ the 124,000 t sold = ₹84,935/t, higher than both, which fits with ~₹205 cr of related-party sales of raw material in the revenue. Excluding them gives ₹68,402/t. How much of the tonnage is traded HR coil is **not disclosed**.
- **Guidance (FY26 AR, MD and CFO):** consolidated revenue of **₹1,500 cr in FY27** and **about ₹3,000 cr in FY29** after the cold-rolling mill (now Dec-2027). Funding is "debt and internal accruals". The company has asked West Bengal for incentives, and the timing of the ₹800 cr plan depends on that answer.

### 2. Standalone financials, FY20 → FY26 (audited; ₹ cr; EBITDA excludes other income, my arithmetic)
| | FY20 | FY21 | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 487.80 | 387.96 | 504.52 | 641.48 | 631.96 | 584.18 | **1,053.19** |
| Growth | — | −20.5% | +30.0% | +27.1% | −1.5% | −7.6% | **+80.3%** |
| Other income | 2.82 | 6.02 | 8.23 | 7.23 | 15.63 | 13.64 | 4.32 |
| EBITDA ex-OI | 14.38 | 27.73 | 38.80 | 17.07 | 32.44 | 12.05 | **72.24** |
| EBITDA margin | 2.95% | 7.15% | 7.69% | 2.66% | 5.13% | 2.06% | **6.86%** |
| PAT | 8.70 | 19.68 | 29.56 | 12.65 | 30.22* | 11.70 | **38.17** |
| PAT margin | 1.78% | 5.07% | 5.86% | 1.97% | 4.78% | 2.00% | 3.62% |
| EPS (₹) | 1.33 | 3.00 | 4.51 | 1.93 | 4.61 | 1.79 | 5.82 |
| ROE (PAT/closing NW) | 4.5% | 9.0% | 11.5% | 4.5% | 9.8% | 3.8% | 11.3% |

*FY24 PBT includes a ₹2.85 cr exceptional gain and ₹15.63 cr of other income (₹12.59 cr of it gains on investments). FY25 other income of ₹13.64 cr included a ₹7.14 cr gain from liquidating the UAE subsidiary Technomet FZE. **In FY24 and FY25 most of the profit came from treasury income, not from steel.**

### 3. Balance sheet and cash (standalone, ₹ cr, 31-Mar)
| | FY20 | FY21 | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Borrowings (all short-term since FY23) | 40.43 | 62.91 | 7.35 | 45.45 | 182.90 | 203.65 | **149.18** |
| Current investments | 2.78 | 3.85 | 22.23 | 86.35 | 145.67 | 104.92 | 68.65 |
| Cash & equivalents | 22.82 | 6.55 | 7.18 | 4.86 | 2.01 | 7.97 | 2.92 |
| Net worth | 193.25 | 218.66 | 257.46 | 281.87 | 308.97 | 306.17 | 338.95 |
| Receivable days (year-end, on revenue) | 32 | 16 | 14 | 9 | 15 | 24 | 22 |
| Inventory days (year-end, on revenue) | 65 | 75 | 59 | 53 | 78 | 83 | 51 |
| Operating cash flow | −5.98 | 34.17 | −1.96 | 29.23 | −49.42 | 13.18 | **62.07** |
| Capex | 3.03 | 0.33 | 6.90 | 8.22 | 38.71 | 68.92 | 37.40 |
| Free cash flow | −9.01 | 33.84 | −8.86 | 21.00 | −88.13 | −55.74 | 24.66 |

- **Seven years in total:** PAT ₹150.7 cr, operating cash flow ₹81.3 cr (54% of PAT), capex ₹163.5 cr. Capex was paid for by running down treasury investments and by short-term debt. The AR's claim of capex funded "entirely through internal accruals without any long-term debt" is true only in the narrow sense that no *term* loan was taken.
- **FY26 operating cash flow of ₹62 cr was helped by suppliers and customers:** trade payables rose from ₹19.6 cr to ₹48.3 cr and other current liabilities from ₹0.9 cr to ₹40.3 cr. Net debt at Mar-26 = 149.18 − 2.92 − 0.23 − 68.65 = **₹77.4 cr**. Bank lines: ₹60 cr fund-based and ₹440 cr non-fund-based (LC/BG) across HDFC, Axis, ICICI, IDBI and Yes.

### 4. Quarters (standalone, ₹ cr)
| | Q4 FY25 | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY27 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 190.13 | 200.98 | 243.79 | 298.34 | 310.08 | **302.22** |
| YoY growth | — | — | +155% | +110% | +63% | **+50%** |
| Other income | 0.85 | 2.51 | 0.96 | 2.70 | −1.84 | 3.67 |
| EBITDA ex-OI | 7.70 | 10.03 | 11.15† | 14.48 | **36.58** | **32.66** |
| EBITDA margin | 4.05% | 4.99% | 4.58% | 4.85% | **11.80%** | **10.81%** |
| PAT | 4.33 | 6.35 | 4.01† | 9.10 | 18.71 | **22.38** |
| Consolidated revenue / PAT | 204.15 / 4.71 | 217.49 / 6.49 | 262.67 / 4.50† | 317.86 / 9.61 | 333.08 / 19.32 | **327.49 / 22.65** |

†Derived: FY26 minus the other three quarters. YoY uses the BSE API's Q2/Q3 FY25 revenue of ₹95.45/142.30 cr. The Q1 FY27 filing says **~40% higher coated-product volumes**, and the Nigerian subsidiary's revenue rose ~50% YoY (management statement). Q2 FY27 results are due by mid-Nov-2026.

### 5. Ownership (SHP 30-Jun-2026 vs 30-Jun-2025)
| Holder | Jun-25 | Jun-26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Payal Agrawal | 19.51% | 19.51% |
| Varun Agrawal (MD) | 19.47% | 19.47% |
| Suresh Kumar Agrawal (founder, NED) | 18.85% | 18.85% |
| Chandrakala Agrawal | 16.40% | 16.40% |
| S K Agrawal & Sons HUF | 0.51% | 0.51% |
| **Promoter group** | **74.75%** | **74.75%** |
| Mutual funds / FPIs / insurers | 0% | 0% |
| Central Govt (IEPF) | 0.63% | 0.63% |
| Bodies corporate (incl. Shree Bahubali Stock Broking 1.10% → 1.23%) | 3.33% | 4.81% |
| Retail ≤₹2 lakh | 16.41% (29,180 holders) | 14.97% (25,749) |
| Shareholders, total | 30,358 | 26,898 |

- **Pledge, NDU and other encumbrance: none.** No warrants, convertibles or ESOPs. The SHP lists Suresh Kumar Agrawal as the significant beneficial owner (74.75%). No insider-trading or SAST filing was found in the 730-day announcement window.
ideas.model:
**Physical revenue model.** The company sells tonnes of coated and cold-rolled steel. FY26: ~1,24,000 t sold (70,000 t in FY25), at about ₹76,000–77,800/t for its own products. The binding limit is the coating capacity of 1,44,200 TPA (GP + Alu-Zinc). Colour-coating (60,000 → 1,50,000 TPA with CCL-II) paints coated substrate, so **CCL-II mostly upgrades tonnes to a higher-priced product rather than adding tonnes**. New saleable tonnes come only from the +31,000 TPA GL/GP in Phase I (no date beyond "by FY30").

| FY27 standalone scenarios (₹ cr) | Bear | Base | Q1 run-rate | Mgmt guidance (consolidated) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 1,209 | 1,209 | 1,209 | 1,500 |
| Basis | Q1 × 4 | Q1 × 4 | Q1 × 4 | FY26 AR target |
| EBITDA margin ex-OI | 6.86% (FY26) | 8.0% | 10.81% (Q1) | 10.24% (Q1 consolidated) |
| EBITDA | 82.9 | 96.7 | 130.7 | 153.6 |
| − Depreciation (Q1×4) / − Interest (Q1×4) / + OI | −10.97 / −13.86 / +4 | same | same | −12.63 / −14.24 / +4 |
| PAT (25.8% tax, FY26 ETR) | 46.1 | 56.3 | 81.5 | 97.0 |
| EPS (₹; 6.553 cr shares) | 7.03 | 8.59 | 12.44 | 14.80 |
| P/E at ₹108.89 | 15.5x | 12.7x | 8.8x | 7.4x |

- **Margin is the whole story.** Each percentage point of EBITDA margin on ₹1,200 cr is ₹12 cr of EBITDA, about ₹8.9 cr of PAT, or ₹1.36 per share. The Q4/Q1 margins came during a steel-price upswing: Mumbai HR coil rose 31% from Dec-25 to Apr-26 and then eased to ₹68,170 in Jun-26. WPI GP/GC sheet rose 21.9% against HR coil's 18.0% from Dec-25 to Apr-26. The company held inventory through the rise (the FY26 change in inventory was −₹34.5 cr), so part of the margin is probably a **gain on inventory bought before the price rise, which would not repeat**. It does not disclose how much; that is unknown.
- **Revenue at ₹1,500 cr needs either much higher prices or more related-party trading.** Coated capacity is ~75% used and CCL-II mostly adds value per tonne rather than tonnes. Shareholders have approved up to ₹600 cr of related-party sales for FY27 (₹205 cr in FY26). Growth that comes from HR-coil trading to Nigerian related parties would carry thin margin and the receivable risk described in red flags.
- **Cross-checks:** the FY26 AR's "Cash profit ₹47.51 cr" = PAT 38.17 + depreciation 9.35 ✓. Its receivable figure of "18 days" is close to average receivables on revenue (17.7 days). Its "inventory ~54 days of consumption" could not be reproduced (year-end 63 days and average 60 days on materials consumed plus inventory change).

**Peers (1-Oct-2026 BSE closes; P/E = close ÷ BSE header TTM EPS; consolidated unless noted)**

| Company | Mcap ₹ cr (BSE) | Close ₹ | EPS ₹ | P/E | What it is |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Manaksia Steels** | 697 | 106.30 | 8.56 | **12.4x** | coated/CR steel, Haldia |
| Manaksia Coated Metals (sister) | 1,350 | 126.60 | 3.82 | 33.1x | coated/colour-coated steel, exporter |

- No listed "Shree Ram" coated-steel company was found in the BSE master. Shree Precoated Steels (533110, X group, ₹4.8 cr, loss-making) is not comparable.
- **The re-rating case in one sentence:** if FY27 confirms ~10% margins on ₹1,200–1,500 cr, the stock is at 7–9x earnings, against sister MANAKCOAT at 33x and tube/coated peers at 19–29x. **The case against:** the margin arrived with a steel-price spike, a fifth of sales go to promoter-family entities, there is no institutional ownership and the stock trades in the trade-for-trade segment. Those are reasons for a discount, and the discount may be warranted.

ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Vadodara EPC contractor (founded 2014) that builds power lines, EHV substations and underground cable networks for state utilities, mostly in Gujarat. The CMD, Nikesh Choksi, spent 21+ years at GETCO (Gujarat's state transmission utility).
- **Where it trades:** **NSE main board only** (symbol VIVIANA, ISIN INE0MEG01014). It listed on NSE Emerge (SME) in Sep-2022 at ₹55 and moved to the main board on 2-Jun-2026. It is **not on BSE**: it is absent from BSE's 1-Oct-2026 bhavcopy, so there is no BSE code. Shares: 1,01,24,800. Close ₹774.50 (NSE, 1-Oct-2026, EQ series) → **₹784 cr market cap**.
- **Why GEC-III matters, and why less than the headline suggests.** The Cabinet's ₹1,86,405 cr scheme (PIB 2316948) has State Transmission Utilities as the implementing agencies. Greenfield intra-state lines go out on **TBCB to developers (build-own-operate-maintain)**. Viviana has never won a TBCB project; it says it wants to bid for ₹1,000–2,000 cr TBCB projects "within couple of years". Brownfield strengthening is **cost-plus through the STUs**, and that is the kind of GETCO 66–220 kV work Viviana does. The scheme also funds **₹50,000 cr for 50 GWh of BESS**, a market it entered with two BOO awards. The release gives **no state-wise split**, so Gujarat's share is unknown.
- **Its current growth does not come from GETCO.** Of the ₹856 cr of awards and L1 positions disclosed in FY27 so far, **₹9.74 cr (1.1%) is GETCO**. The rest is Gujarat discom distribution work (MGVCL, PGVCL and DGVCL 11 kV underground cabling and MVCC lines under the SI/ROBUST-III schemes). GEC-III is upside for the company, not what is driving it today.
- **The numbers jumped, but they were back-ended and have not turned into cash.** FY26 standalone revenue was ₹501.7 cr (+166%) and PAT ₹50.2 cr. **Q4 alone was ₹318.7 cr (64% of the year), and March 2026 alone was ₹257.17 cr.** Year-end receivables plus retention money were ₹444 cr, or 323 days of revenue. Standalone operating cash flow added up to **−₹15.6 cr over FY23–FY26**, against ₹76.8 cr of reported profit.
- **Related-party traffic with a promoter real-estate company.** Viviana bought Viviana Life Spaces from its promoters at par (₹90,000), advanced it ₹22.55 cr, then sold it to promoter-director Priyanka Choksi in Aug-2026 for an undisclosed price. It advanced a further ₹13.53 cr in Apr–Sep-2026, and the AGM approved up to ₹50 cr more for "office premises". The promoter group's 71.7 lakh votes are shown in favour of that resolution in the filed voting results, although the notice says related parties shall not vote.

### 1. The business
- **What it does:** EPC for transmission lines and substations up to 400 kV (a 400 kV D/C LILO for a 323.4 MW wind park was energised on 10-Jul-2026), 11–66 kV distribution, underground cabling and MVCC conversion, and supply of materials. FY26 standalone revenue split: products ₹437.2 cr, services ₹64.5 cr (AR note 29). Sub-contracted labour cost ₹54.0 cr in FY26.
- **Customers:** state utilities. ACER names PGVCL, GETCO, DGVCL, MGVCL and PSPCL, plus Adani Green. **Customer-wise revenue is not disclosed** (unknown). The AR lists "geographic concentration" (western and central India) as a weakness.
- **Transformers:** Aarsh Transformers (distribution transformers up to 500 kVA, 75% owned) was sold on 15-Aug-2026. A leased Por (Vadodara) unit, 66/33 kV class up to 20 MVA and up to 1,000 MVA a year, was inaugurated on 21-Sep-2026. A ~₹90 cr phase-1 greenfield plant (132 kV) is planned: ₹3.5–4 cr spent, ~₹10 cr due in FY27 (Aug-2026 call).
- **BESS (build-own-operate, not EPC):** see the model. Neither project has reached financial closure or notice-to-proceed in the filings read.

ideas.model:
**Revenue model.** This is a project business. Revenue = order book × execution rate. There is no capacity unit.

| ₹ cr | Value | Arithmetic / source |
|---|---:|---|
| EPC book incl. L1 (17-Sep-2026, incl. GST) | ~1,339 | 1,850 stated − 511 BESS (302.46 + 208.74) |
| Q1 FY27 revenue | 71.86 | results |
| Annualised Q1 run-rate | ~287 | 71.86 × 4 |
| FY27 guidance | 875–910 | Q1 deck, Aug call, AR (">₹900 cr") |
| Needed in Q2–Q4 | 803–838 | guidance − Q1 |
| FY26 for comparison | Q1–Q3 182.95, Q4 318.72 | the same back-ended shape |
| PAT at guidance | 74–91 | 875–910 × 8.5–10% (deck PAT band; Aug call: "~9–9.5% annually") |
| EPS at guidance (1,01,24,800 sh) | ₹73–90 | |

The guidance needs an EPC book of ~₹1,339 cr (GST-inclusive, so less ex-GST) to convert at roughly 65% inside nine months. FY26 shows that can happen in a single March. It also showed that collecting the cash is the problem.

**BESS economics (BOO tariff assets, from filings and calls)**
| | RVUNL (Bhopalgarh, Jodhpur) | GUVNL Phase-VII (Asoj) |
|---|---|---|
| Award | LOI, 24-Oct-2025 | 2-Jan-2026 |
| Capacity | **not stated** (the filing quotes the 1,000 MW/2,000 MWh tender total) | 65 MW / 130 MWh |
| Contract value over 12 yrs | ₹302.46 cr → ₹25.2 cr/yr | ₹208.74 cr → ₹17.4 cr/yr (≈₹2.23 lakh/MW-month) |
| VGF | ₹36.00 cr | not in filing |
| Capex | ₹198 cr (Jun-2026 call) | not stated separately |
| Status | land allotted; IOB + Canara sanctions, financial closure pending (Jun/Aug calls) | awaiting GUVNL notice to proceed; shared park with another developer (Aug call) |
Management figures differ from call to call. Total capex was given as ₹350 cr (Dec-2025 call), ~₹300 cr with ₹60 cr equity, ~₹60 cr subsidy and ₹180 cr debt (Jun-2026 call), and ₹240 cr with ₹215 cr debt at the VEPL/Asoj SPVs (ACER). On the Jun-2026 call management agreed with an analyst's sum: ~₹40 cr/yr revenue, ₹17–18 cr/yr interest, ~₹14 cr cash PBT. It said the IRR **"at present... would be in a single digit."** No BESS revenue is expected in FY27. The BESS money is a 12-year tariff stream, not a backlog that turns into revenue within a year or two.

**What GEC-III could add (no number is possible).** Gujarat's allocation is not in the release. Viviana can reach the money three ways: (a) GETCO cost-plus brownfield packages, its historic 66–220 kV niche, worth ₹140.75 cr of awards in 18 months; (b) EPC sub-contracts from TBCB winners; (c) BESS tenders under the ₹50,000 cr / 50 GWh pool (≈₹1 cr/MWh implied, against the RVUNL ₹198 cr capex). Each depends on bids not yet tendered.

ideas.name: Oriana Power Ltd
ideas.industry: Solar & BESS EPC + project developer (asset-recycling IPP model)
ideas.trigger: govt: Green Energy Corridor-III + 50 GWh BESS (Cabinet 30-Sep-2026, ₹1,86,405 cr) — Oriana won two MSEDCL LOAs for 900 MW/1,800 MWh BOO BESS (filed 21-Sep-2026; ~₹3,870 cr over 15 yrs, ₹258 cr/yr, VGF ₹324 cr), taking its state/PSU BESS awards to 2,350 MWh; GEC-III's ₹50,000 cr BESS component is the next tender pool, but ~60% of FY26 revenue was EPC to its own deconsolidated SPVs
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Noida solar EPC contractor (835+ MW delivered, 700+ MW under execution) that is turning into a developer: it builds solar, solar+BESS and standalone BESS plants inside its own project companies (SPVs), books the EPC work as revenue, and then sells the SPVs (74% stakes) to funds such as Actis. It also holds 1,175 MW / 2,350 MWh of state-utility BESS awards on a build-own-operate (BOO) basis.
- **Where it is listed:** **NSE Emerge (SME) only**, symbol ORIANA, series SM, ISIN INE0OUT01027 (new ISIN after the 1:5 split, record date 18-Sep-2026). No BSE listing: the name is absent from BSE's 1-Oct-2026 bhavcopy. The company says main-board migration is a goal; no date.
- **The trigger:** on 21-Sep-2026 it filed two MSEDCL Letters of Award (dated 18-Sep) for **900 MW / 1,800 MWh** of BESS at MSEDCL/MSETCL substations, tariff ₹2.38–2.40 lakh/MW/month (ex-GST), 15-year BESPA, **~₹3,870 cr** of contract revenue (₹258 cr a year) and **₹324 cr** of expected VGF under the PSDF scheme. That is 2.1x FY26 revenue in lifetime contract value; 1,800 MWh is 3.6% of the 50 GWh that GEC-III (Cabinet, 30-Sep-2026) funds.
- **Why it fits the government lane:** GEC-III puts ₹50,000 cr into 50 GWh of BESS "at the RE developer/generator end or any other location of importance". Oriana has already won 5 state/PSU BESS tenders (TNPDCL, RVUNL, NVVN, KPTCL, MSEDCL) and sells solar+BESS hybrids to C&I buyers. The transmission part (₹1,36,378 cr, TBCB/BOOM by transmission service providers) is not Oriana's business: no transmission order appears in its 3 years of filings.
- **What the numbers say:** revenue ₹134.7 cr (FY23) → ₹1,813.7 cr (FY26); PAT ₹10.6 cr → ₹252.3 cr. But **₹1,085.1 cr (59.8%) of FY26 revenue was "sale of solar power plant" to the company's own project SPVs**, which it leaves out of consolidation because it "intends" to sell them (AS 21 para 11). FY25: ₹385.2 cr (39.0%).
- **The hidden balance sheet:** the group guarantees **₹1,384.8 cr** of SPV debt that is *not* in the ₹183 cr contingent-liability total, against **₹1,825.0 cr** of plant assets kept off the consolidated balance sheet (FY25: ₹311.7 cr and ₹522.2 cr). Another **₹719.5 cr** of TReDS/LC "credit arrangement liabilities" sits in other current liabilities, not borrowings, and its rise is counted as *operating* cash flow.
- **Price:** ₹303.45 (NSE close 1-Oct-2026; 2-Oct holiday; no 5-Oct file yet) = ₹3,083 cr market cap = **12.2x FY26 EPS**, 8.3x EV/EBITDA. That is in line with listed EPC peers (9–17x), not a premium. The stock is −45% from ₹555 a year ago (split-adjusted) and +12% since the MSEDCL filing (₹271.30 on 21-Sep).

### 1. The business (FY26, consolidated, ₹ lakh)
| Revenue line (note 24) | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sale of solar power plant (EPC) | 96,454.36 | 1,75,608.26 |
| — of which to own project SPVs (RPT note) | 38,524.37 | 1,08,510.02 |
| Sale of power (own IPP/RESCO) | 2,055.89 | 3,306.55 |
| Unbilled + other operating | 206.35 | 2,452.42 |
| **Total** | **98,716.60** | **1,81,367.23** |

- Segments (H2 FY26): EPC ₹1,016.47 cr revenue, ₹234.19 cr segment profit; RESCO ₹16.02 cr revenue, ₹6.33 cr segment *loss*.
- Model, in management's words (10-Jun-2026 meet): develop "bankable projects" and "selectively monetize assets"; BESS assets "are under different SPVs—not directly in Oriana... that revenue we will book in EPC". Asset sales are planned every half-year (~200 MWp each).
- Employees 257 permanent (AR) / "370+" (deck). Land 4,780 acres (deck).

### 2. BESS awards (all BOO, all with VGF; every figure from the award filing)
| Date | Off-taker | Size | Contract value | Term | VGF | Implied ₹/MW/month |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 02-Jul-2025 | TNPDCL (Karaikudi) | 50 MW/100 MWh | ₹209.00 cr incl GST | 12 yr | ₹27 cr | 2.90 lakh incl GST |
| 07-Jul-2025 | NVVN (Giral, Raj.) | 125 MW/250 MWh | ₹465.15 cr incl GST | 12 yr | ₹67.5 cr | 2.58 lakh incl GST |
| 09-Jul-2025 | RVUNL (Heerapura) via Truere Knight | 50 MW/100 MWh | ₹188.61 cr incl GST | 12 yr | ₹27 cr | 2.62 lakh incl GST |
| 14-Jul-2025 | KPTCL (Shahapur) | 50 MW/100 MWh | ₹212.32 cr incl GST | 12 yr | ₹27 cr | 2.95 lakh incl GST |
| 21-Sep-2026 | **MSEDCL** (2 LOAs) | **900 MW/1,800 MWh** | **₹3,870 cr ex GST** | 15 yr | **₹324 cr** | 2.38/2.40 lakh ex GST |
| **Total** | | **1,175 MW/2,350 MWh** | | | **₹472.5 cr** | |

Math: ₹465.15 cr ÷ 12 ÷ (125 MW × 12) = ₹2.58 lakh/MW/month. MSEDCL: 500 × 2.38 lakh × 12 = ₹142.80 cr/yr; 400 × 2.40 lakh × 12 = ₹115.20 cr/yr; ₹258 cr × 15 = ₹3,870 cr (matches the filing). VGF per MWh fell from ₹27 lakh (2025 awards) to ₹18 lakh (₹324 cr ÷ 1,800 MWh). The GST rate on the 2025 awards is not stated, so like-for-like tariff comparison is not possible.

**Solar+BESS EPC orders cited in the leads (verified):** 18-Aug-2025, 75 MW + ~111.57 MWh for a cement company, ₹476.13 cr incl GST, 8 months; 24-Mar-2026, 32 MW + 20 MWh for three Jodhpur steel/fibre firms, ₹162.68 cr ex GST + ₹1.00 cr O&M. Other large orders: 234 MW floating solar at DVC Maithon, ₹1,180.53 cr incl GST, 18 months (8-Mar-2026); 50 MW for a cement company, ₹214.80 cr (19-Aug-2026); Bellwether Bihar 25.1 MW, ₹94.51 cr (20-Aug-2026); SECI green ammonia supply LOA, 60,000 t/yr at ₹52.25/kg, ~₹313.5 cr a year for 10 years (21-Aug-2025).

**Order book:** ₹6,612 cr at Mar-2026 (CRISIL, 24-Jun-2026); "around ₹6,800 crores" unexecuted (management, 10-Jun-2026), before the MSEDCL awards. That is 3.6–3.7x FY26 revenue. The mix between third-party EPC, own-SPV EPC and BOO annuities is **not disclosed**.

### 3. Growth (consolidated, ₹ cr; AS/Indian GAAP; EBITDA = PBT + finance cost + D&A − other income)
| | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 134.72 | 382.87 | 987.17 | **1,813.67** |
| Growth | — | +184% | +158% | +84% |
| EBITDA ex OI | 19.40 | 80.72 | 234.49 | 398.02 |
| EBITDA margin | 14.4% | 21.1% | 23.8% | 21.9% |
| Other income | 1.12 | 2.92 | 10.90 | 27.34 |
| Finance cost | 3.39 | 6.03 | 24.52 | 62.94 |
| PAT (owners) | 10.56 | 54.35 | 158.57 | **252.34** |
| PAT margin | 7.8% | 14.2% | 16.1% | 13.9% |

| Half-year | H1 FY24 | H2 FY24 | H1 FY25 | H2 FY25 | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 64.06 | 318.82 | 359.54 | 627.62 | 781.18 | 1,032.49 |
| EBITDA ex OI | 11.35 | 69.37 | 75.39 | 159.11 | 180.46 | 217.57 |
| Margin | 17.7% | 21.8% | 21.0% | 25.4% | 23.1% | 21.1% |
| Finance cost | 2.55 | 3.48 | 7.76 | 16.77 | 20.21 | 42.73 |
| PAT | 5.73 | 48.62 | 48.60 | 109.97 | 121.44 | 130.89 |

H2 FY26 PAT rose only 19% YoY on +65% revenue: margin down, finance cost 2.5x, employee cost ₹48.0 cr for FY26 vs ₹16.3 cr. Management had guided ₹2,000–2,500 cr FY26 revenue (Jun/Nov-2025 calls) and missed, blaming the Actis sale slipping out of FY26.

### 4. Cash and balance sheet (consolidated, ₹ cr)
| | Mar-23 | Mar-24 | Mar-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Net worth | 31.71 | 146.20 | 509.64 | 763.43 |
| Borrowings (LT+ST) | 70.76 | 183.53 | 270.61 | 508.55 |
| TReDS/LC "credit arrangement" liabilities | — | — | 137.69 | **719.55** |
| Mobilisation deposits received | — | — | — | 258.87 |
| Trade receivables | 36.66 | 78.52 | 394.15 | 671.14 |
| Receivable days (on revenue) | 99 | 75 | 146 | 135 |
| Contract assets (unbilled) | — | — | — | 75.23 |
| Assets held for sale (SPV stakes) | — | — | 278.48 | 537.98 |
| Cash & bank (of which FDs >3m) | 1.58 | 22.10 | 70.39 | 286.08 (209.80) |
| Operating cash flow | 15.65 | 2.70 | 250.89* | 337.04 |
| Capex (net PPE purchase) | 48.07 | 113.62 | 149.23 | 152.68 |
| Investment in held-for-sale SPVs | — | — | 278.51 | 259.50 |

*FY25 OCF is ₹290.49 cr in the FY25 annual report and ₹250.89 cr in the FY26 comparatives (restated, no explanation found).

- **OCF is flattered by financing.** FY26 OCF counts a ₹690.6 cr rise in other current liabilities, of which ₹581.9 cr is the jump in TReDS/LC credit-arrangement liabilities (CFO on the 10-Jun call: "we are discounting bills using TReDS"). Moving that rise to financing gives FY26 OCF of 337.04 − 581.86 = **−₹244.8 cr**.
- **Off-balance-sheet:** corporate guarantees of ₹1,384.77 cr for held-for-sale SPV loans (note 36, footnote 3) and ₹1,640.34 cr of guarantees outstanding to subsidiaries in total (standalone CARO iii). CRISIL puts standalone debt at ₹701.2 cr and adjusted debt/net worth at **1.23x (0.33x a year earlier)**, with ₹553.05 cr (70.4% of net worth) invested in SPVs.
- Promoters personally guarantee ₹254.50 cr of facilities (standalone note). Loans to related SPVs of ₹249.21 cr are outstanding, all repayable on demand.
- Funding lines: CRISIL-rated bank limits ₹800 cr (raised from ₹600 cr); ₹75 cr of NCDs at 11.65% (7-Jan-2026), secured partly by a pledge of SPV shares; ₹200 cr of NCDs rated but not yet issued (as filed by 24-Jun-2026).

### 5. Can it fund 1.8 GWh?
The company never states BESS capex. Two filed anchors: (i) GEC-III budgets ₹50,000 cr for 50 GWh = **₹1.0 cr per MWh**; (ii) Oriana's April-2026 RPT approvals size SPV support as EPC : equity : guarantee = 1,000 : 250 : 750 (Truere Knight), i.e. **25% equity / 75% guaranteed debt**. On those two anchors:

| MSEDCL 1,800 MWh | at ₹0.8 cr/MWh | at ₹1.0 cr/MWh (GEC-III ratio) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Capex | ₹1,440 cr | ₹1,800 cr |
| less VGF | ₹324 cr | ₹324 cr |
| Net to finance | ₹1,116 cr | ₹1,476 cr |
| Equity at 25% | ₹279 cr | ₹369 cr |
| Debt at 75% (parent-guaranteed) | ₹837 cr | ₹1,107 cr |

On top of this, the 550 MWh of 2025 awards still need funding. Against a ₹763 cr net worth, ₹286 cr of cash (mostly FDs, likely lien-marked: unknown) and Actis proceeds of ~₹194 cr agreed in June for the two SPVs (amount actually received in Sep: not disclosed), the equity alone would absorb 37–48% of net worth. Guarantees would rise from ~1.8x to ~3.3x net worth. Either the MSEDCL SPVs are sold down early (the Actis model), or the parent raises equity. **There is no QIP or preferential plan on file today.**
ideas.model:
**Revenue drivers (all from filings):** EPC revenue = MW (or MWh) executed × ₹/MW. Oriana books EPC both to third parties and to its own SPVs. On top sit (a) the gain on selling 74% of finished SPVs to funds, and (b) for SPVs it keeps, BOO annuities (BESS tariff × MW × 12) and RESCO power sales.

**What MSEDCL adds once commissioned (scheduled COD not yet fixed: the BESPAs are not yet signed):**

| Item | Value | Arithmetic |
|---|---:|---|
| Annual capacity charge | ₹258.0 cr | 500×2.38L×12 + 400×2.40L×12 |
| vs FY26 revenue | 14.2% | 258 ÷ 1,813.67 |
| VGF | ₹324 cr | filing; ₹18 lakh/MWh |
| Unlevered project IRR at ₹0.8 cr/MWh capex, no opex | 21.9% | −1,116 then +258 a year × 15 |
| same at ₹1.0 cr/MWh | 15.5% | −1,476 then +258 × 15 |
| same at ₹1.0 cr/MWh with opex at 2% of capex | 12.5% | +222 a year |
| Breakeven-style read | revenue ÷ net capex = 0.17–0.23 | |

These IRRs are ceilings: they ignore augmentation, charging losses, tax, the timing of VGF disbursement and the residual value. Capex per MWh for Oriana is **unknown**; the two capex cases are anchors from the PIB release (₹1.0 cr/MWh), not company data.

**How the P&L can look in FY27 (management guidance, 10-Jun-2026):** "~40% to 50% CAGR" in revenue and PAT, "~70%" if conditions allow; BESS 35–40% of FY27 revenue; ~238 MWp sold to Actis in H1 and ~200 MWp more in H2; green ammonia revenue only from FY28.

| ₹ cr | FY26 actual | FY27 at +40% | FY27 at +50% |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 1,813.67 | 2,539 | 2,721 |
| PAT at FY26 13.9% margin | 252.34 | 353 | 378 |
| EPS (10.16 cr shares) | 24.84 | 34.7 | 37.2 |
| P/E at ₹303.45 | 12.2x | 8.7x | 8.2x |

Cross-checks: CRISIL (Jun-2026) expects operating income "above Rs 2,000 crore annually in medium term" and margins of 18–20%, below FY26's 22.3% (its basis). At 19% EBITDA on ₹2,100 cr, EBITDA = ₹399 cr, flat on FY26. In other words, the rating agency's base case is not management's 40–50%.

**Quality adjustment to keep in view:** 59.8% of FY26 revenue went to SPVs the company controls. If the SPVs were consolidated, that EPC margin would be eliminated until the asset is sold to a third party. Margin earned on own-SPV work is only realised in cash when Actis-type buyers pay (Truere Guj EV ~₹325 cr, Truere Current EV ~₹176 cr, first tranches closed 25/30-Sep-2026). The H1 FY27 results (due by 14-Nov-2026) should be the first to show those sale proceeds and any gain.

**Read:** Oriana trades at the peer median, not at a discount, even though its earnings carry the own-SPV-revenue and off-balance-sheet guarantee issues the peers (as far as read) do not show to the same degree. Management pointed out on the 10-Jun call that the stock once traded at ~90x and now nearer 17x. The re-rating case in one sentence: if H1 FY27 shows the Actis cash actually received, a gain on sale, OCF positive *after* moving TReDS to financing, and MSEDCL BESPAs signed with a funding plan that does not require cheap equity, the multiple can rise toward 15x as BESS annuities start; if not, 12x on earnings that are 60% internal is not cheap.

updates.title: Corporate guarantee for the Usolar JV's ₹460 cr SBI working-capital line raised from 74% to 100%
updates.body:
Reg 30 filing 6-Oct-2026 (board meeting the same day): the guarantee in favour of State Bank of India for the ₹460 cr working-capital facility of **Oriana Usolar Joint Venture Pvt Ltd** (a subsidiary) is revised from 74% of the facility (14-Sep-2026 filing, already on the card) to the **entire facility**, subject to shareholder approval. Purpose: the 234 MW (AC) floating solar plant on DVC's Maithon dam reservoir — the ₹1,180.53 cr EPC order of 8-Mar-2026 on the card. Tenure 12 months, renewable yearly, repayable on demand; the company says there is no immediate impact and it is a contingent liability. Promoters not interested; arm's length.

| | ₹ cr | Working |
|---|---:|---|
| Facility guaranteed before | 340.4 | 74% × 460 |
| Facility guaranteed now | **460.0** | 100% |
| Added contingent exposure | 119.6 | 460 − 340.4 |
| Facility vs FY26 revenue (₹1,813.67 cr) | 25.4% | |
| Facility vs the Maithon EPC order | 39.0% | 460 ÷ 1,180.53 |

The filing does not say who holds the other 26% of the JV or why the co-venturer's share of the guarantee moved to Oriana — that is the open question for the postal ballot / AGM notice that must follow.

ideas.trigger: filing: CAPEX - BMW Industries filed two Reg 30 disclosures on 05-Oct-2026 (14:47 and 15:08 IST) saying it received the Consent to Operate that day and has commissioned the Colour Coating line, the first phase of a Rs 803 crore greenfield downstream steel complex at Bokaro; Rs 341.6 cr was deployed to 30-Jun-2026 and ~Rs 60 cr capitalised for this line. Revenue from it starts in Q3 FY27.
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.** BMW Industries does not sell steel today; it *processes* other people's steel for a fee. The Bokaro plant commissioned this morning is the company's attempt to stop being a toll processor and start owning the metal it coats. That changes what the revenue line means, and it is the whole investment question.

**What the business physically does.** Three legacy plants in West Bengal and Jharkhand, plus a JV with SAIL (subsidiary SAIL Bansal Service Centre Limited). Capacity and utilisation, from the company's own Q1 FY27 investor presentation (14-Aug-2026):

| Business | Installed capacity (MT) | FY26 production (MT) | FY26 util. | Q1 FY27 production (MT) | Annualised util. |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CGL Complex (HRPO/CR/GP coils, GC sheets) | 10,14,000 | 7,18,605 | 70.9% | 1,65,609 | 65.3% |
| Rolling Mill (TMT bars) | 1,80,000 | 74,975 | 41.7% | 37,583 | 83.5% |
| Pipes & Tubes | 7,32,000 | 2,01,623 | 34.2% | 73,345 | 40.1% |

**The one number that frames everything.** FY26 standalone revenue of Rs 664.07 cr splits (annual report note 32) into **conversion income Rs 411.72 cr (62.0%)**, manufactured product sales Rs 192.83 cr (29.0%), traded goods Rs 4.85 cr and transport/supervision Rs 54.68 cr. Conversion income *fell* 14.5% from Rs 481.58 cr in FY25, while product sales rose 2.4x from Rs 80.50 cr. The shift to owning metal is already in the accounts, 18 months before Bokaro contributes.

**Why that matters for revenue per tonne.** Q1 FY27 revenue divided by tonnes dispatched:

| Business | Q1 FY27 revenue (Rs lakh) | Dispatch (MT) | Rs per tonne |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| CGL Complex | 7,775 | 84,261 | 9,227 |
| Rolling Mill (TMT) | 2,553 | 36,714 | 6,954 |
| Pipes & Tubes | 3,148 | 68,987 | 4,563 |

Rs 4,563-9,227 a tonne is a *conversion charge*. The product itself sells for far more: Mumbai HRC was Rs 63.7/kg and Mumbai PPGI (pre-painted galvanised, 0.5 mm / 90 GSM) Rs 89.3/kg on MetalBook's Indian prints (25-29 Sep 2026). On a proprietary-supply model the same tonne books roughly 7-10x the revenue it books as tolling - at a much thinner percentage margin. That is exactly what management guides to: revenue CAGR of 70-75% FY25-FY28 with PAT margin *falling* to 5-6% by FY28 from 11.9% in FY26.

**What was commissioned today, and what was not.** The Colour Coating line only. The press release puts the subsequent phases at 550,000 TPA Cold Rolled Full Hard and 540,000 TPA GA/GI/ZAM, with no commissioning date given for either. Funding is tied up: Rs 500 cr of debt from a consortium led by SBI, HDFC Bank and Yes Bank, of which Rs 202.4 cr was drawn by 30-Jun-2026 alongside Rs 139.2 cr of internal accruals. The line qualifies under **PLI 1.1 for Coated/Plated Steel** (incentives on sales to FY29) and Jharkhand's industrial policy, and runs on IOCL piped natural gas.

**Capacity of the commissioned line: the documents disagree.** The investor presentation says Colour Coated Coils **2,00,000 TPA**; the MD on the 17-Aug-2026 earnings call said "This is a 1,50,000 tons line" and that it will take "at least three to four quarters to ramp it up all the way". Both are the company's own words three weeks apart. Treat 150,000-200,000 TPA as the range; it is not resolved.
ideas.model:
**Physical driver.** Tonnes of coated steel sold x price per tonne, replacing a conversion fee per tonne. There is no new volume in the legacy business to model - it is a utilisation story (pipes & tubes 34.2% in FY26 to 40.1% in Q1 FY27; the MD's stable-state expectation is "65% to 70% ... by, let's say, FY29").

**Management's own guidance (17-Aug-2026 call, verbatim figures):** consolidated revenue CAGR ~70-75% FY25-FY28; operating EBITDA CAGR ~40-45%; PAT CAGR ~35-40%; EBITDA margin settling at ~12-13% and PAT margin at ~5-6% by FY28.

**Arithmetic on that guidance** (FY25 consolidated revenue Rs 557.08 cr and PAT Rs 63.60 cr, BSE detailed results):

| Line | Low | High | Arithmetic |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| FY28 revenue (Rs cr) | 2,737 | 2,985 | 557.08 x 1.70^3 / 1.75^3 |
| FY28 PAT from margin guide (Rs cr) | 137 | 179 | 5% / 6% of the above |
| FY28 PAT from PAT-CAGR guide (Rs cr) | 157 | 175 | 63.60 x 1.35^3 / 1.40^3 |
| Overlap used (Rs cr) | **157** | **175** | both tests agree here |
| Shares (cr) | 22.51 | 22.51 | mcap 1,250.1 / close 55.54; TTM EPS 3.80 on PAT 85.59 agrees |
| FY28 EPS (Rs) | **6.98** | **7.78** | PAT / shares |

**Independent physical cross-check, and where it falls short.** The colour-coating line at 150,000-200,000 TPA, sold at the Mumbai PPGI print of Rs 89.3/kg, is Rs 1,340-1,786 cr of revenue at *full* utilisation. Ramping from Q3 FY27 over three to four quarters, FY28 would capture perhaps 70-85% of that: Rs 940-1,520 cr. Add legacy revenue at roughly the FY26-FY27 run rate (Rs 665-700 cr) and FY28 lands at **Rs 1,600-2,220 cr** - materially *below* management's Rs 2,737-2,985 cr.

**So the guidance needs the two undated phases.** The gap of roughly Rs 700-1,200 cr is what the 550,000 TPA CRFH and 540,000 TPA GA/GI/ZAM lines are meant to fill, and neither has a commissioning date in any document read today. The MD puts total Bokaro throughput at "about 0.5 million tons"; that is the ceiling the whole complex is built for, not the sum of the three line capacities, which are sequential stages of one metal flow.

**Trailing position** (BSE detailed results, consolidated, Rs cr):

| Period | Revenue | PAT | PAT margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY25 | 557.08 | 63.60 | 11.4% |
| FY26 | 664.07 | 81.63 | 12.3% |
| Q1 FY27 | 165.83 | 19.24 | 11.6% |
| TTM (Q2 FY26-Q1 FY27) | 681.43 | 85.59 | 12.6% |

**One feed discrepancy, stated not hidden.** For Q1 FY26 the BSE detailed-results feed shows revenue Rs 130.37 cr and PAT Rs 10.64 cr, while the company's own Q1 FY27 presentation shows Rs 148.69 cr and Rs 15.20 cr for the same quarter (and the FY26 and Q1 FY27 figures agree between the two sources to within Rs 1 cr). The company's numbers are used above for Q1 FY26 comparisons and BSE's for the annual series; the reason for the Q1 FY26 difference is unknown - I did not open the Q1 FY26 results PDF in this run.

**The re-rating case in one sentence.** BMW trades at roughly half the multiple of the listed coated-steel maker it is trying to become, on earnings that are already there - and if the undated CRFH and galvanising phases land, the FY28 guidance puts it at 7-8x.

**The de-rating case in one sentence.** Revenue multiplies while margin collapses from 12.3% to 5-6%, so the business becomes a thinner, more working-capital-hungry one; if the ramp slips, the market is paying 14.6x for a tolling business whose conversion income is already shrinking.

Where the ROCE sits matters more than the PE here: 9.5% annualised at 30-Jun-2026 with Rs 341.6 cr idle. Management expects it to "progressively improve" as the facility ramps. That is the number to watch each quarter.

ideas.verify:
- **Whether the colour-coating line is actually producing saleable coil, not just passing hot trials.** Today's filing reports a Consent to Operate dated 05-Oct-2026 and "successfully commissioned"; on 17-Aug-2026 the MD said "The hot trials are on, and it will be capitalized in Q2". Monthly despatch tonnage from Bokaro, or a GST e-way-bill trail, would settle it. Only a plant visit or a dealer in Bokaro/Ranchi can confirm it is running at a commercial rate.

- **Commissioning dates for CRFH and GA/GI/ZAM.** The FY28 guidance cannot be met by the colour-coating line alone (see the model). No document read today dates these phases. A direct question at the Q2 FY27 call would resolve the single biggest uncertainty in the thesis.

ideas.industry: Plantations - natural rubber and tea (11 tea estates in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, 8 rubber estates in Kerala)
ideas.trigger: price: Natural rubber - the Rubber Board's Kottayam RSS4 print was Rs 28,000 per 100 kg on 05-Oct-2026 (Rs 280/kg), up 50.5% in a year and 22.3% in six months, and the highest level in the 6,860 readings of that series since 24-Jan-2001; rubber was 54.3% of Harrisons Malayalam's FY26 external revenue and 90% of its segment profit.
ideas.thesis:
**The price, measured.** The Rubber Board publishes a dated daily domestic price; this repo has read and stored it since 2001. Kottayam RSS4:

| Period | Mean Rs/100 kg | Readings | vs year earlier |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY25 (Apr-24 to Mar-25) | 19,988 | 303 | - |
| FY26 (Apr-25 to Mar-26) | 19,730 | 302 | -1.3% |
| Q1 FY26 | 19,862 | 75 | - |
| Q1 FY27 | 25,372 | 73 | **+27.7%** |
| Q2 FY26 | 19,789 | 77 | - |
| Q2 FY27 | 27,713 | 76 | **+40.0%** |
| 05-Oct-2026 (print) | **28,000** | 1 | +50.5% on the 1-year change |

Of 6,860 readings since 24-Jan-2001, **29 sit at or above today's Rs 28,000, and every one of them falls between 15-Jul-2026 and today.** The series maximum is Rs 28,400 on 01-Aug-2026, so today is within 1.4% of the highest print this series has ever carried. This is not an all-time high for Indian rubber - it is the highest level in this particular Rubber Board series over the span it covers. ISNR20 at Kottayam tells the same story (Q2 FY27 mean 25,003 vs 17,486 a year earlier, +43.0%), and so does latex 60% (20,340 today vs a Q2 FY26 mean near 13,700).

**Who it lands on.** Harrisons Malayalam is the company `docs/ideas/commodity_map.json` maps to this group, and the exposure is documented, not assumed:

| FY26 (Rs cr) | Tea | Rubber | Others | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue from external customers | 242.32 | **292.68** | 4.08 | 539.08 |
| Share of revenue | 45.0% | **54.3%** | 0.8% | 100% |
| Segment profit / (loss) | (0.69) | **25.64** | 14.82 | 39.77 |
| FY25 segment profit / (loss) | (10.80) | 35.44 | 3.22 | 27.86 |

CARE Ratings, in its 17-Feb-2026 rationale, calls HML "the single-largest producer of rubber in the country and the second-largest producer of tea in South India", and puts rubber at 57% of total operating income in FY25 (54% in FY24). Tea has been loss-making or barely breakeven at the segment level for two years. **This is a rubber company with a tea problem.**

**The physical unit.** FY26: rubber harvested from own gardens **4,341 MT** (4,800 MT in FY25) plus **4,020 MT** bought (3,062 MT); average rubber realisation **Rs 214.84/kg** against Rs 216.19 the year before - essentially flat, because FY26's Rubber Board mean (Rs 197.30/kg) was flat too. Tea: own gardens 10,070 MT, bought leaf 3,637 MT, realisation Rs 172.44/kg. Roughly 6,731 direct employees; CARE puts labour at ~44% of total cost, and almost all of it is fixed against volume.

**The realisation premium is measurable.** FY26 realisation Rs 214.84/kg against the FY26 Rubber Board RSS4 mean of Rs 197.30/kg is **+8.9%**. That premium is the bridge from the public print to this company's own revenue line.

**And here is the part that cuts against the idea.** Q1 FY27 is the first quarter that carried the higher price, and transmission was weak:

| Q1, standalone, Rs cr | Q1 FY27 | Q1 FY26 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Rubber segment revenue | 63.48 | 58.86 | **+7.8%** |
| Rubber segment result | 5.71 | 5.15 | +10.9% |
| Tea segment revenue | 60.73 | 57.40 | +5.8% |
| Tea segment result | 0.86 | 3.84 | **-77.6%** |
| Profit before tax | 3.94 | 5.96 | **-33.9%** |

The Rubber Board print was up 27.7% in that quarter and rubber revenue rose 7.8%. If realisation tracked the index, volume fell about 15.6% (1.078 / 1.277 - 1). That assumption is mine, not the company's - HML does not publish quarterly tonnage - but the direction is consistent with own-crop falling 4,800 to 4,341 MT in FY26 and with CARE's finding that **mature tapping area dropped from 74.31% of total area in FY21 to 55.7% in H1 FY26** because litigation stopped replanting between 2014 and 2019 and rubber takes about seven years to mature.

**What would make FY27-FY28 different.** CARE: "Mature area is expected to improve from **FY27 onwards**." Q2 FY27 is the quarter where the price gain is largest (+40.0% YoY) and the crop is seasonally heavier than Q1. Q2 results are the test of this idea; the trading window closed on 25-Sep-2026 for the quarter and half-year ended 30-Sep-2026, so the filing is due in the usual November window.
ideas.model:
**Revenue model.** Own crop tonnes x realisation, plus a trading margin on bought rubber, plus tea. Only the own-crop leg carries price through to profit, because its cost is labour that does not move with the price.

**Sensitivity on the own-crop leg** (FY26 actuals as the base; the only assumption is that the +8.9% FY26 realisation premium over the Rubber Board print holds):

| Line | Value | Arithmetic |
|---|---:|---|
| FY26 own rubber crop | 4,341 MT | annual report, Directors' Report |
| FY26 realisation | Rs 214.84/kg | annual report |
| FY26 RSS4 mean | Rs 197.30/kg | Rubber Board series, 302 readings |
| Premium | +8.9% | 214.84 / 197.30 |
| H1 FY27 RSS4 mean | Rs 265.66/kg | Rubber Board series, 149 readings |
| Implied realisation at the same premium | Rs 289.3/kg | 265.66 x 1.089 |
| Gain per kg | **Rs 74.5/kg** | 289.3 - 214.84 |
| On an unchanged 4,341 MT own crop | **+Rs 32.3 cr** | 4,341,000 kg x Rs 74.5 |
| FY26 profit before tax | Rs 29.15 cr | audited FY26 results |

So a full year at H1 FY27 prices, on unchanged own volume and unchanged cost per kg, is worth roughly the whole of FY26's pre-tax profit again. That is the size of the prize, and it is why the group scores where it does.

**Three reasons the Rs 32.3 cr will not arrive in full, each measured:**
1. **Volume.** Own crop already fell 9.6% in FY26 and Q1 FY27 implies a further fall of about 15.6%. Each 10% of own-crop loss costs roughly Rs 12.6 cr of revenue at the new price.
2. **Bought rubber is a pass-through, not a gain.** 4,020 MT of FY26 volume was purchased; its cost rises with the same index.
3. **Tree-felling income is normalising.** CARE: HML "earns tree felling income on selling old rubber trees when they are cut down in replanting, which attracts a higher margin ... tree felling income is expected to normalise going forward, which might lead to a drop in profitability from rubber segment." That is already visible: rubber segment profit fell from Rs 35.44 cr to Rs 25.64 cr in FY26 on flat realisation.

**Cross-check against the price mechanism.** There is no formula contract and no lag to model: a plantation sells at the market of the day, through Rubber Board-quoted grades. Inventory is biological - standing crop is measured at fair value under Ind AS 41 with changes through the P&L on harvest - so a rising price revalues the crop in the period it is tapped, not with a lag. There is no hedging disclosed.

**Tea is the offsetting unknown.** 45.0% of revenue, segment result Rs 0.86 cr in Q1 FY27 against Rs 3.84 cr a year earlier. WPI Tea is up (1m +9.3%, 3m +7.9% on the April-2026 index - the latest WPI month this repo holds), and CARE notes realisations of Rs 170/kg in H1 FY26 with yields improving to 1,970 kg/ha from 1,560. But in the one quarter where both prices rose, tea's contribution collapsed. Whatever is happening in tea costs is undisclosed and is large enough to swamp the rubber gain.

**A caution on the published PE.** BSE's company header shows EPS Rs 14.70 and PE 11.84 for this scrip. Rs 14.70 x 1.84554 cr shares = Rs 27.13 cr, which is the trailing **pre-tax** profit - so the header PE is a pre-tax multiple, and the trailing post-tax multiple is higher. FY26 is the cleanest anchor: audited PAT Rs 24.50 cr (FY25 Rs 10.26 cr) against pre-tax Rs 29.15 cr (FY25 Rs 14.90 cr).

**Peers: there is no profitable listed comparable.** Every listed plantation name in the same business is loss-making (BSE headers read 05-Oct-2026):

| Peer | Mcap Rs cr | PE | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Jay Shree Tea | 240 | -12.9 | EPS -6.43, ROE -6.26% |
| McLeod Russel | 434 | -6.6 | EPS -6.27, ROE -31.14% |
| Andrew Yule | 1,228 | -16.2 | EPS -1.55, ROE -57.08% |
| Rubfila International | 348 | 13.2 | rubber-thread maker - a **buyer** of natural rubber, so a sufferer of this price, not a peer |
| **Harrisons Malayalam** | **321** | **13.1 (on PAT)** | the only profitable one |

So the re-rating case cannot be made on a peer multiple. It has to be made on earnings: at Rs 321 cr of market value, a rubber segment earning Rs 25.64 cr pre-tax in a flat-price year, with the public price for its main product 50% higher than a year ago and mature area starting to recover, is the entire argument. **The market is not paying for it yet - the stock is down 14.1% over one year while the Rubber Board print rose 50.5%.** That divergence is the observation; whether it closes depends on volume, which Q1 FY27 says is going the wrong way.

**Liquidity is a real constraint.** Median daily turnover over the 64 sessions from 03-Jul-2026: **Rs 20.8 lakh on NSE** (measured this run from NSE daily bhavcopies; median volume 10,404 shares) plus Rs 1.0 lakh on BSE. That is below the Rs 25 lakh floor this project's own triage rules use.

**Where it sits in the measured size band.** Rs 321 cr market cap is at the very bottom of the Rs 300-7,500 cr range where the 2026-09-22 study found the odds of a 5x run peak (median winner Rs 1,760 cr, nothing above Rs 25,000 cr ran 5x in three years).

ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **Which company:** *Parag Milk Foods Ltd*, NSE **PARAGMILK**, BSE **539889**, ISIN INE883N01014, face value ₹10. Both codes are confirmed on the company's own filings (every letter is headed "Scrip Code: 539889 / NSE Symbol: PARAGMILK"), and the same ISIN appears in the 5-Oct-2026 NSE and BSE bhavcopies. There are **12,56,09,554 shares** outstanding (Sixth Sense's SAST filing of 25-Sep-2026, and the sum of the Jun-26 shareholding pattern). There are also 90 lakh warrants at ₹179.10, which are due to convert by about Nov-2026.
- **What it makes:** a Pune-based private dairy whose products are mostly value-added. Brands: **Gowardhan** (ghee, paneer, dahi, pouch milk), **Go** (cheese, UHT milk, beverages), **Pride of Cows** (premium farm-to-home milk from its own ~5,000-cow farm, held in the subsidiary Bhagyalaxmi Dairy Farms) and **Avvatar** (whey protein, made from whey left over from its own cheese making). Plants are at **Manchar and Thorandale (Maharashtra)** and **Palamaner (Andhra Pradesh)**. Milk handling capacity is 34 lakh litres/day; ghee plus cheese 110 MT/day (cheese 60 MT/day); paneer 20 MT/day; whey processing 10 lakh litres/day (FY26 AR). The Sonipat (Haryana) plant was idle and has been sold (Q1 FY27 call).
- **Revenue mix:** 'Flagship' categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, dahi) were **61%** of Q1 FY27 revenue. The 'New Age' brands (Pride of Cows plus Avvatar) were **13%**, ingredients/SMP 15%, liquid milk 9% and others 2%. The FY26 AR gives the split as **B2C 70% / B2B 30%**; the Q1 FY27 deck says 65/35. Exports were **2.17%** of standalone revenue. More than ~75% of Avvatar's revenue comes from e-commerce, quick commerce and its own website (Q1 deck).
- **Numbers:** consolidated revenue was ₹3,817.5 cr in FY26 (+11.2%) and ₹944.6 cr in Q1 FY27 (+10.9%). **EBITDA excluding other income** (my arithmetic) was ₹256.8 cr in FY26 (6.73%) and ₹68.3 cr in Q1 FY27 (7.23%). The "EBITDA" the company reports **includes other income** (FY26 ₹310 cr = 256.8 + 53.5). PAT was ₹135.1 cr in FY26 and ₹22.1 cr in Q1 FY27 (−20%, as current tax started to apply). Trailing-12-month PAT is ₹129.5 cr.
- **What the market pays:** at **₹281.00** (NSE close, 5-Oct-2026) the market cap is **₹3,530 cr**. That is **27.3x trailing PAT** (29.7x if trailing pre-exceptional PBT is taxed at 25%), **15.2x EV/EBITDA** (EBITDA excluding other income), 1.04x EV/Sales and 2.80x Mar-26 book. This puts it in line with Heritage, cheaper than Dodla, and far cheaper than Hatsun and Milky Mist.
- **What a careful reader must weigh:**
  - **FY22 history:** the company wrote down **₹509.5 cr of inventory** and adjusted **₹118 cr of milk-aggregator advances** that year, booking a consolidated loss of ₹532.5 cr. That came after FY20-21 profits that had been earned while inventory was piling up. The Income Tax department searched the company in Nov-2021, and income-tax disputes have grown to **₹83.9 cr**.
  - **Cash conversion is weak:** from FY23 to FY26, operating cash flow was ₹270 cr against PAT of ₹398 cr.
  - **Government incentives are a large and shrinking part of profit:** ₹95.4 cr in FY25 and ₹45.8 cr in FY26, booked inside revenue. Another ₹220.6 cr is owed by government authorities and sits on the balance sheet.
  - **Pay:** the three promoter-directors' remuneration rose to ₹15 cr in FY26, plus ₹4.4 cr of commission.

### 1. Category and channel growth (company deck; ₹ cr)
| Segment | Q1 FY27 revenue | YoY | Share |

The FY26 New Age total from these quarters is 75+91+102+100 = **₹368 cr**; the AR says ₹366 cr, +91%. Management says these brands earn "almost double" the company's average margin, but it does not disclose segment margins. The 3–5 year aspiration is for them to reach 20–25% of revenue.

### 2. Milk cost cycle (company deck, average procurement price ₹/litre)
| Q1 FY25 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | Q1 FY26 | Q2 | Q3 | Q4 | Q1 FY27 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

### 3. Consolidated P&L, FY20 → FY26 (audited; ₹ cr; EBITDA excludes other income, my arithmetic)
| | FY20 | FY21 | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 2,437.9 | 1,841.8 | 2,071.8 | 2,892.6 | 3,138.7 | 3,432.2 | **3,817.5** |
| Growth | — | −24.5% | +12.5% | +39.6% | +8.5% | +9.4% | +11.2% |
| Gross margin* | 25.6% | 26.1% | −0.4% | 19.7% | 23.9% | 27.5% | 26.7% |
| EBITDA ex-OI | 211.1 | 124.8 | **−438.4** | 118.3 | 197.1 | 252.7 | 256.8 |
| EBITDA margin | 8.66% | 6.78% | n/m | 4.09% | 6.28% | 7.36% | 6.73% |
| Other income | 7.6 | 13.5 | 21.0 | 45.2 | 25.2 | 40.3 | 53.5 |
| Finance cost | 38.1 | 45.8 | 51.0 | 55.2 | 76.2 | 93.1 | 81.4 |
| PAT | 93.7 | 20.7 | **−532.5** | 53.3 | 90.6 | 118.8 | 135.1 |
| EPS (₹) | 11.16 | 2.47 | −56.91 | 5.07 | 7.71 | 9.97 | 11.06 |

*Gross margin = revenue − materials − purchases ± inventory change. FY26 results regrouped about ₹58 cr of FY25 cost from materials into other expenses: FY25 gross margin is **25.8%** as first published and 27.5% as regrouped. EBITDA is not affected. Ind-Ra's FY25 EBITDA of ₹252.6 cr (7.36%) matches my ex-OI figure.

**Incentives inside revenue (standalone note 26):** Package Scheme (PSI) ₹76.60 cr, PLI ₹11.61 cr and milk subsidy ₹7.20 cr in FY25 (total **₹95.41 cr**). In FY26 they were PSI ₹37.15 cr and PLI ₹8.63 cr (total **₹45.78 cr**). Taking them out, EBITDA is **₹157.3 cr (4.6%) in FY25** and **₹211.0 cr (5.5%) in FY26**. On that basis the underlying business improved more than the headline shows. Management expects incentives to fall a little further in FY27, because GST on ghee and cheese was cut from 12% to 5% in Sep-2025 and the state incentive is a refund of state GST.

### 4. Quarters (consolidated, ₹ cr)
| | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY27 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 851.5 | 1,008.0 | 1,012.7 | 945.3 | **944.6** |
| YoY | +12.3% | +15.7% | +14.5% | +3.0% | **+10.9%** |
| Gross margin | 27.4% | 25.8% | 25.9% | 28.0% | 27.3% |
| EBITDA ex-OI | 57.9 | 71.2 | 68.3 | 59.4 | **68.3** |
| Margin | 6.80% | 7.07% | 6.74% | 6.28% | **7.23%** |
| Other income | 7.6 | 18.0 | 8.9 | 18.9 | 1.4 |
| PBT (after exceptional) | 29.2 | 50.5 | 32.6 | 40.1 | 29.3 |
| PAT | 27.6 | 45.7 | 29.6 | 32.2 | **22.1** |

- In Q1 FY27, EBITDA excluding other income rose **18%** year on year (57.9 to 68.3). The company's headline figure of +6% includes other income, which fell from ₹7.6 cr to ₹1.4 cr.
- PAT fell because current tax restarted. The Q1 FY27 tax charge was ₹7.24 cr on PBT of ₹29.29 cr (24.7%), against an FY26 tax rate of 11%.
- Q3 FY26 carried a ₹5.72 cr exceptional charge for the new Labour Codes.
- The **subsidiary Bhagyalaxmi Dairy Farms** (the Pride of Cows farm) lost **₹15.83 cr after tax in FY26** on ₹197.5 cr of income (AOC-1). Standalone Q1 FY27 PAT (₹25.43 cr) was above consolidated (₹22.05 cr), so the subsidiary was still loss-making.

### 5. Physical model: FY27 and FY28 (my arithmetic; not company guidance)
- **FY27 revenue.** The COO guides to growth "more than 10%". At +11 to +13%, revenue would be ₹4,240–4,310 cr. The arithmetic: Q1 is ₹945 cr; New Age at Q1's ₹118 cr run-rate growing to about ₹130 cr a quarter gives about ₹500 cr; Flagship and the rest grow 8–10%. Physical capacity is not the limit in FY27: the cheese plant is "close to full utilisation" at 60 MT/day, but the 60 MT/day addition (₹105 cr) is due by Mar-2028, and the paneer addition (20 → 80 MT/day, ₹100 cr) by Jun-2027 / FY28.
- **FY27 margin.** EBITDA excluding other income at 7.0–7.5% gives **₹300–320 cr**. Deduct D&A of about ₹75 cr and interest of about ₹80 cr, and add about ₹20 cr of other income: PBT is about ₹165–185 cr. At 25% tax, PAT is **₹125–140 cr**. On 13.46 cr shares after the warrants convert, EPS is **₹9.3–10.4**, a **27–30x forward P/E** at ₹281. FY27 PAT may be lower than FY26 because current tax restarts.
- **FY28.** Revenue grows 12% to about ₹4,800 cr. EBITDA margin of 8% gives about ₹385 cr. PAT is about ₹190 cr, an EPS of about ₹14.1 and a **20x P/E**. This needs New Age to reach ~16–18% of sales and the paneer and cheese additions to be running.
- **The re-rating case in one sentence:** if margin excluding incentives moves toward double digits as New Age reaches 20% of sales, Parag would earn something like Dodla's PAT on a smaller market cap; the risk is that FY22-type inventory accounting and heavy incentive dependence come back.
- **Company guidance:** it does not give annual guidance. Its stated aims are a "₹10,000 cr" roadmap (no date; X and forum posts say FY29–30, unverified), "double-digit EBITDA margin" in coming years, 1.5 million retail outlets in 3 years (4.6 lakh today) and FY27 capex of ₹60–70 cr (Q4 call). That capex figure was given **before** the cheese (₹105 cr) and paneer (₹100 cr) projects were announced.

- **Seven years in total:** PAT −₹20.4 cr, operating cash flow ₹155.1 cr, capex ₹453.3 cr.
- **The gap was filled with equity:** ₹387.5 cr in FY22 (IFC, Sixth Sense and promoter warrants at ₹111), ₹200.3 cr in FY23 (AG Dynamic Funds 1.10 cr shares and Pivotal 10 lakh shares at ₹93.75, Akshali Shah 20 lakh warrants at ₹93.75), ₹40.3 cr of warrant money in FY26, and IFC's ₹77.4 cr FCCB converted at ₹135 (Sep-2025).
- **Net debt:** ₹522 cr on my arithmetic; the deck says ₹484 cr (its "internal metrics" are not reconciled).
- **Rating:** India Ratings upgraded the company to **IND BBB+/Stable / A2 (7-May-2026)** on ₹600 cr of bank lines and ₹81 cr of NCDs. ICRA's BBB- (Negative) was withdrawn in 2025 at the company's request. Ind-Ra lists "sustained improvement in corporate governance" as a positive trigger.

### 8. Red flags checklist (answered)
1. **Inventory and accounting history.** FY22: ₹5,095 m inventory write-down plus ₹1,180 m of milk-aggregator advances adjusted, both carried as an emphasis of matter by the auditor (FY22 AR). Inventory had built up from ₹462.9 cr (FY19) to ₹694.8 cr (FY21) while profits were reported. Current inventory is ₹730 cr (70 days). **Advances to suppliers/others are still ₹194.5 cr** (Mar-26), and how much of that is with milk aggregators is not disclosed.
2. **Tax.** The Income Tax department searched the company under s.132 in Nov-2021 (FY22–FY25 ARs). The AY2021-22 assessment order refers to the search and is under appeal. **Income-tax contingent liabilities rose from ₹54.2 cr to ₹83.9 cr** in FY26 (AY2016-17 to AY2022-23; the biggest is AY2019-20 at ₹26.7 cr). The FY26 AR no longer repeats the note about the search. Other disputes: GST ₹5.2 cr, MVAT ₹3.2 cr, and a new ₹20 cr corporate guarantee for vendor financing.
3. **Government money.** Incentives were 38% of FY25 EBITDA excluding other income and 18% of FY26's. Balances owed by government authorities are ₹179.6 cr non-current plus ₹41.0 cr current = **₹220.6 cr (18% of net worth)**. When this cash will be received is not disclosed.
4. **Related parties and promoter pay.** Remuneration was ₹5.00 cr each to Devendra, Pritam and Akshali Shah (₹15 cr, up from ₹5.66 cr), plus ₹1.47 cr commission each and rent of ₹1.28 cr to the two brothers. Total promoter-family pay is about ₹20 cr, **15% of FY26 PAT**. The subsidiary sold the parent ₹72.0 cr of goods and received ₹10 cr of new loans (₹30 cr outstanding) and ₹31.8 cr of advances. New promoter-linked entities: Awasari Infracon, SHAJ Livewell Nutrient LLP and Vitalia Tradeglob. Vitalia was reclassified out of the promoter group in Jul-2026 and holds nil shares.
5. **Auditor.** Sharp & Tannan, reappointed for 2025–30, gave an unmodified opinion. Key audit matters were receivables and revenue recognition. CARO: no defaults and no fraud reported. The previous auditor, Haribhakti, left in 2020 at the end of its term limit.
6. **Pledge.** Nil since Mar-2021. The Dec-2019 and Mar-2020 shareholding patterns flag shares pledged, with encumbrance disclosures in Feb–Apr 2020.
7. **Dilution and pricing.** The 2022 issue at ₹93.75 was below the promoters' own 2021 warrant price of ₹111. The 2025 warrants at ₹179.10 were above the ICDR floor of ₹178.62. Promoters hold 60 lakh of the 90 lakh warrants. The rest: Trishakti Power Holdings (Paresh Doshi) 14 lakh, Utpal Sheth 13 lakh, CSO Ankit Jain 2 lakh, Rajesh Kabra 0.44 lakh and Vishesh Dalal 0.56 lakh.
8. **Management.** There was no full-time CFO from Apr-2023 (the MD was interim CFO) until **Rakesh Kothari was appointed on 7-Aug-2026**. His self-introduction on the call ("two decades with Citibank") matches the deck's biography of **Ankit Jain**, while the deck gives Kothari a Marico and Arvind background. The two bios contradict each other.
9. **Insider selling.** **Sixth Sense India Opportunities III**, whose founder Nikhil Vora is a non-executive director, sold 29,54,115 shares between 19-Nov-2025 and 23-Sep-2026 and now holds 2.69% (it held 6.84% at Mar-2025).

ideas.verify:
- **Inventory:** physical inventory and its age at the depots and the Manchar cold stores, especially ghee, cheese and whey powder. This is the FY22 failure point, and only a stock count or audit sample can confirm it.
- **Milk aggregators:** who the aggregators are and how big the ₹194.5 cr supplier advances are. A forum member says about 60% of milk comes through agents; management says the landed price is the same as direct procurement.
- **Incentive cash:** whether Maharashtra PSI incentive money (₹220.6 cr shown as due from government authorities) is actually being received in cash. A state-level check or the annual-report cash-flow detail would show it.
- **New Age sell-through:** Avvatar and Pride of Cows on quick-commerce platforms after the July-2026 price rise. A channel check or subscription panel data would confirm it.
ideas.unknowns:
- **Not disclosed:** the B2C/B2B split by category; segment margins; utilisation of the ghee, whey and powder plants; the size of the Sonipat sale.
- **Balance sheet at Jun-26:** Q1 FY27 results have no balance sheet, so debt and inventory at Jun-26 are unknown.
- **Status of the 2021 income-tax search;** what the ₹20 cr vendor-finance guarantee covers.
- **Why** shareholding patterns for 10 quarters were revised on 11-Dec-2025.
- **Capex funding:** total FY27–FY28 capex, now about ₹205 cr of announced projects plus maintenance, and how it will be split between debt and the ₹120.9 cr of warrant money.
- **Industry inputs not measured here:** market prices of SMP and butter; import, FTA and US-deal risk for dairy (none was read in a primary filing for this note).
- **Peers:** the exact post-IPO share count and net debt of Milky Mist; Prabhat Dairy's delisting date.
- **India Ratings May-2026 rationale:** the PDF is scanned and only its cover letter was read.
ideas.confidence: medium: every P&L, balance-sheet and shareholding number traces to filings read in this run, but earnings quality is the open question (the FY22 ₹509 cr inventory write-down, incentives that were 18–38% of EBITDA, operating cash flow at 68% of PAT over FY23–26), and the Jun-26 balance sheet is not yet published

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying.** The dedicated thread has 341 posts (Jan-2016 to Aug-2026, ~107k views). It was enthusiastic in 2018–19, then from 2019 to 2022 turned distrustful over pledges, management churn, inventory, the Dec-2021 income-tax raid and the FY22 write-down (one Jul-2022 post: "all the worst fears about inventory manipulation were true"). Since mid-2025 the tone has been cautiously bullish: New Age mix, the pledge released, investors coming in through the warrants. The bears now focus on margins that are no better than Hatsun's, falling PSI income, Q4 FY26 volumes and the long-running interim CFO.
