ideas.name: Om Power Transmission Ltd
ideas.industry: Civil Construction (power transmission & distribution EPC: HV/EHV lines, substations, underground cabling, substation O&M)
ideas.trigger: filing: ORDER - Om Power Transmission filed two Reg 30 disclosures on 06-Oct-2026 (17:02 and 19:41 IST) reporting two Letters of Intent from Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation Ltd (GETCO): Rs 69.18 cr for the 220 kV D/C Prantij-Jantral Line Package 2 (24 months) and Rs 60.48 cr for the 220 kV Kotda-Sanghani AIS substation (18 months). Rs 129.66 cr including GST together - 28.9% of FY26 revenue of Rs 449.16 cr, and 22.8% of the Rs 567.47 cr order book the company reported at 30-Jun-2026.
ideas.thesis:
**What the business physically does.** Om Power Transmission is a Gujarat power-T&D contractor. It builds high-voltage and extra-high-voltage transmission lines (11 kV to 400 kV), air-insulated substations (up to 220 kV) and HV/EHV underground cable networks on a turnkey basis - supply, erection, testing, commissioning, civil works - and it operates and maintains substations for the utility. Its own FY26 presentation states the cumulative physical record: **1,000+ CKM of transmission line erected and 14 substations completed since incorporation** (14 years), and **107 substations under operation and maintenance** as of FY26. It holds an **AA Class certification from GETCO** for transmission-line and substation work, which is what admits it to GETCO's larger tenders.

**Revenue by segment (FY26 order mix, company presentation).** Transmission-line EPC 72%, substation EPC 23%, underground cabling and O&M the remainder. By counterparty, **82% of the FY26 order book was PSU** and 18% private; **the top 10 customers were 93% of FY26 revenue from operations**. GETCO is the dominant single counterparty, and both of today's LOIs are GETCO.

**Why today's filings matter more than the headline number.** The one metric that had been deteriorating was the order book, and the company said so itself. Read its own disclosures in sequence:

| Order book, unexecuted | Date | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Rs 745 cr | 31-Dec-2025 | FY26 earnings call, management answer |
| Rs 621.28 cr | 31-Mar-2026 | Q1 FY27 investor presentation |
| Rs 567.47 cr | 30-Jun-2026 | Q1 FY27 investor presentation |

Two consecutive quarters of decline. In Q1 FY27 the company executed **Rs 121.63 cr** of work but took in only **Rs 67.82 cr** of new orders - a book-to-bill of **0.56x** - and the Chairman's own commentary named the cause: *"Tender activity from GETCO has been somewhat lumpy/muted at the start of the financial year, and we expect it to pick up as the year progresses."* Today's two LOIs are Rs 129.66 cr in a single day, slightly more than a full quarter of execution, and they come from the exact counterparty whose tendering had gone quiet. That is the reason to look, not the rupee figure on its own.

**Where it sits in the measured record.** On the two tests this page's own order study found to work (runbook 144c, 1,245 order filings):

- **Size against a year of sales: favourable.** Rs 129.66 cr is **28.9%** of FY26 revenue of Rs 449.16 cr - inside the 25-50%-of-sales band, where 35.7% of filers reached 2x within two years against 21.4% for orders under 10% of sales. Against market cap it is 24.5%, which the same study found predicts nothing; the sales ratio is the one that mattered.
- **Rarity: unfavourable, and this is the main argument against.** Counting BSE's own announcement list (read complete this run, `announcements_status: complete`), Om Power has filed **eight order announcements** - 30-Apr, 25-Jun, 09-Jul, 10-Aug, 27-Aug, 17-Sep and two today - in the **5.7 months since it listed on 17-Apr-2026**. Eight or more prior filings is the bucket that reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and **never reached 5x**. The honest qualification: it listed in April 2026, so it had no filing obligation before that, and eight filings compressed into six months is not the same object as eight spread over two years. Either reading places it among frequent filers, which is what a utility-panel EPC contractor is.
ideas.model:
**Physical driver.** CKM of line and number of substations converted into revenue through the order book. Management states the execution clock on the earnings call: *"generally our timeline is 12 to 24 months, so averaging it, our timeline is 18 months."* Gross margin is held at **23-25%** and EBITDA at **12-13%**, and *"almost all our POs have price variation calculations"* - so conductor, transformer and insulator inflation is passed through rather than absorbed.

**The arithmetic, from the company's own figures:**

| Step | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Order book 30-Jun-2026 | Rs 567.47 cr | Q1 FY27 presentation |
| + today's two GETCO LOIs (incl GST) | Rs 129.66 cr | the two Reg 30 filings |
| = order book after today | **Rs 697.13 cr** | arithmetic |
| at the stated 18-month average execution | Rs 465 cr a year | arithmetic |
| Q1 FY27 revenue, actual | Rs 121.63 cr | BSE detailed results |
| Q1 annualised | Rs 486 cr (+8.3% on FY26) | arithmetic |

**Against that, management's guidance looks hard.** On the FY26 call the CFO was asked directly whether FY27 would grow "50% plus" and answered *"Yes."* Fifty per cent on FY26's Rs 449.16 cr is Rs 674 cr, which needs **Rs 552 cr over Q2-Q4, or Rs 184 cr a quarter - 51% above the Q1 run-rate of Rs 121.63 cr**. Today's orders do not fix that: they run 18 and 24 months from the LOA, so the bulk lands in FY28, not FY27. The arithmetic says the realistic FY27 outcome is nearer Rs 500-550 cr than Rs 674 cr, and the gap between those two is the single thing to watch at the Q2 results.

**Earnings at each revenue level**, using the FY26 PAT margin of 8.86% (FY26 PAT Rs 40.02 cr on revenue Rs 449.16 cr; Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 10.52 cr on Rs 121.63 cr = 8.65%, so the margin is holding):

| FY27 revenue | PAT at 8.86% | EPS (3.4245 cr shares) | PE at Rs 154.3 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Rs 486 cr (Q1 annualised) | Rs 43.1 cr | Rs 12.58 | 12.3x |
| Rs 550 cr | Rs 48.7 cr | Rs 14.23 | 10.8x |
| Rs 674 cr (management's 50%+) | Rs 59.7 cr | Rs 17.43 | 8.9x |
ideas.valuation:
**At the 06-Oct-2026 BSE close of Rs 154.3** (mcap Rs 528.4 cr; paid-up capital Rs 3,424.50 lakh = **3.4245 cr shares** of Rs 10, from the Q1 FY27 filing, which reconciles exactly to BSE's market cap):

| Multiple | Value | Basis |
|---|---:|---|
| PE trailing (FY26) | **13.2x** | FY26 PAT Rs 40.02 cr = Rs 11.69/share on the current count |
| PE on Q1 annualised | **12.6x** | Q1 FY27 PAT Rs 10.52 cr x 4 |
| EV / FY26 revenue | ~1.2x | mcap Rs 528.4 cr, debt/equity 0.35x pre-IPO |
| Order book / mcap | **1.32x** | Rs 697.13 cr after today |
| Order book / FY26 sales | **1.55x** | Rs 697.13 cr / Rs 449.16 cr |

The reported FY26 EPS of Rs 15.53 is on the pre-IPO weighted count and is not comparable to today's price; Rs 11.69 is the same profit on the post-IPO 3.4245 cr shares.

**Peers.** The site's industry bucket for this scrip is "Civil Construction", which is not a transmission-EPC comparable set, so the dossier's mechanical peer list (IL&FS Engineering PE 54.79, Mold-Tek Technologies 31.23, Markolines 14.13, MBL Infrastructure 39.39, W.S. Industries 165.52) says little. The one true listed comparable priced from BSE's own header this run is **Rajesh Power Services (BSE 544291): PE 9.62 on EPS Rs 76.38, market cap Rs 1,359.4 cr** - cheaper than Om Power on trailing earnings and 2.6x the size. The other names the market groups with it (Advait, Viviana Power, Quality Power) were not priced in this run: **unknown**.

**The re-rating case in one sentence.** If GETCO tendering has genuinely turned - today's two LOIs being the first evidence - then a 12-13x contractor with a 1.55x-of-sales order book, 44% ROCE and 38% ROE (FY26, company presentation) re-rates on order inflow rather than on earnings; if today was a lumpy catch-up rather than a trend, the Q1 book-to-bill of 0.56x is the truer picture and there is nothing to re-rate.

**Price context, which cuts against the trigger.** The stock closed at **Rs 154.3 against its 65-day window high of Rs 177.55 and window low of Rs 152.45** - it is at the bottom of the range, down 12.4% in a month and 10.7% in three. It is also **11.8% below its Rs 175 IPO price** of April 2026. Volume on the day was **0.7x** the 60-day median, i.e. the two LOIs landed after the close (17:02 and 19:41 IST) and the market has not traded on them. There is no volume breakout here, which this page's own study treats as a point in favour rather than against: 81% of 5x runs had a volume explosion and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere.

A single state utility's tendering calendar sets this company's growth rate - which is exactly what the muted Q1 demonstrated. | FY26 presentation |
| Order book direction | **Fell two quarters running**: Rs 745 cr (Dec-25) to Rs 621.28 cr (Mar-26) to Rs 567.47 cr (Jun-26). Q1 FY27 book-to-bill 0.56x. | earnings call; Q1 presentation |

Stated collection terms: 80% of each running-account bill within 30 days, 10% on erection of supplied material, 10% on project completion and final invoice. Management says GETCO pays on time; that is an assertion, not a measurement I could verify. | earnings call |

ideas.verify:
- **Whether the two LOIs convert to Letters of Award, and on what date.** Both filings are *Letters of Intent*, and both execution clocks (18 and 24 months) run *"from the date of LOA"*, not from the LOI. The LOA date is therefore the fact that decides which financial year the revenue lands in, and it is not in either filing. GETCO's own award notices or the company's next Reg 30 would settle it.
- **Whether GETCO's tendering has actually turned.** The thesis rests on two LOIs in one evening reversing two quarters of decline. GETCO's published tender pipeline, and the Q2 FY27 order-intake figure when the company reports it, are the test. Management has already flagged 765 kV and HVDC as the next step up and confirmed it holds **no 765 kV order today** - so any claim of a 765 kV win needs its own filing.
- **The retention and receivable ageing at 30-Sep-2026.** Rs 66 cr was in retention at March. Whether that grew while the order book shrank is the question a half-year balance sheet answers and a quarterly P&L does not.
ideas.unknowns:
- **FY27 revenue.** Management affirmed "50% plus" growth on the FY26 call in May, before a Q1 with 0.56x book-to-bill. It has not been restated since. Whether the guidance still stands is **unknown** until the Q2 results or the next call.
- **The counterparty mix inside the order book after today.** The company gives PSU/private at 82/18 for FY26 but has not published a post-Q1 split, and today's LOIs push it further toward GETCO. **Unknown.**
- **Margin on these two specific orders.** Management declined to generalise: *"It actually differs from project to project ... it exactly isn't anything fixed."* So the 12-13% EBITDA band is a company average applied to these orders, not a figure disclosed for them. **Unknown.**
- **Whether the Rs 60.48 cr substation LOI is the same 220 kV Jantral work already counted.** The Q1 presentation records a Q1 intake *"including an order win from GETCO for the 220 kV Jantral AIS substation"*. Today's two LOIs name the **220 kV Kotda-Sanghani AIS substation** and the **220 kV D/C Prantij-Jantral Line Package 2** - different assets by name, and the line package is a line not a substation, so on the documents these are new. But "Jantral" appears in both the Q1 intake and today's line award, and nothing in the filings rules out overlap of scope. **Unknown, and it matters: if one leg were a re-announcement, the Rs 129.66 cr falls out of the favourable 25-50%-of-sales band.**
- **Number of order filings before April 2026.** It was a private company with no disclosure obligation, so the two-year rarity count cannot be completed. **Unknown.**
ideas.confidence: medium: the trigger is two dated, signed, counterparty-named LOIs whose value is 28.9% of a trailing year's sales - the one order ratio this page's study found predictive - landing on the exact metric (order intake from GETCO) that the company's own last two disclosures showed deteriorating, at 12-13x earnings with a 1.55x-of-sales order book and no volume chase. Held to medium, not high, by three measured things: eight order filings in 5.7 months puts it in the bucket that never produced a 5x, 93% of revenue comes from ten customers with GETCO dominant, and management's 50%+ FY27 growth needs a 51% step up on the Q1 run-rate that today's 18-24-month orders cannot supply.

**What X is saying.** Thin and dated - there is no dedicated analyst following and nothing at all about today's two LOIs, which is expected since they were filed at 17:02 and 19:41 IST and search indexing lags a day or two. What exists is IPO-period commentary: @Akash17971 placed the company in a cohort of listed Gujarat power-T&D contractors and described its scope, and @renewablemirror covered the SEBI approval for the issue. One number from these posts did verify against a primary document, and it is a useful one.

### Posts found

| Date | Handle | What it says | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026 (IPO period) | @Akash17971 | Groups it with "Rajesh Power, Advait Energy, and Viviana Power" as T&D EPC; describes HV/EHV scope, 1,000+ CKM, 11 substations, and an order book of ~Rs 744.6 cr as of December 2025 | [link](https://x.com/Akash17971/status/2041825782163701786) |
| 2026 (pre-IPO) | @renewablemirror | SEBI approval for the IPO; "plans to issue 1 crore equity shares to fund capex, debt repayment, and working capital" | [link](https://x.com/renewablemirror/status/2032776279779684418) |

### New verified data from these posts

| Data point | Primary source that confirms it |
|---|---|
| Order book ~Rs 744.6 cr at December 2025 | **Confirmed.** The FY26 earnings call transcript records management's own answer: *"our order book was INR 745 crores at the end of December '25"*. This is what establishes that the book fell for two straight quarters to Rs 567.47 cr - the central fact in this note, and it entered it from a post and was then matched to the transcript. |
| IPO funded capex, debt repayment and working capital | **Confirmed and quantified** by the Q1 FY27 filing's IPO-objects table: machinery Rs 11.21 cr, debt prepayment Rs 25.00 cr, long-term working capital Rs 55.00 cr, general corporate Rs 28.11 cr. |
| Peer set is Rajesh Power / Advait / Viviana | **Partly confirmed.** Rajesh Power Services is a real listed comparable and was priced from BSE's own header this run (PE 9.62). Advait and Viviana were not priced. |

### Claims on X not verified

- "**1 crore equity shares**" (@renewablemirror). The Q1 FY27 filing states the completed IPO was **85,75,000 shares at Rs 175**, of which 75,75,000 fresh. The post describes the SEBI-approved plan, not the executed issue; treat the executed figure as the fact.
- "**11 substations ... since inception**" (@Akash17971). The company's own FY26 presentation says **14 substations completed since incorporation**. The post is either older or wrong; the presentation is the source of record.
- "**1000+ CKM transmission lines**" - matches the FY26 presentation exactly, but the post is the only place the order-mix percentages (69.7% transmission / 22.7% substation / 3.9% underground / 3.7% O&M) appear; the presentation gives FY26 order mix as 72% / 23% and does not publish that four-way split, so the post's version is **not verified**.

### Where X disagrees with the filings

- The substation count (11 on X vs 14 in the FY26 presentation) and the share count of the issue (1 cr on X vs 85.75 lakh executed). Both are resolved in favour of the company's documents above. No post contradicts a financial figure in the results.

updates.title: Third GETCO LOI in two days: Rs 78.84 cr 220 kV Chorania-Salejda line, 24 months
updates.body:
Reg 30 filing of 07-Oct-2026 (signed 19:06 IST): Letter of Intent from Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation Ltd for supply, erection, testing and commissioning of the 220 kV D/C Chorania-Salejda transmission line on a turnkey basis, contract price Rs 78,84,08,034.94 including GST, to be executed in 24 months from the LOA date; domestic, no promoter interest, not a related-party transaction.

| Measure | Value | Arithmetic |
|---|---:|---|
| This LOI vs FY26 revenue | **17.6%** | 78.84 / 449.16 |
| Three GETCO LOIs of 06-07 Oct | Rs 208.50 cr | 69.18 + 60.48 + 78.84 |
| Three LOIs vs FY26 revenue | **46.4%** | 208.50 / 449.16 |
| Three LOIs vs Q1 FY27 order intake (Rs 67.82 cr) | 3.1x | 208.50 / 67.82 |
| Order book, 30-Jun-2026 | Rs 567.47 cr | Q1 FY27 presentation |
| Order book after the three LOIs | **Rs 775.97 cr** | 567.47 + 208.50, before any Q2 execution |
| Order book / FY26 sales | 1.73x | 775.97 / 449.16 |

Against the card: the model was built on an order book of Rs 697.13 cr after the first two LOIs; this one lifts it to about Rs 776 cr, the third GETCO award in two days after two quarters of a falling book (Rs 745 cr Dec-25, Rs 621.28 cr Mar-26, Rs 567.47 cr Jun-26). Timing is unchanged: at 24 months from the LOA, most of this revenue lands in FY28, so it does not close the gap between the Q1 FY27 run-rate (Rs 121.63 cr a quarter) and the 50%-plus FY27 growth affirmed on the FY26 call. An LOI is not yet an LOA: value and schedule can move at contract signing.

ideas.name: Veegaland Developers Ltd
ideas.industry: Residential, Commercial Projects (Kerala residential apartment developer; part of the broader V-Guard promoter family)
ideas.trigger: filing: RESULT - Veegaland Developers filed its first results as a listed company on 06-Oct-2026 (results 15:11 IST, press release 15:38, investor presentation 19:52): Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 74.32 cr +79.1% YoY, PAT Rs 9.72 cr +202.6% YoY, EBITDA Rs 14.31 cr +134.7%, pre-sales Rs 129.85 cr +64.8%, on a limited review by Varma & Varma with an unmodified conclusion. Volume was 7.6x the 60-day median and the stock closed at its listed-life high.
ideas.thesis:
**What the business physically does.** Veegaland plans, builds and sells multi-storey residential apartments in Kerala - Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram, Kozhikode and Thrissur - under the brand *Veegaland Homes*, across mid-premium, premium, ultra-premium and luxe segments. It is a single-segment company: the Chief Operating Decision Maker reviews it as one business, real-estate development, all in India. The promoter is **Kochouseph Thomas Chittilappilly**, founder of V-Guard Industries and Wonderla Holidays; the presentation describes the company as part of the broader V-Guard group with a business legacy from 1977.

**The physical unit is square feet, and the portfolio is fully disclosed.**

| Portfolio | Projects | Units | Saleable area |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Completed | 10 | 692 | 11,05,009 sq ft |
| Ongoing | 12 | 994 | 18,57,460 sq ft |
| Upcoming (land acquired, approvals in progress) | 3 | 212 | 4,62,010 sq ft |

Plus **6.51 acres of land reserves** (70 cents acquired in Q1). The company puts the upcoming three projects' estimated gross development value at **Rs 450 cr** and the Q1 launch, *Veegaland Amora* at Maradu, Kochi (1,59,923 sq ft, 3 BHK), at **Rs 150 cr** of developable value.

**Why the quarter is a trigger and not just a number.** This is the first results filing in the company's listed life - it listed on 18-Sep-2026 - and every line moved together, which is the pattern this page's own earnings study found behind 5x runs (profit doubling in 73.9% of them, revenue +50% in 53.8%, versus 8.8% and 2.7% of the stocks that went nowhere):

| Rs cr | Q1 FY27 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY26 | YoY |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue from operations | 74.32 | 70.33 | 41.50 | **+79.1%** |
| Gross profit | 20.99 | 19.27 | 12.17 | +72.6% |
| EBITDA | 14.31 | 14.32 | 6.10 | **+134.7%** |
| EBITDA margin | 18.9% | 19.9% | 14.5% | +441 bps |
| Profit after tax | 9.72 | 9.19 | 3.21 | **+202.6%** |
| PAT margin | 12.9% | 12.8% | 7.7% | +521 bps |

And the forward indicators moved with them: **pre-sales Rs 129.85 cr (+64.8% YoY, +21.0% QoQ)**, pre-sales area 1,46,786 sq ft (+40.4%), **gross collections Rs 70.97 cr (+72.5%)**, and **average realisation of Rs 8,886/sq ft on agreements executed in the quarter**, against Rs 8,527 in Q4 FY26 and Rs 7,301 in Q1 FY26 - **+4.2% QoQ and +21.7% YoY computed from the slide's own bars**. (The slide's arrows read "down 5.5% QoQ" and "up 17.5% YoY", neither of which reconciles with the three figures printed beneath them; see the red-flag table.) Collections of Rs 70.97 cr against recognised revenue of Rs 74.32 cr mean the revenue is very nearly cash-backed, which matters in a percentage-of-completion business where it need not be.

**One caveat on the headline that has to be said with it.** The auditor's own Other Matter paragraph states that the **Q1 FY26 comparative was not subjected to an audit or review** - it is management-compiled - and that the Q4 FY26 column is a balancing figure between the audited full year and unpublished audited nine months. So the reviewed figure is the Rs 74.32 cr itself; the *+79.1%* is measured against an unreviewed base.
ideas.model:
**Physical revenue model.** Area sold x realisation per square foot, recognised over time on percentage of completion (actual project cost incurred, including land and finance costs, over total estimated project cost). The company publishes the order book that drives it:

| Step | Value | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| Contracted order value at 30-Jun-2026 (agreements executed) | Rs 910 cr | Q1 FY27 presentation |
| of which recognised to date | Rs 479 cr (53%) | presentation |
| **of which still to flow through the P&L** | **Rs 431 cr (47%)** | presentation |
| Area under development, 12 ongoing projects | 18,57,460 sq ft | presentation |
| Q1 FY27 realisation on agreements executed | Rs 8,886/sq ft | presentation |
| Ongoing-portfolio value at that realisation | 18.57 lakh x Rs 8,886 = **Rs 1,651 cr** | arithmetic |
| Upcoming 3 projects, company's own GDV estimate | Rs 450 cr | presentation |

**The arithmetic, two ways.** Recognised revenue was Rs 74.32 cr in Q1; annualised that is **Rs 297 cr against FY26's Rs 250.98 cr (+18.4%)**. But recognition is the lagging half of this business. The leading half is pre-sales: Rs 129.85 cr booked in Q1 annualises to **Rs 519 cr**, against Rs 297 cr being recognised - so the company is currently selling at roughly 1.7x the rate at which it is recognising revenue, and the Rs 431 cr of unrecognised order value is **1.72x FY26 revenue**. As construction on the 12 ongoing projects progresses, that gap converts. At the FY26 PAT margin of 10.47%, the Rs 431 cr already contracted carries **about Rs 45 cr of profit** - more than FY26's entire Rs 26.61 cr - though spread over the recognition period, not one year, and the period is not disclosed.

**Earnings on each path**, on the post-IPO count of 4.875 cr shares:

| Basis | Revenue | PAT | EPS | PE at Rs 148.95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FY26 actual | Rs 250.98 cr | Rs 26.61 cr | Rs 5.46 | 27.3x |
| Trailing twelve months | Rs 283.80 cr | Rs 33.12 cr | Rs 6.79 | **21.9x** |
| Q1 FY27 annualised (margin 12.9%) | Rs 297.28 cr | Rs 38.88 cr | Rs 7.98 | **18.7x** |

TTM is FY26 less Q1 FY26 plus Q1 FY27. **No management revenue or margin guidance exists** - there has been no earnings call and no annual report as a listed company - so the third row is an extrapolation of one quarter, not a forecast the company has endorsed.
ideas.valuation:
**At the 06-Oct-2026 BSE close of Rs 148.95.** Share count is firm from three independent documents that agree: the SAST 29(2) disclosure states total voting capital of **4,87,50,000 shares of Rs 10**; the Q1 results show paid-up capital of Rs 3,375 lakh (3.375 cr shares) at 30-Jun-2026 plus a post-quarter IPO of 1,50,00,000 shares; and 4.875 cr x Rs 148.95 = **Rs 726.1 cr**, exactly BSE's market cap.

| Multiple | Value | Basis |
|---|---:|---|
| PE, FY26 | 27.3x | FY26 PAT Rs 26.61 cr on the post-IPO count |
| PE, trailing twelve months | **21.9x** | Rs 33.12 cr |
| PE, Q1 FY27 annualised | **18.7x** | Rs 38.88 cr |
| Price / book, approximate | ~1.5x | Rs 266.90 cr net worth at 31-Mar-26 (capital Rs 33.75 cr + other equity Rs 233.15 cr) plus Rs 210 cr gross fresh issue plus Q1 PAT |
| Unrecognised order value / mcap | 0.59x | Rs 431 cr |
| Debt / equity | **0.26x**, from 0.32x | Q1 FY27 presentation; this is the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, i.e. **before** the IPO money arrived, so the post-IPO figure is lower |
| ROE / ROCE | 3.58% / 4.05%, **not annualised** | presentation; the company labels them as quarterly |

**The IPO and where the price sits.** 1,50,00,000 shares at **Rs 140**, listed NSE and BSE on 18-Sep-2026; paid-up capital rose by exactly that number of shares, so it was a fresh issue of **Rs 210 cr gross**. Today's Rs 148.95 is **+6.4% on the issue price** after 13 sessions, and it is the **high of the listed life so far** (12-day window: high Rs 148.95, low Rs 139.70) on **7.6x the 60-day median volume** and Rs 49.9 lakh of median daily turnover. The breakout is real but the history is 12 days long, so "window high" here means very little - this page's own study is explicit that a volume explosion is an alarm bell and not evidence, present in 81% of 5x runs and 78% of the stocks that went nowhere.

**Peers: unknown, and that is a genuine gap.** The site's industry index returned no Kerala or South-Indian residential developer for this scrip - the mechanical peer list it produced (Grover Jewells, Enkei Wheels PE 32.01, Axtel 23.17, Yogi 56.23, Patil Automation) is a market-cap neighbour list, not a comparable set, and none of them is a property developer. BSE's own header for 544923 returns no PE, EPS, PB or ROE, as expected 13 sessions after listing. So **no peer multiple was measured in this run**, and the 18.7-21.9x range above stands on its own rather than against a sector.

**The re-rating case in one sentence.** A developer selling at 1.7x the rate it recognises revenue, with Rs 431 cr of already-contracted revenue to run through the P&L, realisation up 21.7% a year on its own printed figures, falling leverage and a promoter buying in the open market, re-rates if the pre-sales rate holds through FY27; it does not if Q1's +64.8% was the launch of Amora pulling forward a year's bookings.

| Check | Finding | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Auditor remarks | **Unmodified limited-review conclusion** on Q1 FY27 from Varma & Varma, Chartered Accountants (FRN 004532S), dated 06-10-2026, UDIN 26203094FVTWRM1534: *"nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe ... it contains any material misstatement."* | limited review report attached to the results |
| **An internal contradiction in the filing** | Note 1 says the statutory auditors *"have carried out limited review of the results for the quarter ended 30 June 2026"*, and the review report is attached - but **note 5 of the same statement says the 30 June 2026 figures *"have not been subjected to review or audit by the Statutory Auditors"***. The two cannot both be true. The auditor's own Other Matter resolves it: what was *not* reviewed is the **corresponding quarter ended 30 June 2025**. So note 5 reads as a drafting error carrying the wrong year - but it is a drafting error in the first results statement the company ever filed, and the growth base is the figure it concerns. | results filing notes 1 and 5; auditor's Other Matter |
| The +79% comparative | **The Q1 FY26 base of Rs 41.50 cr is management-compiled and was not audited or reviewed** - the auditor says so explicitly. Q4 FY26's Rs 70.33 cr is a balancing figure between the audited year and unpublished audited nine months. | auditor's Other Matter; results note 6 |
| Promoter holding and recent buying | **Promoter bought in the open market immediately after listing**: Kochouseph Thomas Chittilappilly acquired 8,00,000 shares on 18-Sep-2026 (listing day) and 3,00,000 on 21-Sep-2026, 11,00,000 in all (2.26%), taking the promoter group from **63.69% to 65.95%** (acquirer 48.82%, K. Chittilappilly Trust 17.13%). | SAST Reg 29(2) disclosure, filed 23-Sep-2026 |
| Pledge / encumbrance | **Zero.** The SAST disclosure reports nil shares in the nature of pledge, lien, non-disposal undertaking or other encumbrance, and nil warrants or convertibles, both before and after the acquisition. | SAST Reg 29(2) disclosure |
| Dilution | The IPO fresh issue of 1.5 cr shares at Rs 140 took the count from 3.375 cr to 4.875 cr - **a 44.4% increase in shares**, which is why FY26's reported EPS of Rs 8.77 is not comparable to today's price and Rs 5.46 is. A pre-IPO rights issue at Rs 1,000/share (17,50,000 shares, Aug-2025) and a 4:1 bonus (2,70,00,000 shares, Sep-2025) preceded it. | results notes 3 and 4 |
| **Arithmetic in the company's own presentation does not tie** | The average-realisation slide prints Rs 7,301 (Q1 FY26), Rs 8,527 (Q4 FY26) and Rs 8,886 (Q1 FY27), which work out to **+4.2% QoQ and +21.7% YoY** - but the arrows on the same slide read **"down 5.5% QoQ" and "up 17.5% YoY"**, and the caption repeats "Realisation up 17.5% year on year". The QoQ arrow has the wrong sign against the slide's own bars. Not a financial misstatement - realisation is not in the reviewed P&L - but the second presentation-level error in the company's first reporting cycle, alongside note 5. Flagged, not resolved. | Q1 FY27 investor presentation |
| Revenue quality | Percentage-of-completion accounting means revenue can be recognised without cash. Here it broadly was not: **collections Rs 70.97 cr against revenue Rs 74.32 cr** in the quarter. | presentation |
| Related-party loans or purchases | **Not disclosed in a quarterly filing, and there is no annual report as a listed company yet.** With a promoter family that controls V-Guard Industries and Wonderla Holidays, this is the specific disclosure to read when the FY27 annual report appears. **Unknown.** |  |
| Promoter salary versus profit | **Unknown** - no annual report as a listed company. |  |
| Geographic concentration | **Entirely Kerala**, four cities, one reportable segment. Management itself raises Middle East demand as a driver - *"such strong sales performance has been achieved amidst ongoing uncertainties in the Middle East, which has been a strong source of demand"* - so NRI remittance conditions in the Gulf are a demand variable this company cannot hedge. | press release; results note 7 |
| Listed history | **13 trading sessions.** No earnings call, no transcript, no annual report, one reviewed quarter. The research standard this page applies - eight quarters of results, the annual report's MD&A and auditor remarks, concall history - **cannot be met for this name yet**, and that is the single biggest limitation of this note. | BSE filings, 240-day window: 12 filings in total |
ideas.verify:
- **Whether the Q1 pre-sales rate holds without a new launch.** Rs 129.85 cr of pre-sales includes the quarter's launch of Amora (1,59,923 sq ft, Rs 150 cr estimated developable value). Q2 FY27 pre-sales, with or without a launch, is the number that separates a growth rate from a launch effect. Only the company's Q2 disclosure answers it.
- **RERA registrations and construction progress on the 12 ongoing projects.** Percentage-of-completion revenue depends on cost incurred against total estimated cost, which is a management estimate. Kerala RERA's project filings carry independent completion and approval status for each of the 12, and the 3 upcoming projects are described as having *"approvals in progress"* - which approvals, and how far, is not in any filing read here.
- **Whether realisation of Rs 8,886/sq ft is holding on new bookings, and which realisation number the company stands behind.** The slide prints Rs 7,301 (Q1 FY26), Rs 8,527 (Q4 FY26) and Rs 8,886 (Q1 FY27) - arithmetic on those is +4.2% QoQ and +21.7% YoY - while the arrows on the same slide say down 5.5% QoQ and up 17.5% YoY. The company's clarification, and a dealer or channel check on current asking prices in Kochi and Maradu, would settle both the level and the trend.
ideas.unknowns:
- **FY27 revenue and margin.** No guidance of any kind exists - no earnings call has been held. The Rs 297 cr annualisation is arithmetic on one quarter. **Unknown.**
- **Over what period the Rs 431 cr of unrecognised order value converts.** The presentation says only *"over time as construction progresses"*. Without project-level completion schedules the annual split is **unknown**, and it is the main input to any forward EPS.
- **Peer multiples.** No comparable Kerala or South-Indian listed developer was priced in this run; BSE's header carries no PE for this scrip yet. **Unknown.**
- **Land cost and inventory on the balance sheet.** The quarterly filing carries no balance sheet detail; 6.51 acres of land reserves and the land component of project cost are **unknown** in value.
- **The split of the IPO between fresh issue and any offer for sale.** Note 3 states an IPO of 1,50,00,000 shares at Rs 140 without that split; the paid-up capital rising by exactly 1.5 cr shares implies it was all fresh, but the filing does not say so in terms. One X post said the plan was to raise Rs 250 cr, against Rs 210 cr at 1.5 cr x Rs 140 - **unreconciled.**
- **Why note 5 says the reviewed quarter was not reviewed.** Read above; the auditor's report resolves the substance, but the company has not corrected the note. **Unknown whether a corrigendum follows.**
ideas.confidence: medium: the trigger is a reviewed quarter in which revenue (+79.1%), EBITDA (+134.7%), PAT (+202.6%), pre-sales (+64.8%), collections (+72.5%) and realisation (+17.5%) all moved together, with Rs 431 cr of already-contracted revenue to recognise against FY26 sales of Rs 251 cr, leverage falling to 0.26x, zero encumbrance, and the promoter buying 11 lakh shares in the open market on the listing day and the Monday after. Held at medium and no higher by the thinness of the record: thirteen trading sessions, one reviewed quarter, no concall, no annual report as a listed company, no peer multiple measurable, an unreviewed +79% comparative base, a filing that contradicts itself on whether the quarter was reviewed, and a business that is wholly in one state with Gulf remittances named by management as a demand driver.

The rating rationale was not found on icra.in on 09-Oct-2026 (the filing says it will be on www.icra.in), so ICRA's stated drivers are unread.

ideas.name: Shining Tools Ltd
ideas.industry: Industrial Products — solid-carbide cutting tools (Tixna) + tool regrinding services
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME (544607, not NSE) Rajkot solid-carbide tool maker, IPO ₹114 (Nov-2025), crashed to ₹38.52 (Mar-2026) then +313% to ₹159.20; FY26 revenue ₹18.29 cr (+24%), PAT ₹3.89 cr reported +117% but only +33% vs the prospectus-restated FY25 and EBITDA ex-OI +6%; H2 FY26 PBT −17% YoY; CFO resigned Aug-2026; Yiwu 'machinery' export order; 55:45 subsidiary with promoter family
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** Shining Tools Ltd (brand "Tixna"), Pipaliya near Rajkot, Gujarat. It grinds solid-carbide cutting tools (end mills, drills, reamers, ball-nose, custom tools) and re-sharpens and re-coats customers' worn tools. FY26 revenue: products ₹15.47 cr (85%), re-sharpening job work ₹2.82 cr (15%). One plant, 31 permanent employees.
- **Where it is listed:** **BSE SME only.** Scrip 544607, symbol SHTL, ISIN INE0D8001018. The shareholding filing says "NSE Symbol: NOTLISTED", and the ISIN is not in NSE's 6-Oct-2026 bhavcopy.
- **IPO:** fixed-price, ₹114 a share, 15,00,000 new shares (₹17.10 cr), open 7–11 Nov 2025, listed 14-Nov-2025. The stock opened at ₹104 and hit lower circuits to **₹38.52 on 30-Mar-2026 (−66% vs issue)**. It then rose to ₹177.24 on 23-Sep-2026 and closed at **₹159.20 on 6-Oct-2026**. BSE asked for price-movement clarifications twice (9-Apr and 18-Sep-2026).
- **Headline growth is mostly accounting:** FY26 PAT is reported as ₹3.89 cr, "+117%". But the FY25 base used (₹1.80 cr audited) is the figure the IPO prospectus itself restated **up** to ₹2.93 cr by reversing ₹1.09 cr of excess depreciation. Against the restated base, PAT grew **+33%**. EBITDA before other income grew only **+6–7%** (₹6.29/6.23 cr → ₹6.68 cr) while revenue grew 24%. The margin fell from 42.7% to 36.5%.
- **Post-IPO half was weak:** H2 FY26 (Oct-25–Mar-26) revenue rose only +9.5% YoY. Pre-tax profit **fell 17%**, and fell 32% excluding other income. The EBITDA margin dropped to 29.8%. Reported H2 PAT rose only because tax was nil (a ₹58.38 lakh deferred-tax credit) and a ₹28.3 lakh forex gain on machine imports.
- **Cash:** FY26 operating cash flow was ₹1.03 cr, against PAT of ₹3.89 cr (26%). H1 FY26 OCF was negative. Receivables are at 135 days and inventory at 115 days of sales. Capex was ₹12.07 cr, funded by the IPO.
- **Governance churn:** five independent directors resigned in ten months (May-2025 to Feb-2026). The executive director-cum-CFO resigned on 4-Aug-2026; no new CFO had been filed by 6-Oct. A 55:45 subsidiary (Shinvi Tools) was formed on 10-Sep-2026 with the promoter family holding the other 45%. Shareholders approved a ₹10 cr related-party limit with only 64,800 votes (1.15% of shares).
- **Two order filings, one odd:** a ₹2.01 cr (incl. GST) brazed-carbide-anvil order from Chandan Process (12-May-2026). And a "first-ever export order" for "1,708 units of machinery" worth US$95,292 from **Yiwu Kaipan Import & Export Co.**, a trading house, for delivery in 15 days (24-Aug-2026). The company makes cutting tools, not machinery.

**Bull case, from the filings.** IPO capex (6 ANCA 5-axis grinders, ₹9.07 cr budgeted) more than doubles certified capacity, from 1.25 lakh to 2.75 lakh pieces a year. Utilisation was 90–92% before the expansion. At FY25 realisations, full capacity at 85% use is worth roughly ₹31 cr of revenue against ₹18.3 cr in FY26. Debt fell from ₹8.18 cr to ₹6.30 cr, and India is pushing to localise tooling.

**Bear case, from the filings.** Growth stalled in the half after listing. Margins are compressing while tungsten import prices have roughly tripled. Customer concentration is high (top-10 customers 57% of FY25 product sales), although the annual report claims "no client concentration". There is a record of Section 185 loans to promoter relatives (₹30 lakh compounding fee, May-2025) and a pending criminal complaint by IDFC First Bank against a promoter firm. Statutory dues have been paid late, and the accounts contain several internal contradictions. At ₹159.20 the stock trades at 23x reported and ~29x normalised FY26 EPS, and ~36x annualised H2.

**Implied realisation (derived):** FY25 product sales of ₹1,183.72 lakh ÷ 39,388 tools ≈ **₹3,005 per tool**. Job work of ₹289.16 lakh ÷ 72,800 ≈ **₹397 per regrind**. FY26 product sales rose 30.7% to ₹1,547.17 lakh while job work fell 2.4% to ₹282.32 lakh. The FY26 split between volume and price is **not disclosed**.

**Full-capacity arithmetic (illustrative, not guidance):** 99,000 × 85% × ₹3,005 = ₹25.3 cr of tools, plus 1,76,000 × 85% × ₹397 = ₹5.9 cr of service, giving **≈ ₹31.2 cr**. That is +71% on FY26 revenue of ₹18.29 cr. Management gives **no revenue guidance** in any filing read. When the machines started running is unknown: P&M additions were ₹808.38 lakh in FY26, the forex outflow note mentions "two machines purchased", and a capital-goods advance of ₹393.00 lakh was outstanding at 31-Mar-2026.

**FY27 scenarios.** Depreciation is taken at ₹1.95 cr (H2 FY26 × 2), finance cost at ₹0.84 cr, tax at 25.17%, and 56,58,400 shares.

ideas.thesis:
**What the business physically does.** A Jaipur-based EPC contractor for power transmission and distribution: it surveys, designs, supplies, erects, tests and commissions substations, HT/LT distribution lines, distribution transformers, underground cabling, GIS mapping and asset tagging, on a turnkey basis, for state electricity distribution companies. It is **asset-light by design** - project equipment is leased rather than owned, and the RHP puts fixed-asset turnover at 70.72x in FY26 (153.67x FY25, 78.90x FY24). The physical unit that drives revenue is a work order executed against a DISCOM tender, so the revenue driver is the order book and the speed at which the government hands over sites.

The customer list is a list of state utilities: West Bengal (WBSEDCL), Madhya Gujarat Vij, Assam Power Distribution, Goa Electricity Department, Himachal Pradesh SEB, Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam, Jaipur Vidyut Vitran Nigam, Uttarakhand Power Corporation, Ajmer Vidyut Vitran Nigam and Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam. The RHP states **96.87% of FY26 revenue came from government-utility projects and 100% of the order book as at 31-Jul-2026** was government-awarded.

| Fiscal | Govt-utility revenue (Rs cr) | As % of revenue from operations |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2024 | 188.28 | 89.84% |
| 2025 | 339.04 | 96.66% |
| 2026 | 487.82 | 96.87% |

**The three-year record (RHP, restated, certified by the statutory auditor 24-Aug-2026).**

| Rs cr unless stated | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total income | 211.33 | 352.60 | 505.57 |
| Revenue from operations | 209.58 | 350.76 | 503.57 |
| EBITDA | 23.71 | 43.89 | 70.85 |
| EBITDA margin | 11.31% | 12.51% | 14.07% |
| Net profit | 13.98 | 27.45 | 41.43 |
| Net profit margin | 6.67% | 7.82% | 8.23% |
| RoNW | 32.84% | 43.36% | 35.44% |
| ROCE | 25.15% | 23.14% | 25.76% |
| Debt / equity (x) | 0.88 | 1.44 | 0.73 |
| Order book (year end) | 391.39 | 650.23 | 687.44 |
| Order book / revenue (x) | 2.08 | 1.92 | 1.41 |
| Basic EPS (pre-IPO shares, Rs) | 5.65 | 11.09 | 15.70 |
| NAV per share (Rs) | 20.03 | 31.12 | 57.69 |

**The order itself, from the filing.** The Reg 30 annexure names MSEDCL as the awarding entity, the scope as distribution infrastructure and system strengthening in the Bhandup region of Maharashtra (new substations, HT/LT lines, distribution transformers, augmentation, underground cabling, GIS mapping, asset tagging), the size as **Rs 615.76 cr including taxes**, the execution period as **24 months from the date of the LOA**, and answers "No" to both the promoter-interest and related-party questions. The accompanying press release adds that the project is **ADB-funded**, that it is the largest single order in the company's history, that it marks entry into Maharashtra as the 10th state, and that it lifts the unexecuted order book to **about Rs 1,400 cr** from Rs 687 cr in March.

**Where this order sits against the only two things the order study found predictive (runbook 144c, 1,245 order filings).**

- *Size against a trailing year of sales, which works.* Rs 615.76 cr gross is **1.22x FY26 revenue from operations of Rs 503.57 cr**. The filing states the figure is inclusive of taxes and gives no break-up; at an assumed 18% GST the revenue component is about Rs 521.8 cr, still **1.04x a year of sales**. Either way the order is larger than every bucket the study measured (orders at 25-50% of sales reached 2x within two years 35.7% of the time, against 21.4% for orders under 10%), so the study does not price an order of this size - it only says that this is the ratio that matters.
- *Size against market cap, which does not work.* Rs 615.76 cr is 0.86x the Rs 716.9 cr market cap. The study found the 25-50%-of-market-cap bucket produced no 3x at all, so this ratio is reported here only to be set aside.
- *Rarity, which works - and here it misleads.* This is the company's **first order announcement as a listed company**, and the study pays first-in-two-years filers best (2x 30.4% of the time, 5x 3.5%) while a serial bidder with eight or more prior filings reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and 5x never. **That signal is an artifact of a six-trading-day listing history, not real rarity.** The RHP's own top-five order table shows it winning large tenders repeatedly while unlisted: AVVNL Sikar RDSS Rs 225.34 cr (18-Oct-2025), RSDCL Pugal solar-park evacuation Rs 158.12 cr (31-Jul-2025), HPSEBL Solan/Nahan smart grid Rs 95.42 cr (19-Feb-2025), WBSEDCL Siliguri underground cabling Rs 81.27 cr (11-Oct-2023) and PGVCL Bhachau Rs 79.01 cr (08-Jul-2026). In substance this is a regular DISCOM bidder, which is the low-hit-rate side of the study. **Read the rarity as neutral, not as the 30.4% bucket.**

**One measured thing in the stock's favour on the two band rules.** Market cap Rs 716.9 cr sits inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where the 5x runs happened, and today's move came on **0.2x the median volume** - no volume explosion, which the study calls an alarm bell rather than evidence (81% of 5x runs had one and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere). ideas.model:
**The order book series, measured rather than quoted.**

| As at | Unexecuted order book (Rs cr) | Source |
|---|---:|---|
| 31-Mar-2024 | 391.39 | RHP KPI table, auditor-certified |
| 31-Mar-2025 | 650.23 | RHP KPI table, auditor-certified |
| 31-Mar-2026 | 687.44 | RHP KPI table, auditor-certified |
| 31-Jul-2026 | ~916.7 | derived: RHP top-5 projects Rs 639.16 cr = 69.72% of total |
| 07-Oct-2026 | ~1,400 | press release (not auditor-certified) |

The Rs 687.44 cr at FY26 end is exactly the "Rs 687 crores in March" the press release quotes, so the two documents agree on the base. The jump to ~Rs 1,400 cr is the Rs 615.76 cr MSEDCL award plus the FY27 wins already in the 31-Jul book, less about four months' execution - Rs 916.7 cr + Rs 615.76 cr = Rs 1,532.5 cr against the stated ~Rs 1,400 cr implies roughly Rs 130 cr executed in August-September, consistent with a Rs 500-700 cr annual run-rate.

**The revenue model: management's own board-approved projection, recovered by arithmetic.** The company has filed no results yet (listed 30-Sep-2026, first results due mid-November), so there is no guidance statement to quote. But the RHP's working-capital section carries a **FY27 projection approved by board resolution dated 24-Aug-2026 and certified by an independent chartered accountant**, built from holding periods expressed in days of revenue. Inverting those gives management's own FY27 revenue assumption:

| Projected FY27 item | Rs cr | Stated holding basis | Implied revenue (Rs cr) |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Trade receivables | 147.53 | 75 days of revenue from operations | 717.9 |
| Other current assets | 43.09 | 22 days of revenue from operations | 715.0 |
| Retention money | 230.14 | 120 days of EPC revenue | 700.0 |
| Margin money | 57.53 | 30 days of EPC revenue | 700.0 |
| Unbilled revenue | 57.53 | 30 days of EPC revenue | 700.0 |

Five independent line items converge on **EPC revenue of about Rs 700 cr and revenue from operations of about Rs 715-718 cr for FY27** - call it Rs 718 cr, **+42.6% on FY26's Rs 503.57 cr**. This is not my forecast; it is the number the board's own resolution is arithmetically built on.

**Cross-check against the order book.** Rs 1,400 cr against Rs 718 cr of FY27E revenue is 1.95x - the book alone covers about two years at the projected run-rate before any new win. The FY26 conversion of the opening book was 503.57 / 650.23 = 77.4%, and FY25's was 350.76 / 391.39 = 89.6%; applying 77-90% to the Rs 687.44 cr opening book gives Rs 532-616 cr from the opening book alone, so **the Rs 718 cr projection needs roughly Rs 100-185 cr from orders won during FY27** - which the Rs 79 cr PGVCL award and a partial quarter of MSEDCL could supply. The arithmetic hangs together; it is not loose.

**What MSEDCL itself contributes, and when.** LOA dated 07-Oct-2026, 24-month execution. The RHP says the average time from award to project start over the last three fiscals was 2-3 months, so execution starts around January 2027. At an assumed 18% GST the Rs 615.76 cr is about Rs 521.8 cr of revenue; spread evenly over 24 months that is **Rs 261 cr a year**, or about Rs 65 cr in Q4 FY27 and Rs 261 cr in FY28. Two explicit assumptions sit in that sentence: the 18% rate (the filing gives no tax break-up) and linear recognition (EPC revenue is usually lumpier, weighted to supply milestones). **FY28 is where this order mostly lands, not FY27.**

**Earnings.** Net margin has risen 6.67% -> 7.82% -> 8.23% over three years while EBITDA margin rose 11.31% -> 12.51% -> 14.07%. The Rs 129 cr fresh issue took debt/equity from 0.73x, and management's FY27 plan holds current borrowing flat at Rs 112.00 cr against Rs 112.09 cr in FY26 - so interest should fall as a share of revenue even if not in absolute rupees.

| FY27E net margin | PAT (Rs cr) | EPS (Rs) | PE at Rs 210.10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8.00% (below FY26) | 57.4 | 16.83 | 12.5x |
| 8.23% (FY26 actual) | 59.1 | 17.31 | 12.1x |
| 8.75% (interest leverage) | 62.8 | 18.41 | 11.4x |

EPS is computed on the **34,120,187 shares outstanding at 30-Sep-2026** from the BSE shareholding pattern, which at Rs 210.10 reconciles exactly to the Rs 716.9 cr market cap in BSE's scrip master. Note that the RHP's FY26 basic EPS of Rs 15.70 is on the pre-IPO share count; **on the post-issue count FY26 PAT of Rs 41.43 cr is EPS of Rs 12.14, so the trailing PE at Rs 210.10 is 17.3x, not 13.4x.**

ideas.red_flags:
Each item answered from the RHP dated 17-Sep-2026 or the shareholding pattern as at 30-Sep-2026.

1. **Contingent liabilities, and they are large.** Rs 272.68 cr at 31-Mar-2026, essentially all performance bank guarantees, which the RHP itself describes as "almost 7 times of the PAT and almost 164 times of the cash and cash equivalents". The series is Rs 99.42 cr -> Rs 122.76 cr -> Rs 272.68 cr. For a turnkey DISCOM contractor this is normal in kind, but the growth rate compounds the working-capital problem because each guarantee needs margin money.
2. **Working capital eats the cash flow.** Covered with the arithmetic above: 2.54x EBITDA absorbed in FY25, 99.7% in FY26, another Rs 160 cr planned for FY27. This is the single biggest reason the idea is not high-confidence.
3. **Customer concentration is total, by class.** 96.87% of FY26 revenue and 100% of the 31-Jul-2026 order book from state DISCOMs; the top two projects are 41.83% of the order book and the top five are 69.72%. A budget pause or a pre-qualification change at one or two utilities is a revenue event.
4. **Litigation against a customer, over money already received.** Civil Writ Petition 8325/2021 in the Rajasthan High Court (Jaipur) against the State of Rajasthan, AVVNL and REC: after a CAG audit objection, AVVNL was directed to recover price-variation amounts paid on copper-wound transformers, and issued a show-cause notice. Contingent liability about Rs 1.88 cr, pending, next hearing not notified. Separately a claim of Rs 3.60 cr by JVVNL. Small in rupees; notable because it is a clawback of revenue already booked and collected.
5. **GST.** Two West Bengal appeals pending, Rs 31.84 lakh (FY24) and Rs 15.87 lakh (FY23), plus a Rs 0.59 lakh TDS demand inherited from the predecessor partnership firm. A larger Rs 10.62 cr GST penalty shown in FY24 **was set aside on appeal** by an order dated 31-May-2024, so it is closed.
6. **Promoters run a company in a similar line.** Risk factor 52 discloses promoter involvement in Galaxy Concab India LLP, which deals in overlapping items (wires, cables, circuit breakers); Galaxy Concab appears in the promoter-group list in the shareholding pattern with nil shares. The only protection disclosed is a memorandum of undertaking dated 02-Feb-2025 under which Galaxy Concab will not directly compete or solicit customers for five years. An MoU between related parties is a weak instrument.
7. **Related-party transactions**, Rs 19.92 cr in FY26 - salary, interest, rent, purchases, sales, freight and consumables - 3.96% of revenue, improving from 7.96% in FY24 and 5.14% in FY25. Direction is right.
8. **Promoter pay against profit.** Vinay Gupta (MD) Rs 1.99 cr and Ruchira Gupta (WTD) Rs 1.75 cr in FY26, Rs 3.73 cr together, **9.0% of FY26 PAT**. One director's basic salary was raised from Rs 4.60 lakh to Rs 14.00 lakh with effect from 01-Apr-2025 - a 3x step-up in the year before the IPO.
9. **Execution has slipped before.** The RHP states past delays "ranged between 6 to 12 months" on account of site handover, non-clearance of drawings and delayed payments by government clients, with 2-3 months typically between award and start. The 24-month MSEDCL period should be read against that record.
10. **Preferential issue below market.** The pre-IPO placement at Rs 165 (28-Jul-2025) is below the Rs 210.10 close, as is normal for a pre-IPO round; the weighted average cost of acquisition for the selling promoters was Rs 4.30 to Rs 14.80 a share.
11. **Auditor remarks - partly unread.** The statutory auditor is M/s A Bafna & Co, which certified the KPIs and restated figures on 24-Aug-2026. Risk factor 54 refers to "the said emphasis of matter" in the audit report on the restated financials, but **the text of that emphasis of matter was not located in the pages read this run, so its subject is unknown.** It is listed again under "Unknowns" and under "Still to verify".
12. **No volume chase and no orders claimed without a counterparty** - the two things this page treats as warning signs are absent. Today's volume was 0.2x median and the order names MSEDCL, a zone, a scope and a tender process.
ideas.verify:
1. **That the LOA becomes a signed contract with a site handover.** An LOA is not a contract, and the RHP's own record is 2-3 months from award to start with past slippage of 6-12 months. Confirmation would come from the company's Q2 FY27 results commentary or a subsequent Reg 30 filing; a tender-portal check of MSEDCL's Bhandup Zone award would be stronger. Not doable from documents alone.
2. **The ADB funding claim.** The press release says the project is ADB-funded and that the company focuses on multilateral-funded work; the Reg 30 annexure does not mention ADB at all. ADB's project database or MSEDCL's tender document would settle it. **adb.org was not reachable from this run's sandbox, so this is unverified.** It matters because multilateral funding is the company's stated reason to expect faster payment than a plain DISCOM contract.
3. **Q2 FY27 results, due by mid-November 2026** - the first results the company will ever file. The Rs 718 cr FY27 trajectory implies roughly Rs 180 cr a quarter against FY26's Rs 126 cr average; the half-year number will show whether the board's projection is live.
4. **The emphasis of matter** in the FY26 restated audit report - its subject, and whether it recurs in the first audited annual report as a listed company.
5. **The tax break-up of the Rs 615.76 cr.** The filing states "including taxes" without a rate. An 18% assumption moves the revenue component by about Rs 94 cr; the contract or the first revenue recognition under it would pin it.
6. **Whether the ~Rs 1,400 cr order book is on the RHP's definition.** The RHP's Rs 687.44 cr is auditor-certified as "work order in hand at end of period"; the press release's Rs 1,400 cr is not certified and the basis is not stated. A reconciliation in the Q2 FY27 presentation would confirm it.
